text:
Today, Congresswomen Suzan DelBene (WA-01) and Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) reintroduced the Strengthening Welfare in Marine Settings (SWIMS) Act, legislation that would end the future capture and breeding of whales for public display.
Certain cetaceans, such as orcas, beluga whales, pilot whales, and false killer whales, are cognitively, emotionally, and socially complex animals who cannot thrive in captivity, according to multiple studies. Whales held for display often exhibit signs of suffering and distress and have significantly shorter lifespans than whales in the wild. Currently, there are approximately 70 whales held in captivity in the United States.
The SWIMS Act would:
    - Prohibit the taking, importation, or exportation of these whales for public display.
- Prohibit any breeding of these whales for future public display.
- Allow exemptions for animals being transported to a sanctuary setting or released to the wild.
“Whales and dolphins are treasures to the Pacific Northwest, and they belong in the wild,” said DelBene. “Scientific evidence shows that when these majestic animals are kept in captivity, they suffer significant distress and shorter life spans. This legislation would prevent the capture and breeding of whales for public display to ensure they remain in their natural habitats and free from abuse and exploitation.”
“Whales belong in the open ocean, not behind glass,” said Dexter. “These extraordinary animals are icons of the Pacific Northwest, forming deep family bonds and playing a vital role in healthy oceans. Captivity robs them of the space, freedom, and connection they need to thrive. Their lives should be defined by the ocean’s possibilities, not the walls of a tank.” 
“Science increasingly supports the conclusion that we cannot provide conditions in a concrete enclosure that accommodate the size, wide-ranging nature, and physiological, behavioral, and social needs of these species,” said Dr. Naomi Rose, senior scientist for marine mammal biology at the Animal Welfare Institute. “The SWIMS Act recognizes that reality and offers a path forward by prohibiting breeding, trade, and capture for public display. Let this be the last generation in captivity of these ocean predators.”
The SWIMS Act is supported by the Animal Legal Defense Fund, Animal Welfare Institute, Born Free USA, Cetacean Society International, CompassionWorks International, Humane World Action Fund, Humane World for Animals, International Marine Mammal Project of Earth Island Institute, Last Chance for Animals, Oceanic Preservation Society, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine, Whale and Dolphin Conservation, Whale Sanctuary Project, and World Animal Protection.
The bill text can be found 
here
.
title: DelBene, Dexter Introduce Legislation to Stop Future Capture, Breeding of Whales for Public Display

Reps. Tlaib and Green lead letter demanding release of DACA recipient in ICE custody
WASHINGTON – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Al Green (TX-09), joined by 21 Members of Congress, demanded the release of Ya’akub Ira Vijandre, who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a year ago as of yesterday. In a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Acting Director David Venturella, the Members pressed for answers regarding Ya’akub’s unconstitutional arrest and prolonged detention after a federal judge allowed his habeas challenge to proceed.
Ya’akub, a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipient, has lived in the U.S. since he was 14 years old. He spent a decade working for American Airlines as a senior safety specialist and was recognized for supporting grieving families after a helicopter crashed into a plane in Washington, D.C. Despite having no criminal record and not being charged with any crime, he was targeted and arrested at gun point for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza and for “liking” a social media post with Quranic verses–both of which are protected by the First Amendment.
“The administration’s stated basis for [Ya’akub’s] detention has been inconsistent and appears to rely substantially on his speech and social media activity,” the Members wrote. “DHS has sought to justify his detention by citing his social media commentary regarding the prosecutions of the Holy Land Foundation Five, his criticism of the treatment of Guantanamo detainees, his advocacy for Palestine, and his engagement with religious Islamic content, including ‘liking’ Instagram posts containing Quranic verses. We are deeply concerned that constitutionally protected political and religious expression is being used as a basis for his continued detention or deportation.”
The letter renews concerns and questions from a letter Rep. Green sent in June. Rep. Tlaib also spoke on the House floor urging for Ya’akub’s release in August.
“We are also concerned by reports, previously flagged in Congressman Green’s June letter, that the FBI approached Mr. Vijandre in November 2023 seeking his cooperation as a confidential informant and that he declined,” the Members continued in their letter. “His DACA status, renewed as recently as May 2024 through May 2026, was subsequently revoked. The proximity and sequence of these events—an FBI approach he declined, followed by a DACA termination and detention grounded largely in the government’s characterization of his religious and political speech—continue to raise serious questions about possible retaliation that Congress has not yet received satisfactory answers to.”
The letter, led by Reps. Tlaib and Green, was signed by 21 other Members of Congress: Greg Casar (TX–35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).
The letter was also endorsed by 38 organizations: American Friends Service Committee, Americans for Justice in Palestine Action, Arab American Caucus of the California Democratic Party, Arlington for Palestine, Asian Americans Advancing Justice – Atlanta, CAIR Action, Center for Constitutional Rights, Codepink, Community Alliance for Peace and Justice, Demand Progress, Havertown-Community Action Network, IMEU Policy Project, Indiana Center for Middle East Peace, Institute for Policy Studies New Internationalism Project, Maine Coalition for Palestine, Majdal: Arab Community Center of San Diego, MARUF CT, Massachusetts Peace Action, Methodist Federation for Social Action, Muslim Advocates, National Political Prisoner Coalition, NE Oakland Indivisible, NH Peace Action, Palestine Legal, Peace Action Montgomery, Peace Justice Sustainability NOW!, Philly Neighborhood Networks, Pittsburgh Palestine Solidarity Committee, Project TAHA, Restore The Fourth – Action, ReThinking Foreign Policy, River Valley for Palestine, The Justice Coalition, United Methodists for Kairos Response, US Campaign for Palestinian Rights Action, Virginia for Palestine, Whistleblower & Source Protection Program at ExposeFacts, Worcester Multifaith for Palestine.

Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H.Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day."
"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Congressman Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."
"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Congressman Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."
"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," Congressman Tonko said. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."
"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Congressman Valadao.
"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.
"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of FCHEA. "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large."
BACKGROUND
National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.
The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power.
U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Representatives Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors.
Senator Richard Blumenthal (CT) led the introduction of the Senate Resolution, with Senators Bill Cassidy (LA), Chris Coons (DE), and Chris Murphy (CT) joining as original cosponsors.
title: Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day

Republican Health Care Cuts Are Decimating American Families
July and August Tally of Layoffs, Closures, and Harms to the American Health Care System Reveals Looming Crisis Following Republicans’ Cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act
Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and House Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr., D-N.J., today released their latest report spotlighting the consequences of Donald Trump and Republicans’ health care cuts, with a focus on the fallout of the Republican Big Ugly Bill.
“It has been over a year since Trump's Big Ugly Bill hit the Americans health care system like a wrecking ball, leaving states and communities across the country in financial crisis," Wyden said. “The Trump administration and their Republican allies continue to deflect the devastating consequences of their catastrophic cuts, while millions of Americans around the country grapple with higher costs, worse coverage, and more red tape.”
“In the year since President Trump signed his Big Ugly Bill, millions of Americans have lost their insurance coverage, premiums and deductibles are higher than ever, hospitals are shutting down, and essential workers are being laid off on a monthly basis,” Pallone said. “It’s time to stop this madness and reverse the Republican health care cuts.”
Numbers from July and August demonstrate a continuing attack on Americans’ health care.
- The Trump Administration improperly kicked three-quarters of a million Americans off of their coverage: 760,000 low- and middle-income American families were kicked off their Affordable Care Act (ACA) coverage as the Trump Administration colludes with insurance companies to terminate coverage without cause for individuals and families simply because they had not seen a doctor this year.
- In just July and August, dozens of hospitals and clinics closed, and others are struggling to remain in operation: 31 hospital closures, clinic closures, and service reductions across 13 states and Washington, D.C.: California, Iowa, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Tennessee, Virginia, and Wyoming.
- Essential health care workers are losing their jobs at alarming rates: Nearly 400 employees have been laid off across five states and Washington, D.C.: California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Montana, and Tennessee.
- These catastrophic numbers reflect the cost of gutting over $1 trillion from Medicaid and the ACA. Trump's legislation has wreaked havoc on the American health care system. Since the bill passed, health insurance premiums have soared, 339 clinics and hospitals have closed across 45 states, and over 11,000 health care employees from 31 states and D.C. have lost their jobs.
Last month, Wyden and Pallone released a report on the impact of Republican health care cuts for June 2026.

Congressman Deluzio Announces $200,000 for Mental Health Services in Beaver County
CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) announced that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has awarded Beaver County, Pennsylvania $200,000 to invest in mental health and substance abuse services across the county. The federal funding will help the county execute its REACH (Respond Educate Assist Connect and Help) Program.
“I’m proud to announce that Beaver County is receiving $200,000 in federal funding to boost their mental health and substance abuse services,” said Congressman Deluzio. “These are challenges that impact so many Western Pennsylvanians and their families. It’s critical to have the care folks need close to where they live—I'm glad to celebrate this funding coming home for more resources in Beaver County.”
“Beaver County Behavioral Health is thankful for this Federal award from SAMHSA and is excited about the positive impact it will have on our County,” said Lisa McCoy, Administrator of Beaver County Department of Human Services and Beaver County Behavioral Health. “Beaver County REACH (Respond, Educate, Assist, Connect & Help) will engage various groups in our community, including youth, families, veterans, first responders, individuals reentering the community after incarceration, older adults, and individuals employed in manufacturing/skilled trades, and deliver evidenced based trainings to increase mental health awareness and connections to needed treatment and supports.”
HHS’s Center for Mental Health Services (CMHS), which is housed in the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration program, awarded this funding. CMHS aims to improve the nation’s mental health by increasing state and community access to mental health services, addressing serious mental illness, and promoting recovery outcomes for Americans with mental and behavioral health conditions. Further grantee eligibility information is available here.
If you or someone you know is struggling, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available 24/7 by text, call, or chat: 988lifeline.org
The Trump Administration’s efforts to freeze funding and pause federal grants has created significant uncertainty for grantees, varying by agency and program. As of now, courts have paused many of these freezes. However, Congressman Deluzio’s office will continue to monitor these developments and fight to make sure this congressionally-authorized funding keeps going to projects that make life better for Western Pennsylvanians. If you are the recipient of a federal grant and have been notified that this funding is no longer available to you or are experiencing other issues accessing your lawfully appropriated funds, please share your concerns with Congressman Deluzio’s office at PA17Grants@mail.house.gov.

Pallone Introduces Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act
New Legislation Amends the No Surprises Act to Help Lower Health Insurance Premiums, Rein in Bad Actors, and Ensure Health Care Providers Are Paid Within 30 Days
Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) announced he’s introducing the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act that would fix the No Surprises Act's broken arbitration process, which bad actors have exploited to drive up health insurance premiums for everyday Americans.
“The No Surprises Act has been an overwhelming success when it comes to protecting patients from surprise medical bills. Prior to the law, millions of Americans were on the hook for surprise bills and caught in the middle of payment disputes,” Ranking Member Pallone said. “Today, I’m pleased to say patients no longer receive these outrageous bills, but unfortunately the arbitration process is clearly not working. A few bad actors—largely backed by private equity—are gaming the system, creating backlogs, delaying payments, and driving up premiums. The Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act will replace the broken arbitration system with a fair and timely payment process that lowers people’s health insurance premiums.”
Pallone was one of the authors of the bipartisan No Surprises Act in 2020, which took patients out of the middle of surprise billing payment disputes and established an arbitration process between health care providers and payers. The law established guidelines for determining a fair payment amount, but a series of court decisions in lawsuits have weakened those guidelines, resulting in increasingly large awards that overwhelmingly delay payments and drive up insurance premiums for millions of patients.
Today, a small number of organizations mostly backed by private equity account for the overwhelming majority of disputes filed through the arbitration process. Of the 2.5 million disputes submitted in 2025, approximately 67 percent were submitted by ten provider groups. Taken together, the 15 arbitration firms authorized to handle surprise billing disputes were paid $1.3 billion in fees in 2025 alone, compared to the $885 million these firms received from 2022 to 2024.
Collectively, the 15 arbitration firms awarded nearly $15 billion in payments to providers in 2025, which will result in higher premiums for consumers and employers. According to an analysis in Health Affairs, the arbitration process contributed to an estimated $22.4 billion in total costs over just four years. For instance, the New York State Employee Plan cited the arbitration award amounts as the primary contributor to the 10 percent premium increase this year.
The Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act will amend the No Surprises Act by replacing the broken arbitration system with a fairer payment system based on the median in-network rate and require that payments be issued within 30 days of the claim being filed.
“To help make health care more affordable, Congress needs to close the loopholes in existing law that private equity-backed and corporate firms are exploiting to secure inflated payments — loopholes that ultimately push premiums ever upward,” said Anthony Wright, Executive Director of Families USA. “While the bipartisan No Surprises Act continues to successfully protect patients from unexpected out-of-network medical bills, we need Congressional action to prevent premium increases due to corporate middlemen abusing its arbitration process. Representative Pallone's bill would take commonsense steps to replace the arbitration system with a market-based benchmark that ensures providers receive fair but not inflationary payments that raise costs for everyone. All who worry about health costs need Congress to act urgently to stand up to industry groups that have been profiteering off of the No Surprises Act arbitration process at the expense of consumers."
Legislative text of the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act is available HERE.

title: Pallone Introduces Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act

Gov Watchdog Finds Geothermal Developers Lack Permitting Tools Oil and Gas Companies Already Have
Washington, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a new report showing that companies trying to build geothermal power on public lands lack basic permitting tools that oil and gas companies already have and face confusing rules with no way to see where their permits stand, even as demand for geothermal development has grown more than fortyfold since 2020.
The watchdog report, requested by U.S. House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Susie Lee (D-Nev.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) found that the permitting process can be inconsistent and lacks transparency, creating uncertainty for geothermal developers and federal land managers. Oil and gas companies file permits online, track them through a dedicated system, and work from public handbooks, while geothermal developers submit permit applications in writing, wait on unpublished handbooks, and have no system tracking their permits.
The report comes as Congress has shown bipartisan interest in expanding geothermal energy development and private-sector interest in federal lands has grown significantly. According to GAO, nominations of federal lands for geothermal development increased from approximately 25,000 acres in 2020 to more than one million acres in 2025.
Despite this growing interest, geothermal developers reported to GAO inconsistent permitting decisions for exploration activities. BLM has developed handbooks intended to clarify terminology and provide consistent guidance, but those documents have remained in draft form since at least 2022. 
GAO also found that BLM lacks a comprehensive mechanism for tracking geothermal permitting activity. BLM shut down its geothermal tracking system in 2021, and the system that took its place has no way to track geothermal permits. Oil and gas wells, however, are tracked in a dedicated system from initial permitting through final closure. As a result, BLM has limited visibility into permitting timelines and workloads, making planning more difficult for both developers and federal officials to anticipate project timelines and resource needs.
The House has already voted to address these problems. The bipartisan Geothermal Energy Advancement Act (H.R. 5631), which passed the House in June, includes legislation sponsored by Rep. Lee, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, and Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.). Rep. Ansari’s Geothermal Gold Book Development Act would require the Bureau to publish standard permitting procedures, in line with GAO’s recommendation.
Read the full report and recommendations here.

U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12), and Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) are expressing concerns about workplace safety at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan and across other Southeast Michigan USPS Facilities. Since May 2026, employees have raised safety concerns and offered solutions to management, but to date employees report that nothing has been done to rectify the situation. 
“On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate,”
 the lawmakers wrote. 
The lawmakers continued:
“According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan. This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.” 
In a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, the lawmakers noted that the USPS has a responsibility to ensure that employees are safe and protected on the job.
A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:
Dear Postmaster General Steiner:
This letter is regarding workplace safety concerns at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan. We are concerned by the reports of unsafe practices at this facility and across Southeast Michigan.
On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate.
According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan.  This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.
Given the USPS’s role in ensuring worker safety, we request clarification on this matter and written responses to the following questions:
1. Was USPS aware that a non-maintenance supervisor had knowledge of and used a maintenance bypass code on multiple occasions, which could have led to serious, life-threatening consequences?
2. What steps will USPS take to ensure that only qualified employees have access to the maintenance code?
3. Have any disciplinary actions been taken, and if not, what correctional actions will USPS pursue?
4. How often are program evaluations, service talks, safety observations, and inspections conducted at this facility, as described in the Employee and Labor Relations Manual, and how will USPS adapt the safety training and protocols to address this problem at the facility?
5. What are the appropriate procedures for employees to communicate complaints or concerns with the appropriate staff when a supervisor is involved in an unsafe practice?
6. What future actions will USPS put in place to ensure a similar situation does not recur?
Ensuring worker safety remains our top priority. Thank you, and we look forward to your full and prompt response.
title: Dingell, Colleagues Express Concern Over Workplace Safety at Pontiac USPS Facility

Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon Visit Oakland Head Start Facility and Community Health Center, Condemn Republican Cuts to Childcare, Healthcare, and Education Programs
OAKLAND, CA – This week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12) hosted, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA-05), the highest-ranking woman in the House of Representatives, in Oakland’s Fruitvale neighborhood. They visited the Unity Council’s Head Start and Early Head Start Preschool facilities and La Clínica de La Raza, a federally qualified health center, to meet with families, frontline health care staff, and care workers who have been impacted by Republicans’ devastating federal aid cuts.
President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ “One Big, Cruel, Ugly Bill” has made deep cuts to federal funding for healthcare, childcare, education, and food assistance programs. In California’s 12th Congressional District, it is estimated that 31,000 people are experiencing rising healthcare costs and 35, 595 people will lose health coverage because of Republican cuts to Medi-Cal and decision to end enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits. In Congress, Congresswoman Simon has consistently fought against cuts to Medicaid/Medi-CAL and SNAP and attempts to gut Head Start.
“My daughter was a Head Start child, and I know intimately that federally supported childcare and healthcare is a lifeline for many families. It allows children to learn safely and be healthy while their parents attend school or work in our local businesses,” said Congresswoman Simon. “Whip Clark and I are taking everything we heard from our visit back to D.C., where we are hell bent on fighting this Administration and reversing their harmful policies so our Head Starts, our community health centers, our care workers, our families have everything they need to continue growing and being brilliant.”
"Congresswoman Lateefah Simon is an unrivaled champion for working families," said Democratic Whip Katherine Clark. "It was a privilege to join her in Oakland to see firsthand what communities need from the federal government: investments in healthcare, childcare, and the wellbeing of regular people, not giveaways to the ultra-rich. While the Republican Party continues to bend its knee to the billionaire class, Democrats are ready to take back the People's House and get to work for the working class.”
“We are honored to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark to Fruitvale and share firsthand the impact of The Unity Council’s work,” said CEO of The Unity Council, Chris Iglesias. “From giving our youngest learners, a strong foundation at our De Colores Head Start, to bringing La Catrina de Oakland to Fruitvale as a powerful celebration of culture and community, our work is rooted in creating opportunities and strengthening families. Their visit underscores the importance of continued investment in the people, programs, and places that allow communities like Fruitvale to thrive."
“At our De Colores Head Start Center, we see every day how a strong start can shape not only a child’s future, but an entire families’,” said Chief Early Learning Officer of The Unity Council, Luis Arenas. “Head Start creates opportunities for children to learn and grow while giving parents the support and resources they need to move their families forward. We were proud to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark into our classrooms and share the real, lasting impact this work has on families throughout our community.”
“We are deeply grateful to Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon for visiting La Clínica and for their tireless advocacy on behalf of the communities we serve. Their visit shows what federal investment looks like on the ground, and highlights what is at risk when coverage and resources for community health centers are reduced,” said La Clínica CEO, Jane García. “What’s at stake is whether parents can get their children to the doctor, whether patients can access dental and behavioral health care along with primary care, whether families can afford their medications, and whether community health centers have the resources to keep the staff who provide this care. La Clínica thanks Whip Clark and Congresswoman Simon for listening to our patients and staff and for bringing their voices back to Washington. The decisions made there have very real impacts here in the Bay Area.”

title: Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon Visit Oakland Head Start Facility and Community Health Center, Condemn Republican Cuts to Childcare, Healthcare, and Education Programs

WASHINGTON—Today, Congressman James P. McGovern (D-MA) released the following statement calling for the release of detained Egyptian journalists:
“As the Democratic Co-Chair of the bipartisan Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, I condemn the arrest of six journalists affiliated with the independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash and call on the government of Egypt to release them immediately. 
"On September 28, Egyptian security forces raided the homes of and arrested Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira and Abdullah Qadri, both of whom are editors at Matsadaash. Later that day, Egyptian state security arrested four additional journalists, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud, and Mohamed Adel, constituting the entirety of the newsroom. Authorities have not publicly issued charges against the journalists or justification for their arrest. 
"This comes after the Trump Administration shamefully released $320 million in military aid to Egypt which had been withheld due to human rights concerns.  
"Matsadaash has repeatedly been targeted by Egyptian authorities for its open-source investigative reporting. The recent arrest of its newsroom represents an alarming escalation of repression against independent media and freedom of expression in Egypt, particularly as some of the detainees report having been tortured.  Pursuant to its obligations as a state party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the Convention Against Torture, Egypt must respect the rights of its citizens to freedom of expression and freedom from arbitrary detention and torture. 
"As a partner in the Defending Freedoms Project, which campaigns to free prisoners of conscience around the world, I demand that the Egyptian government release the six detained journalists immediately. I also call on authorities to refrain from further targeting of members of the Matsadaash platform and other press workers.”
title: McGovern calls for the release of detained Egyptian journalists

Rep. Summer Lee Receives Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services
PITTSBURGH, PA – OCTOBER 8, 2026 — Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) received the Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services (RHLS), joining housing advocates, nonprofit developers, legal aid leaders, and community partners from across Pennsylvania at the organization’s annual awards reception in Downtown Pittsburgh.
Rep. Lee was recognized for her work advancing affordable housing and tenant protections in Congress and delivering federal investments for housing across Western Pennsylvania.
“I am proud to receive this award, but this one belongs to the tenants fighting to stay in their homes, the families trying to keep a roof over their heads, the organizers, lawyers, advocates, and nonprofit developers doing the hard work to keep our communities whole,” said Rep. Lee. “In Congress, I have been focused on putting federal dollars and federal protections behind that work, from bringing millions home for affordable housing to fighting for legal representation for tenants facing eviction and taking on Wall Street investors buying up our homes for profit. Nobody should have to watch their neighborhood finally get investment just in time to be priced out of it. We are going to keep fighting until staying in the community you helped build is something every single family can count on.”
Rep. Lee has brought millions of federal dollars home for affordable housing and community development, including $3 million for affordable housing projects across Allegheny County and $1 million to help convert underused office buildings in Downtown Pittsburgh into housing through her Community Project Funding initiatives.
Rep. Lee also helped advance the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a sweeping housing package that passed Congress with overwhelming bipartisan support and included provisions to limit additional single-family home purchases by large institutional investors, support home repairs and housing preservation, improve small-dollar mortgage access, and strengthen protections for homeowners challenging inaccurate appraisals. When President Trump initially withheld his signature from the bill, Rep. Lee publicly pushed for the housing relief to move forward without delay.
Her work in Congress has also focused on keeping families in their homes and preventing displacement. Rep. Lee introduced the Eviction Right to Counsel Act, which would help guarantee legal representation for low-income tenants facing eviction, and has fought to preserve affordable housing in historically underserved communities.
Rep. Lee also helped reintroduce the Stop Wall Street Landlords Act, legislation aimed at ending federal tax advantages that help large institutional investors buy up single-family homes and compete with working families.
During the event, Rep. Lee was honored alongside Pennsylvania Senate Minority Leader Jay Costa, Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato, State Rep. Lindsay Powell, and State Rep. Brandon Markosek.
To view photos/video from the event, please click HERE.
Congresswoman Summer Lee serves on the House Committee on Judiciary and the Committee on Education and Workforce. Since taking office in January 2023, she has delivered historic levels of federal investment totaling over $2.7 Billion brought back to Western PA, including over $580 million for infrastructure, over $110 million for affordable transit, over $500 million to keep clean energy manufacturing at home in Pennsylvania, and over $55 million on clean energy efforts in and around schools to help keep our kids and communities safe. These investments will help improve Western Pennsylvania’s infrastructure and transit, ensure cleaner air and drinking water, lower housing costs, fund research institutions, fuel clean manufacturing, fund STEM innovation and entrepreneurship, boost workforce development, and create thousands of good paying union jobs. Lee and her team have also delivered casework and constituent services to over 4,000 constituents with issues ranging from helping our seniors and disabled community access Medicare and social security to helping folks secure housing and helping families with immigration support and passports.
title: Rep. Summer Lee Receives Federal Housing Equity Award from Regional Housing Legal Services

Rep. Aguilar Highlights Importance of Food Assistance Programs for Cal State San Bernardino Students as Grocery Prices Rise
Faced with rising grocery costs, more CSUSB students are turning to the on-campus food pantry or enrolling in food assistance benefits
SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) held a press conference highlighting the impact of rising food prices on students and the importance of food assistance programs. This fall semester, 2,200 students at California State University, San Bernardino (CSUSB) have used the on-campus food pantry and student applications for CalFresh, California’s version of SNAP, have more than doubled since last year.
Across the country, people are struggling to afford the skyrocketing prices of gas, groceries, housing and electricity because of Trump’s and Republicans’ policies. Last year, Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill kicked more than 5 million Americans, including more than 340,000 Californians, off their food assistance benefits in order to give a tax break to billionaires. For CSUSB students, rising costs mean cutting back spending or relying more on food assistance programs and campus food pantries to avoid going hungry. You can watch the full video of the press conference here and find photos from the event above and here.
“Students are already juggling classes, homework, housing and even jobs and childcare, so finding enough to eat shouldn’t be another concern,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “That’s why CalFresh and the Obershaw DEN food pantry are so important. When you don’t have to worry about your next meal, you can focus in class and have energy for everything else college offers. Even after Trump and Republicans cut millions of Americans’ food assistance, I’m grateful that CSUSB students have somewhere to turn to so they don’t go hungry. But in the wealthiest nation on earth, this shouldn’t be the case. I’ll keep fighting to bring down costs and protect CalFresh so Inland Empire students get the meals they need to do well in school and graduate.”
“Students cannot fully focus on their education when they are worried about where their next meal will come from,” said President Terri Gómez, CSUSB. “CSUSB’s Basic Needs and Student Support services provide compassionate, holistic assistance — from food pantry access and CalFresh application support to emergency housing and other resources — so students can meet immediate challenges, remain focused on their goals and succeed academically.”

RELEASE: Squeezed by High Costs, Gottheimer Hosts Agriculture Roundtable with Sussex County Farmers
Farmers Hit with by High Diesel, Fertilizer, Equipment Costs, Tariffs, and Losses from Winter Freeze Announces New FROST Relief Act to Help Farmers Recover from April Freeze Outlines Farm Bill Priorities to Lower Costs, Help Specialty Crops and Give Farmers Certainty Continued Support for 4-H, FFA, and the Next Generation of Agriculture Leaders
Above: Gottheimer hosts agriculture roundtable.
AUGUSTA, NJ — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted an agriculture roundtable with farmers from across New Jersey’s Fifth District to hear how rising diesel, fertilizer, and equipment costs, low dairy prices, and a shrinking number of farms in the Garden State are putting family farms under pressure, along with concerns about fewer cooperative plants and fewer meat processing facilities, and concerns about shrinking access to milk haulers. Gottheimer also laid out his priorities for the final Farm Bill, focusing on specialty crops, dairy, and agritourism, and asked farmers what they need to see in the final bill.
“It’s because of all of you, and the more than 1,000 farms in New Jersey’s Fifth District, that families across our state and nation have fresh, high-quality, nutritious meals on the table,” said Gottheimer (NJ-5). “You do your part, every single day, rain or shine. The question for Washington is whether they’re doing everything they can for you. And right now, the clearest test of that is the Farm Bill.”
Farmers are getting squeezed from every direction. For a family farm already running on razor-thin margins, those costs add up fast. When it costs more to fuel the tractor, buy supplies, and get the crop to market, even a good harvest may not be enough.
Then came the freeze. Last April, a hard freeze hit right as crops were budding and blooming. Many growers lost a huge share of their harvest, including peaches, cherries, apples, strawberries, blueberries, and more, adding up to estimated losses of $300 million. For too many farmers, the help has not been there. New Jersey’s Fifth District is home to more than 1,000 farms, and New Jersey is a top-ten specialty crop state. Right now, a specialty crop grower can lose a season to a freeze and find that crop insurance does not fit the risk.
Meanwhile, the Farm Bill, which last became law in 2018, has been kicked down the road with one extension after another, leaving farmers unable to plan their planting season, equipment purchases, or hiring.
At the roundtable, he announced the Farmer Recovery Opportunity and Support for Temperatures (FROST) Relief Act, new federal legislation to help growers recover from the April freeze that caused an estimated $300 million in losses.
The FROST Relief Act and the TEMP Act will:
- Create a Block Grant Program for Freeze Losses: The FROST Relief Act would create a block grant program for farmers in the 13 states hit by the April freeze: Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia.
- Get Resources to Farmers Without Red Tape: The money goes to the states that were hit, so it can reach the farmers who lost their crops without months of red tape.
- Develop Temperature-Based Crop Insurance: The TEMP Act directs federal crop insurance to develop an affordable, temperature-based policy that covers freeze and cold-weather losses for specialty crop growers.
Gottheimer’s additional actions:
- Fight to Expand Rural Eligibility: In April, Gottheimer offered an amendment to the Farm Bill to raise the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) population cap for “rural” eligibility from 20,000 to 50,000, so more North Jersey communities can qualify for broadband and infrastructure support. It did not make it into the House bill, and it remains a top priority for the final bill.
- End the Hiring Freeze at the Farm Service Agency: Gottheimer offered amendments to end the hiring freeze at the Farm Service Agency (FSA), so loans and assistance get processed faster, especially for new and beginning farmers.
- Restore Local Food Resources: The Administration cut more than $1 billion from the Local Food for Schools and Local Food Purchase Assistance programs. Because of those cuts, New Jersey lost $26 million in commitments that would have supported 46 local farms and food producers, including 11 in the Fifth District. Gottheimer has demanded the resources be restored and offered a Farm Bill amendment to do it.
- Fix the SNAP Provisions in the House Bill: As written, the House bill would force New Jersey to cover 5 percent of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and raise the state’s share of administrative costs, adding up to $200 million a year in new costs for Jersey taxpayers. It would also push families off SNAP, stripping their children of automatic eligibility for free school meals. Gottheimer is urging the Senate to fix it, and he introduced the Feed Our Kids Act, which would provide free school meals to every student and push schools to buy nutritious food locally when they can.
- Back Specialty Crops and Rural Communities: Gottheimer is backing more resources for the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program, more help fighting invasive species including the spotted lanternfly, more investment for meat and poultry processors, and reliable, affordable broadband for rural communities.
- Stand Up for Jersey Dairy Farmers: After farmers raised the issue at a previous roundtable, Gottheimer backed whole milk in schools, and the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act was signed into law in January. He is also a member of the Dairy Caucus, so he can continue working across the aisle on commonsense solutions for dairy producers and sellers.
- Support the Next Generation of Jersey Agriculture: Ahead of National 4-H Week, celebrated annually during the first full week of October, Gottheimer reaffirmed his support for 4-H and USDA’s Positive Youth Development programs.
- Lower Costs and Go After Price Collusion: Gottheimer is pushing an All-of-the-Above Energy Plan to boost domestic capacity and bring down diesel and fertilizer costs, and he helped pass legislation to go after meat and poultry companies that collude to rig prices on the backs of hard-working families.
Gottheimer was joined by Ed Wengryn, New Jersey Secretary of Agriculture; Senator Parker Space, LD24 Senator; Louis Crescitelli, Chief of Staff to Senator Space; Commissioner Alan Henderson, Sussex County Commissioner; Commissioner Jill Space, Sussex Director Board of County Commissioners; Ken Schwemmer, Confidential Assistant to Commissioners; Liz Thompson, NJ Farm Bureau Executive Director; Paul Hlubik, USDA NJ Farm Service Agency State Committee Chair and NJ Agricultural Society President; Dave Foord, 4-H Senior Program Coordinator, RCE Sussex County, State 4-H Enrollment Coordinator; Holly Systema, Member of New Jersey State Board of Agriculture and the owner of The Farm at Windy Flats; Rocky Hazelman, President of the Passaic County Board of Agriculture and the Chairman of the Passaic County Agriculture Development Board; Stacey Kennedy, NJ Agricultural Society Director; Joe Atchison III, NJ Department of Agriculture Assistant Secretary and NJ Department of Agriculture Marketing and Development Director; Mike Burger, Sussex County Board of Agriculture President; Lindsay Caragher, USDA NJ Farm Service Agency Deputy State Executive Director; Rich Byma, Dairy Farmer at By-Acre Holsteins; Phil and Keri Brodhecker, Beef and Grain Farmers at Brodhecker Farms; Jason Swarts, Dairy Farmer for Deckertown Holsteins; Pete Southway, Springhouse Creamery; Mitchell Jones, Mountain Top Farm in Warren County.
Below: Gottheimer hosts agriculture roundtable.

Gov Watchdog Finds Geothermal Developers Lack Permitting Tools Oil and Gas Companies Already Have
Washington, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a new report showing that companies trying to build geothermal power on public lands lack basic permitting tools that oil and gas companies already have and face confusing rules with no way to see where their permits stand, even as demand for geothermal development has grown more than fortyfold since 2020.
The watchdog report, requested by U.S. House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Susie Lee (D-Nev.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) found that the permitting process can be inconsistent and lacks transparency, creating uncertainty for geothermal developers and federal land managers. Oil and gas companies file permits online, track them through a dedicated system, and work from public handbooks, while geothermal developers submit permit applications in writing, wait on unpublished handbooks, and have no system tracking their permits.
The report comes as Congress has shown bipartisan interest in expanding geothermal energy development and private-sector interest in federal lands has grown significantly. According to GAO, nominations of federal lands for geothermal development increased from approximately 25,000 acres in 2020 to more than one million acres in 2025.
Despite this growing interest, geothermal developers reported to GAO inconsistent permitting decisions for exploration activities. BLM has developed handbooks intended to clarify terminology and provide consistent guidance, but those documents have remained in draft form since at least 2022. 
GAO also found that BLM lacks a comprehensive mechanism for tracking geothermal permitting activity. BLM shut down its geothermal tracking system in 2021, and the system that took its place has no way to track geothermal permits. Oil and gas wells, however, are tracked in a dedicated system from initial permitting through final closure. As a result, BLM has limited visibility into permitting timelines and workloads, making planning more difficult for both developers and federal officials to anticipate project timelines and resource needs.
The House has already voted to address these problems. The bipartisan Geothermal Energy Advancement Act (H.R. 5631), which passed the House in June, includes legislation sponsored by Rep. Lee, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, and Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.). Rep. Ansari’s Geothermal Gold Book Development Act would require the Bureau to publish standard permitting procedures, in line with GAO’s recommendation.
Read the full report and recommendations here.

SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, released the following statement regarding the Trump administration’s actions to suspend Microsoft’s ability to sponsor workers through the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program.
“This is a crucial issue for me as the top Democrat on the Immigration Subcommittee, the only member of Congress to have actually had an H-1B visa, and the Representative for tens of thousands of Microsoft workers. The administration has been consistently working to take away legal pathways for immigrants to contribute their talents to our country, and this is yet another of those attacks.
“The PERM program is the first step toward an employment-based green card for countless workers who want to contribute to this country, and it lays out a clear process with steps to ensure that this is a net benefit to our economy and does not harm American jobs. Our economy, our communities, and our families depend on immigrants in many sectors, including the tech sector, and heavy-handed attacks like this only hurt efforts to build a strong, stable, and diverse base of workers who have legal pathways to come and be in the United States while also protecting U.S. workers from unscrupulous employers.
“You don’t fix a broken immigration system by taking a hammer to legal immigration. Microsoft has been a leader in advocating for comprehensive immigration reforms that modernize an antiquated immigration system and provide more — not fewer — legal pathways for immigrants from all over the world to work here and be with their families. Targeting Microsoft or the PERM program in this way simply undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate.”

Congresswoman Gwen Moore Leads Effort to Crack Down on Corrupt, Taxpayer-Funded Settlements
Congresswoman Gwen Moore introduced the Executive Settlement Review Act to provide stronger oversight and independent review and approval of any legal settlements that occur between the President, his political allies, or personal associates, and the federal government they oversee. This legislation comes as the Trump administration has sought to use taxpayer funds for a $1.8 billion slush fund, which could have paid violent January 6th insurrectionists.
“Trump has attempted to use sham government settlements to enrich himself and protect his family from legal scrutiny. And it likely doesn’t stop at him. I’m dismayed by recent reports that Treasury Secretary Bessent may be negotiating sweetheart deals with the IRS for himself. Congress and the Judiciary must work to prevent corruption and grift in the executive branch. My bill, the Executive Settlement Review Act, fulfills a need for a fair and comprehensive process to ensure that our tax dollars aren’t misused and that the public and Congress are aware of the details of any settlement that are at a heightened risk of abuse,” said Congresswoman Gwen Moore.
The provisions of this bill would apply to pending lawsuits brought against the United States by the currently serving President, Vice President, Cabinet members, certain senior federal officials, their families, and their businesses, with exemptions for those seeking small claims.
Key Provisions of the bill:
    - Formal filing of the proposed agreement by the Department of Justice with a federal district court, led by a panel of three judges.
- A 60-day period in which the public can and submit comments on any proposed settlements, comments that the government must address and which the court must consider. 
- Submission of written briefs to the court by both parties outlining the merits and rationale of the agreement, including the disclosure of any documents or communications that informed their decision to settle.
- Review of the settlement by the three-judge district court panel, who will assess whether the settlement agreement is lawful, factual, and settles a legitimate legal dispute, among other criteria.
title: Congresswoman Gwen Moore Leads Effort to Crack Down on Corrupt, Taxpayer-Funded Settlements

October 8, 2026
MEDIA CONTACT:
e: jessica.myers@mail.house.gov
c: 202.913.0126
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY-09) and Julia Letlow (R-LA-05) introduced a bipartisan, bicameral resolution to establish October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18th as World Menopause Day. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced the resolution’s companion in the Senate.
These observances will contribute to the spread of global awareness and access to care during menopausal transition and post-menopause, as well as provide organizations and individuals around the world with an opportunity to advocate for resources and support for the 75 million American women in perimenopause, menopause, and post-menopause.
“Throughout our lives, women deserve the support we need to confront every trial and embrace every triumph each of our chapters has in store for us. Menopause is a natural experience that we all must face, yet the stigma that follows it continues to inflict needless ridicule and shame on women at a time when all we ask for is acceptance and understanding,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “World Menopause Awareness Month and World Menopause Day will be the bridges to normalizing menopause and ensuring the women confronting it have the resources, care, and confidence they need to tackle their new horizons head on, and I am proud to lead this bipartisan legislation to see both codified as national observances.”
“Through any stage of life, women need access to reliable information to make educated decisions about their health. World Menopause Awareness Month shines a light on the millions of women undergoing menopause every year, highlighting the need for women to have a better understanding of the treatments and options available to them,” said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.
“Generations of women have faced the transition to menopause, yet for too long this experience has been overlooked, under-researched, and treated as taboo,” said Lisa Senator Blunt Rochester. “It’s far past time we ensure women have the care and support they need to feel their best in all phases of life. I’m proud to introduce the World Menopause Awareness Month Resolution to elevate the challenges of menopause and encourage further investments into research that will help women meet this transition with confidence.”
“Our health care system has failed women struggling with menopausal symptoms that disrupt their livelihoods, and this unfortunate reality disproportionately affects Black and Hispanic women,” said Senator Cory Booker. “This resolution is a reminder that we must do more to support women navigating menopause and provide them with the resources they need. Menopause should not be a barrier to the quality of life every woman deserves.”
“The resolution introduced by Congresswoman Yvette Clarke represents another important step toward breaking down the barriers that have too often left women without the information, care, and relief they need throughout the menopause transition,” said Donna Klassen of Let’s Talk Menopause. “We proudly support this resolution and applaud Congresswoman Clarke’s leadership in bringing greater attention to menopause, expanding access to trusted health information and care, and ensuring women have the resources they need to navigate this stage of life with confidence and support.”
“Menopause is a universal experience for women, and yet, for too long menopause has been understudied. This has left us with significant knowledge gaps about menopause itself, including its symptoms and treatments, but also about the effects of menopause on overall health and healthy aging. Fortunately, we now have momentum to course correct. The Society for Women’s Health Research thanks Representative Clarke for her leadership on the resolution designating October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18 as World Menopause Day. We must collectively continue raising awareness about menopause, which can help shape research priorities and ensure women and health care providers have the evidence and information needed to make informed decisions about menopause care,” said Lindsey Miltenberger of the Society for Women’s Health Research.
Menopause is more than a personal, biological transition—it has lasting implications for women’s health and well-being, and for families, workplaces, and society. The Black Women’s Health Imperative endorses this resolution to recognize October as World Menopause Awareness Month and expand awareness, provider education, and access to the resources and care that women, particularly Black women, need for a healthy, dignified menopause, ” said Ifeoma Udoh, Ph.D. of the Black Women’s Health Imperative.
The resolution is endorsed by the American Medical Association, Astellas, Greater New York Hospital Association, Healthcare Association of New York State, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Mount Sinai Health System, National Medical Association, National Minority Quality Forum, Novo Nordisk, Inc., NYU Langone Health, One Brooklyn Health System, Reproductive Health Access Project, Ritual, The Fibroid Foundation, and The White Dress Project.
Read the full bill text HERE.

Rep. Torres Introduces the Improving Access to WIC Act to Ease Access to Nutrition Support for Moms and Children
With More Than 4 in 10 WIC-eligible families Not Enrolled, Legislation Closes Gap by Helping States Strengthen Partnerships with Healthcare Providers, Lower Barriers to Participation, and Boost Outreach Efforts
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) introduced the Improving Access to WIC Act, legislation to make it easier to enroll in and stay connected to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). As families struggle with the ongoing affordability crisis, WIC helps feed mothers from the moment they find out they are pregnant to when their children are five years old. WIC not only helps moms access free, healthy foods, but also helps with breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health resources.
Nearly 25,000 mothers, infants, and children benefit from WIC in California’s 35th Congressional District. Nationwide, in fiscal year 2025, WIC served 6.9 million participants every month. The program is proven to save lives and improve lifetime health outcomes. Despite this, the most recent data show that more than 4 in 10 eligible individuals do not participate in WIC, and WIC utilization is lower for pregnant mothers and 1- to 4-year-olds. This legislation will tackle this participation gap.
The Improving Access to WIC Act would establish a federal grant program for states, tribes, and territories to improve access to, participation in, and retention in WIC. States that opt into the program would receive flexible funding to help strengthen partnerships between WIC agencies and healthcare providers, modernize the enrollment experience, improve community outreach, and help enroll mothers and children on SNAP and Medicaid who already qualify for WIC but do not yet participate.
“WIC provides critical nutrition assistance to moms, babies, and young children, and getting enrolled should not mean jumping through unnecessary hoops,” said Congresswoman Torres. “Moms are already juggling doctor’s appointments, work, child care, and countless responsibilities. We should be making it easier, not harder, for eligible families to access the support they need. My Improving Access to WIC Act will help states integrate WIC enrollment with healthcare providers, reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork, and make it easier for families to enroll and stay on WIC.”
“Despite the incredible public health benefits of WIC, we are still reaching only a little more than half of eligible families. Investing in targeted outreach, data sharing, and healthcare linkages will make it easier for families who qualify to connect with WIC. We thank Rep. Torres for her leadership and support for WIC.” Georgia Machell, President & CEO, National WIC Association
“WIC is an evidence-based, time-limited program with proven positive outcomes for families and communities, yet there is a significant portion of eligible families not connected to services. Supporting innovative outreach methods and healthcare linkages to improve access to the program is an important investment. We appreciate Rep. Torres’s support for WIC and young families.” Megan Esparza, Executive Director, California WIC Association
“The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC) is one of the most critical tools pediatricians have to ensure infants and young children can receive proper nutrition support in their earliest years. The Improving Access to WIC Act would provide states with resources to make enrolling eligible families in WIC easier, more efficient, and more effective. The American Academy of Pediatrics thanks Representative Torres for introducing this important legislation and calls on Congress to advance it,” said Andrew D. Racine, MD, PhD, FAAP, President of the American Academy of Pediatrics.
“The American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists has a long history of supporting the WIC program and is proud to endorse the Improving Access to WIC Act,” said ACOG President Camille A. Clare, MD, MPH, CPE. “Families are facing growing financial pressure, and putting healthy food on the table can be especially difficult during pregnancy and after a baby is born. With significant changes to SNAP under H.R. 1, making WIC easier to access is more important than ever. This bill would help eligible families get the nutrition support they need instead of getting stuck in red tape. ACOG thanks Rep. Norma Torres for her leadership and commitment to strengthening the WIC program.”
"WIC is a proven intervention that supports the health of women, babies, and young children. Yet far too many eligible families are missing out on the many benefits of the program. We applaud Rep. Torres for introducing the Improving Access to WIC Act. Establishing a federal grant program to help states improve access to and participation in WIC would make it easier for eligible families to connect with this critical support. We urge Members of Congress to co-sponsor this legislation, so more families are connected to the nutrition they need to thrive." - Crystal FitzSimons, President of the Food Research & Action Center (FRAC).
The bill is supported by: National WIC Association (NWA), California WIC Association (CWA), American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), Food Research and Action Center (FRAC), Alliance to End Hunger, Coalition on Human Needs.
Bill Summary:
The Improving Access to WIC Act authorizes $50 million for Fiscal Years 2027 through 2031 for the grant program. States, tribes, and territories that choose to opt in would receive, to the maximum extent practicable, $200,000 and an additional amount based on each participating state’s national share of WIC participants.
The bill also requires the U.S. Department of Agriculture to publicly report on the program’s outcomes, including its impact on WIC participation and retention, and share best practices that states can use to improve enrollment and access.
Under the legislation, participating states could use grant funding to:
- Connect more eligible families with WIC by: 
  - Improving outreach in clinical settings and building up systems to make it easier for doctors and health care providers to directly refer patients to WIC, including through statewide referral systems, and
  - Expanding outreach in trusted community settings, including at Head Start and Early Head Start programs, preschools, schools, and other places to meet WIC-eligible families where they are.
- Improve secure data sharing between health care providers and WIC agencies to streamline WIC referrals and certification, while protecting privacy, requiring individual consent, and maintaining federal confidentiality protections.
- Reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork by making it easier for health care providers, consistent with applicable laws and with individuals’ consent, to securely provide WIC agencies with information such as height, weight, hemoglobin measurements (blood tests), and other documentation needed for WIC certification.
- Modernize the enrollment process, including by establishing or expanding online WIC applications.
- Help reach and enroll moms and children on Medicaid (Medi-Cal) or SNAP (CalFresh) who already qualify for WIC, but are not participating.
Original Cosponsors: Nanette Barragán (CA-44); Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01); Yvette Clarke (NY-09 ); Jim Costa (CA-21); Jasmine Crockett (TX-30); Chris Deluzio (PA-17); Debbie Dingell (MI-06); Sylvia Garcia (TX-29); Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04); Adelita S. Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.
2026 was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and devastating lives. Weather conditions, exacerbated by extended drought, heat, and wind, caused over 900,000 acres, or 1,400 square miles, to burn across Washington state – taking homes and lives. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead.
In the Eighth District, the Little Giant, Three Queens, Sisi, King, Goat, and West Fork fires – among others – devastated communities, property, livestock, and businesses. The damages from this wildfire season continues to overwhelm state, local, Tribal, nonprofit, and private-sector capabilities.
“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” members of the delegation wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”
Joining Congresswoman Schrier in the letter to President Trump were Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), and U.S. Representatives Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Dan Newhouse (R, WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (R, WA-05), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10).
The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”
“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.
The full letter is available HERE.
title: Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State
