text:
RELEASE: On Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly, Gottheimer Marks Third Anniversary of October 7th
Introduces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember 10/7, Combat Terror
Above: Gottheimer announces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember October 7th in Tenafly alongside Alexander Family.
TENAFLY, NJ — Today, Wednesday, October 7, 2026, on the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined local leaders, community members, and the family of former hostage Edan Alexander on Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly to remember the victims, honor the hostages and their families, and announce new efforts to combat terror. Gottheimer, along with U.S. Representatives Lois Frankel (FL-22), Joe Wilson (SC-2), and Young Kim (CA-40), and dozens of their colleagues, introduced a bipartisan resolution marking the third anniversary of October 7th.
Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here and here.
“We will speak the truth about October 7th. We will stand up to hate, wherever it rears its ugly head. And we will never stop fighting for the day when Hamas lays down its arms for good, and communities can live in peace free from terror,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “We cannot pretend the work is done. Hamas has not disarmed. The terrorists who carried out October 7th still hold weapons and still hold power in Gaza, and they will keep threatening Israel, and the Palestinian people until that changes.”
Gottheimer also announced new and continuing efforts to combat terror and antisemitism:
- October 7th Remembrance Resolution: The bipartisan resolution honors every person murdered on October 7th, condemns the attacks as the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust, and honors the hostages and their families. It also supports Israel’s right to defend herself, a durable cease-fire, and the full implementation of the framework, including Hamas disarmament, humanitarian aid and reconstruction for Gazans, and a future for Gaza without Hamas. The resolution also condemns the rise in antisemitism at home, including in schools and on college campuses. The House resolution is endorsed by the American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), Hadassah, Jewish Women International, and the Israel Allies Foundation.
- Holding the United Nations accountable: New legislation with Congressman Lawler (NY) that would bar U.S. funds from going toward U.S. contributions to the United Nations until the U.N. has designated Hamas and Hezbollah as terrorist organizations. This is critical as UNRWA currently does not screen for Hamas ties in its hiring of teachers and other employees, leading to Hamas terrorists infiltrating its ranks. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
- October 7th Gold Medal Act: Bipartisan legislation introduced last year with Congressman Lawler (NY) to award the Congressional Gold Medal to the American victims and hostages of October 7th, including Americans like Edan who survived captivity in Gaza. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Hostages and Missing Families Forum, American Jewish Committee (AJC), the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Jewish Women International, the Weitzman National Museum of Jewish American History, and the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
- October 7th Remembrance Education Act: Bipartisan legislation introduced last year with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA) to direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to build a model curriculum for schools to teach the attacks committed on October 7 and the antisemitism that followed. The bipartisan bill is endorsed by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), Jewish Women International, and the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).
The announcement builds on Gottheimer’s work since the attacks, including securing $100 million in the defense bill for his U.S.-Israel Anti-Killer Drone Act to counter drone attacks from Iran and its proxies, along with a provision to stop Hamas weapons smuggling on the Gaza-Egypt border; House passage last month of his bipartisan bill to cut off funds to colleges that enable BDS on their campuses; and legislation with Congressman Lawler to dismantle UNRWA and replace it with humanitarian assistance out of the hands of Hamas terrorists. At home, Gottheimer continues to work across the aisle to boost funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program so that every synagogue, church, mosque, and temple has the resources to protect itself.
Gottheimer noted the sharp rise in antisemitism since October 7th: the ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States last year, a 68 percent increase since 2022, with New Jersey ranking third highest in the country and Bergen County recording 139 incidents, the most in the state.
“Three years later, the horror of October 7th remains seared into our hearts,” said Congresswoman Lois Frankel. “We remember those who were murdered, honor the survivors and hostages and their families, and stand firmly against antisemitism and terrorism. Now we must build a future where Hamas is disarmed, Israel is safe and secure, and Palestinians and Israelis can live in peace and dignity.”
“Today marks the third anniversary of the massacre of 1,200 and kidnapping of 251 innocent men, women, and children in Israel by the Iranian terrorist puppet, Hamas. This cowardly act will forever be remembered around the world, but no more meaningful than to the families and friends who lost loved ones. I am grateful for the leadership of President Donald Trump, with the support of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and our allies, for ensuring that all hostages, living and deceased, were brought home,” said Congressman Joe Wilson.
“Three years ago, the world witnessed unspeakable evil as Hamas carried out the deadliest massacre of the Jewish people since the Holocaust. We remember the 1,200 innocent lives lost, the hostages who faced unimaginable suffering in Hamas captivity, families whose lives were irrevocably changed, and the extraordinary courage and selflessness shown by ordinary Israelis on that day,” said Congresswoman Young Kim. “We will never forget the darkness of October 7th or allow the world to forget what happened. As antisemitism continues to rear its ugly head around the world, the United States must stand firmly with the Jewish people and confront this hatred in all its forms.”
“Three years after Hamas’s October 7th attack on Israel, we remember and mourn the more than 1,200 innocent people brutally murdered, honor the hostages who have finally returned home and the families who endured unimaginable pain, and stand with all those whose lives were forever changed. American Jewish Committee proudly supports this bipartisan resolution introduced by Representatives Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Young Kim (R-CA), Lois Frankel (D-FL), and Joe Wilson (R-SC), which ensures the atrocities of October 7 are never forgotten and reaffirms America’s commitment to Israel’s security and the fight against antisemitism,” said Ted Deutch, CEO of American Jewish Committee.
“The tragedy of October 7 and the surge in antisemitism that followed that day will forever be etched in the memory of the Jewish people,” said ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt. “On this solemn third anniversary of the attack, we remember the innocent lives lost, the hostages who were taken, and the survivors whose lives were changed forever. We thank Reps. Gottheimer, Wilson, Frankel, and Kim for introducing this bipartisan resolution and for honoring the victims and survivors of October 7, and reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that ‘Never Again’ truly means never again.”
“Three years after October 7, we honor the memory of every person murdered by Hamas and its terrorist allies, and we honor the hostages and their families who endured unimaginable suffering. This resolution is an important affirmation that complete disarmament of Hamas and dismantling of its terrorist infrastructure are essential to ensuring that October 7 can never happen again and to building a future of security, peace, and dignity for Israelis and their neighbors. It also reinforces that we must confront the dangerous rise of antisemitism that has followed October 7 and continue to work hand-in-hand with government to ensure that our communities are secure in the face of this violent threat,” said Eric D. Fingerhut, President & CEO of Jewish Federations of North America.
“On the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, we pray for the innocent lives lost and renew our resolve to thwart future threats to peace. Hamas has yet to capitulate and disarm in Gaza, and terror groups continue to operate alongside Israel’s borders, sustained by state sponsors of terrorism. On this solemn day, we recognize that peace has not yet been achieved, and that further efforts are needed to safeguard civilians and demilitarize those bent on perpetuating violence,” said Tyler Stapleton, Senior Director of Government Relations, FDD Action.
“As we mark three years since Hamas terrorists carried out the deadliest attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust, we remember and honor all those who were murdered, injured, tortured, raped or held captive by Hamas. We thank Representatives Lois Frankel, Josh Gottheimer, and Joe Wilson for introducing this resolution, which condemns the atrocities of October 7, 2023, affirms Israel’s right to self-defense and supports the critical conditions of the ceasefire, including the disarmament of Hamas. We urge members of Congress to support this bipartisan resolution and to continue to confront the rise in violent antisemitism across the country and around the world,” said Carol Ann Schwartz, National President, Hadassah, The Women’s Zionist Organization of America.
“I listened with horror to whispers of the sexual atrocities committed by Hamas. I watched with horror the video of young women, pulled from their beds and pushed bloodied into trucks to be taken into Gaza. I saw with horror the photo of a naked, bound woman surrounded by terrorists raising guns in victory. I sat with horror in the silence of the world, in the silence of the feminist organizations. In the three years since, the silence, the denial, the distortion, and the hate not only continue; they grow. It is virulent and dangerous. Resolutions like this are critical in the fight against hate and disinformation. We are grateful to Representatives Gottheimer, Frankel, and Joe Wilson for standing up to hate and amplifying the truth. For those who died, and those who survived, we owe them as much,” said Meredith Jacobs, CEO of Jewish Women International (JWI).
Gottheimer was joined by Tenafly Mayor Mark Zinna, Tenafly Councilwoman Lauren Dayton, Tenafly Councilwoman, Jenny Jackson, Adi and Yael Alexander, and Rabbi Kirshner of Temple Emanu-El, Debra Mazon and her colleagues from Hadassah, Rabbi Levy from AJC, Brandi Katz Rubin from the ADL, and Shlomo Schorr from Agudath Israel, Rabbi Shmuel Bergman from Young Israel of Fort Lee, Rabbi Genack and his wife Sarah from Englewood, Tenafly Police Chief Michael Greenly, Rabbi Krishner with Temple Emanu-El, Rabbi Zev Reichman from East Hill Synagogue, and the Alexander family.
Below: Gottheimer Announces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember October 7th in Tenafly.
Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:
Good morning. Thank you all for joining us on this solemn day as we mark three years since October 7th, the deadliest attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust. As many of you know, for 842 days the posters of every single hostage held in Gaza hung on the wall outside my office in Washington – right next to the Israeli flag.  
It was a reminder to everyone who visited the United States Capitol of the responsibility we held here in the United States to do our part, not only for our key ally, but for what is right, until every hostage was returned to their families. The hostage photos were not just Israelis. They were of Americans. Of Thais. French. British. Filipinos. They were young and old. L’dor vador, from generation to generation. We all had a responsibility to do everything in our power, in every corner of the globe, to bring them home. It is a relief that this anniversary is the first without the need to wear yellow ribbons calling for the return of those being held.
Yet, as I walk past the empty wall into my office every day, I can still see those images, staring at me. It’s almost a reminder to me that we must never forget what happened – and of the work that lies ahead to heal and bring us back together. As it’s said in Isaiah, “Your ancient ruins shall be rebuilt; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations; you shall be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of streets to live in.”
Let’s be honest. We have a great deal of repairing and restoration ahead of us.
But, on this third anniversary of October 7th, while we mourn those we lost, we also have much to be grateful for – for all the hostages who were reunited with their loved ones, who are rebuilding their lives. Among those taken that day, and who came home, was our very own Edan Alexander, a young man from right here in Tenafly. A graduate of Tenafly High School, who swam on the swim team and biked on these streets, a Jersey boy through and through. Today, we are standing here on Edan Alexander Way, a street we named last year in honor of his unshakable strength and courage.
To Adi and Yael Alexander: thank you for being with us today. I know Edan can’t be here, but I know he is living his life to the fullest today in Israel. I met your family on October 23rd, 2023, just over two weeks after the attack, and you have been like family to me and Marla ever since. For nearly two years, while Edan endured the unimaginable, you never — not for a single moment — surrendered hope. You called for action, and you would not be quieted until your son came home.
You pressed me, as you pressed so many others in our community, for action and for answers. And, I was proud to carry the courage and conviction you gave me, both on my trips to the Middle East and in the halls of Congress every single day.
I especially want to thank the people of Tenafly. Three years ago today, the world changed, and this community was asked to carry something unimaginable. But, you never recoiled – you never looked away. You stood here with the Alexander family while Hamas terrorists held their son for 584 days.
You stood in Huyler Park at five o’clock in the morning to watch him be released – I was there – and you filled these streets by the thousands to welcome Edan home in May of last year. You showed what a town can do when it stands together.
You’ve also shown us the importance of never forgetting.
That’s especially important today when some are actually glorifying Hamas terrorists as martyrs – or trying to justify the actions that day, when Hamas terrorists brutally murdered, raped, burned alive, decapitated, and kidnapped more than twelve hundred people – including innocent babies, children, women, men, and elderly people, and dozens of Americans, while taking 251 hostages into tunnels in Gaza. It’s unfathomable.
Some may try to bury their head in the sand or rewrite history. But, anybody who has seen the videos and images of those heinous and unthinkable acts knows what Hamas and its accomplices are capable of. They sowed terror at the Nova music festival, in the kibbutzim, in cities across Southern Israel. Like many of you, I traveled to Israel afterward to see their path of destruction with my own eyes – to give me the first-hand knowledge to confront the haters.
But, despite the truth, since Hamas’s devastating attack, we have unfortunately witnessed a tidal wave of antisemitism that has only grown more persistent, starting just hours after the terrorists attacked Israel. Instead of empathy from people and organizations around the globe, there was a flood of criticism and blame, and it hasn’t stopped.
Just days after the October 7 attack, during the “Day of Rage” in New York City, someone shouted at a group of Jewish people: “I wish Hitler was still here; he would’ve wiped all of you out.” Other protestors said: “Say it loud, say it clear, we don’t want Zionists here!”
At Columbia University, Jewish students were chased out of their dorms, received death threats, were spat upon, stalked, and pinned against walls. People in masks screamed, “Go back to Poland!” and “Globalize the Intifada.” On October 8th, the day after the largest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust, a faculty member at Rutgers declared October 7th “awesome.”
Three years later, the protests continue – including today – against Jews simply practicing their religion in America.
Recently, at one just outside a synagogue chanting hateful slogans like “We are all Hamas,” “Death to Zionists,” and “Long live October 7th” at worshippers. Businesses have even boycotted my Jewish colleagues – refusing to serve them.
Last year, the ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States. That’s a 68 percent increase since 2022, before October 7th. And here in New Jersey, we ranked third highest in the entire country. Right here in Bergen County, we had 139 incidents, the most in New Jersey.
No other county in our state had more than 80. That’s our backyard. And, now you have internet personalities like Hasan Piker and Candace Owens spreading misinformation and hate to millions of followers online, with comments like calling a Jewish reporter a “Pig Dog,” justifying the violence on October 7th as “resistance”, blood libel, and conspiracy theories about Jewish control.
I say this not only as your Congressman, but also as a member of the Jewish community. This is deeply personal for me.
But, even in those moments of despair, we have also seen moments that give us hope. Light through the darkness.
Just a month ago, I joined the Chancellor of Vanderbilt, along with leaders from colleges ranging from the University of Alabama to Washington University to the University of Texas, in saying that hatred and religious discrimination against anyone isn’t welcome on their campus. We’ve had leaders in business, nonprofits, in the arts, in Hollywood, and in government stand strong against antisemitism, even though it has cost them personally.
Nations like the UAE and Argentina have bucked their own history and doubled down to protect the Jewish people.
And, of course, the greatest light. On May 12th of 2025, Edan came home. I will never forget the moment I first met him after his release. His humility, poise, and self-assurance stopped me in my tracks. He told me he was not a hero, that the real heroes were the ones still there … those who gave their lives. And, then he said something that will echo in my heart forever: “My story doesn’t end with survival. It continues with service.”
He meant it. Edan returned to the Israel Defense Forces and has since been promoted to Sergeant First Class. Just this summer, he stood before the world at the opening ceremony of the Maccabiah Games to explain why he went back into uniform. He has refused to let evil triumph. So neither can we.
A year ago this month, the remaining twenty living hostages came home. And in the months since, the remains of the fallen were returned, including Americans Omer Neutra and Itay Chen, whose families waited and waited until the last were finally brought home in January. Today, we remember every one of them.
We cannot pretend the work is done. Hamas has not disarmed. The terrorists who carried out October 7th still hold weapons and still hold power in parts of Gaza, and they will keep threatening Israel, and the Palestinian people until that changes.
That is why today, three years later, I am proud to announce new efforts to combat terror.
First, I’ve introduced a bipartisan resolution marking the third anniversary of October 7th. It honors every person murdered by Hamas. It condemns the attacks as the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust.
It honors the hostages and their families. It supports Israel’s right to defend herself, a durable cease-fire, and the full implementation of the framework, including Hamas disarmament, humanitarian aid and reconstruction for Gazans, and a future for Gaza without Hamas. And, it condemns the rise in antisemitism here at home, including in our schools and on our college campuses. I’m proud to be joined by Representatives Lois Frankel, Joe Wilson, and Young Kim, as well as fifty of my colleagues in introducing this resolution.
Second, I’m introducing legislation to hold the United Nations accountable.
Here’s the simple, shocking truth: the UN has never designated Hamas or Hezbollah as terrorist organizations. Not before October 7th. Not after. The Security Council maintains sanctions lists for ISIS and al-Qaeda, but not for Iran’s proxies. And, because Hamas isn’t on the list, UN agencies, including UNRWA, don’t even screen for Hamas membership when they hire. The USAID Inspector General has found more than 100 UNRWA staff with Hamas affiliations, even though we believe there are far more, and only nine have been fired for direct involvement in the October 7 attacks. That is unacceptable.
So, my bill is straightforward. No U.S. funds can go toward our contributions to the United Nations until the Security Council has designated Hamas and Hezbollah as the terrorist organizations that they are.
Today, we are also recommitting to two bipartisan bills I introduced last year, and that I am continuing the fight to pass them.
The October 7th Gold Medal Act, with Congressman Lawler from New York, will award the Congressional Gold Medal to the American victims and hostages of October 7th, including Americans like Edan who survived captivity in Gaza.
And, the October 7th Remembrance Education Act, with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick from Pennsylvania, will direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to build a model curriculum for schools to teach the heinous and brutal attacks committed on October 7th, and the antisemitism that followed.
We can’t afford for our children to learn history – and be filled with anti-American, antisemitism-filled disinformation — from TikTok. From Hasan Piker. The truth and the facts – history – should be taught in every classroom across America.
This builds on the work we’ve been doing since that terrible day. This summer, I secured $100 million in the defense bill for my U.S.-Israel Anti-Killer Drone Act to counter drone attacks from Iran and its proxies, along with a provision to stop Hamas weapons smuggling on the Gaza-Egypt border.
Just last month, the House passed my bipartisan bill to cut off funds to colleges that enable BDS on their campuses. With Congressman Lawler, I also introduced legislation to dismantle UNRWA and replace it with humanitarian assistance we can trust, out of the hands of Hamas terrorists.
Here at home, we’re going to keep working across the aisle to boost funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program, so every synagogue, church, mosque, and temple has the resources to protect itself.
This is not a red or blue issue. It’s about the safety of our families. Our Jersey Values mean that we don’t allow our communities to be torn apart. We stand together and protect one another. That’s exactly what we’re doing here today in Tenafly, just feet from Edan Alexander.
So today, we remember. We honor those we lost. We thank the heroes. And we recommit ourselves to the work ahead.
We will speak the truth about October 7th. We will stand up to hate, wherever it rears its ugly head.
And we will never stop fighting for a day when Hamas has laid down its arms for good, and Israelis and Palestinians alike can live in peace.
If we keep doing that, I know that here, in the greatest country in the world, antisemitism and hate will lose, and our best days will be ahead of us.
Thank you. God bless. And may God continue to bless and watch over the United States of America.
###

ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Local Community Members to Raise Alarm Over Marana Detention Facility
Marana, Arizona — Yesterday, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva joined local community members in Marana for a press conference addressing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s new contract with Management and Training Corporation (MTC) to open an immigration detention facility in Marana within the next 60 days.
The press conference brought together community members and local voices to raise concerns about the proposed facility and the record of MTC, the company contracted to operate it. MTC has previously operated correctional facilities in Arizona that faced allegations and documented concerns involving conditions including sexual abuse, inadequate food, extreme heat, and prison riots. The State of Arizona has terminated previous contracts with MTC under both Democratic and Republican governors.
Earlier this year, Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem. This comes after Rep. Grijalva wrote a letter demanding transparency on the proposed facility to then-Secretary Noem and joined community members earlier in the year at a press conference alongside Reps. Stanton and Ansari.
A copy of her remarks are below: 
“Buenas tardes. Thank you to PRICE for organizing this press conference.
We’re here today because DHS is once again rushing to open another private detention facility in Arizona.
Eso no está bien. Nuestra comunidad merece respuestas.
This is happening as deaths in ICE custody reach record levels – and as the agency fails to provide even the most basic care for the people already in its custody.
Just today, I learned about another disease outbreak - this time at a facility in Eloy.
Yet instead of addressing these conditions, this Administration is marching full steam ahead to fuel its cruel mass-deportation agenda.
And there is another reason we should be deeply concerned about this particular facility: Management & Training Corporation, or MTC, has a long and documented history of serious problems at facilities it has operated.
Here in Arizona, that history includes allegations of sexual abuse that were not properly reported, chronic understaffing and inadequate training, major security failures, and destructive prison riots.
In 2010, three inmates escaped from an MTC-operated prison in Kingman due to serious security failures.
While on the run, two of the escapees brutally murdered an elderly couple in New Mexico, leading to a large wrongful death settlement between the state of Arizona and the victims’ family.
Five years later, after riots at the same prison, an investigation found a “culture of disorganization, disengagement, and disregard.”
Those aren’t my words. Those are the findings that led Republican Governor Doug Ducey to terminate the state’s contract with MTC.
In 2017, at an MTC-operated ICE Processing Center in New Mexico, the DHS Office of the Inspector General raised concerns about the treatment and care of detainees.
Two people detained there died after pleading for medical help from facility staff.
This is the company the federal government is entrusting with the lives of hundreds of people here in Marana.
And they are moving fast. MTC says it plans to have this facility up and running within 60 days of signing its contract with ICE.
Sixty days.
That should alarm every person in this community, especially when there are still so many unanswered questions.
First and foremost: How many people are actually going to be held here?
A document earlier this year suggested more than 1,300, but the contract MTC signed says up to 775. Both of these numbers are significantly above the 513-bed capacity the state prison previously operated under.
Regardless of what the final number is, one thing is abundantly clear: local residents do not want this facility.
La gente de Marana merece tener voz.
Since President Trump returned to office, at least 56 people have died in ICE custody, including four in Arizona.
And now the federal government has awarded MTC a contract with a potential value of more than $355 million to operate this facility.
That is a drop in the bucket of the nearly $261 BILLION Congress has approved for immigration enforcement under Trump.
Our communities are tired of our taxpayer dollars being wasted on these private detention centers to meet arbitrary deportation quotas.
We are tired of seeing private companies profit off Trump’s cruel and inhumane immigration agenda.
No queremos más dinero para compañías privadas
While the federal government operates in secrecy, local residents and their elected officials across the country are pushing back against these facilities, using zoning, public nuisance laws, and other means.
MTC’s history of poorly-run facilities, combined with the track-record of abuses at DHS, underscore the concerns of Marana residents.
Unfortunately, the responsibility of oversight has fallen on local governments because the federal government is willfully asleep at the wheel.
We will continue asking questions.
We will continue demanding accountability.
And we will continue fighting to ensure that the people of Marana have a voice in what happens in their own community.
Vamos a seguir luchando por nuestra comunidad.
Thank you. Muchas gracias.”
###
title: ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Local Community Members to Raise Alarm Over Marana Detention Facility

Comisionado Residente solicita nuevas respuestas tras revisar documentos sobre contrato de generación temporera
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó nueva información y documentación sobre el proceso de adquisición y contratación de generación temporera adjudicado al consorcio encabezado por Power Expectations, LLC, tras identificar interrogantes en los documentos producidos al Congreso sobre la investigación y el manejo de alegaciones surgidas durante el proceso competitivo.
En una carta dirigida al Zar de Energía, Josué Colón Ortiz, y al presidente del Third Party Procurement Office (3PPO), Osvaldo Carlo Linares, el Comisionado Residente solicita información para esclarecer qué se investigó sobre la alegada firma no autorizada de Enchanted Rock, quién realizó esa revisión, con qué autoridad, y por qué transcurrieron casi más de siete semanas antes de referir el asunto a las autoridades competentes.
La gestión da seguimiento a una carta enviada por el Comisionado Residente el 3 de septiembre. Tras examinar los informes, referidos y comunicaciones producidos al Congreso, su oficina identificó que un informe de 3PPO del 8 de agosto describió una “revisión exhaustiva” de las alegaciones, mientras que una comunicación enviada al día siguiente indicó que la revisión se había limitado a evaluar la suficiencia de la documentación sometida durante el proceso competitivo.
“Desde nuestra primera solicitud hemos estado revisando cuidadosamente los documentos y siguiendo los hechos. La información que recibimos nos permitió avanzar, pero también levantó preguntas adicionales que ahora corresponde aclarar”, expresó el Comisionado Residente. “Queremos entender con precisión qué se revisó, qué se determinó y cómo se tomaron las decisiones durante este proceso.”
A partir de esa revisión, el Comisionado Residente identificó varias áreas que aún requieren aclaración y, en esta carta, busca precisar:
- El propósito y alcance de la revisión realizada por 3PPO y qué asuntos permanecían sin resolver.
- La cronología de las gestiones realizadas entre el 17 de junio y el 10 de agosto.
- Qué información y hallazgos existían cuando el asunto fue referido al Departamento de Justicia de Puerto Rico y a las autoridades federales.
- Cuándo fueron informadas la AEE y la Junta de Supervisión Fiscal, y cómo se tomaron las decisiones de informarles.
- Las comunicaciones y documentos internos relacionados con la revisión y el manejo de las alegaciones.
La información deberá ser entregada no más tarde del 15 de octubre de 2026.
“Estamos dando seguimiento a lo que surge de los propios documentos y vamos a continuar procurando las respuestas que aún están pendientes”, concluyó el Comisionado Residente.
###
title: Comisionado Residente solicita nuevas respuestas tras revisar documentos sobre contrato de generación temporera

MATSUI, DEGETTE, BEYER STATEMENT ON ILLEGAL IMPOUNDMENT OF HEALTH RESEARCH FUNDS
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representatives Doris Matsui (CA-07), Diana DeGette (CO-01), and Don Beyer (VA-08) released the following statement after the Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued a legal determination confirming the administration illegally impounded $78 million in Fiscal Year 2025 funding for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ). The decision comes more than a year after Reps. Matsui, DeGette, and Beyer sent the initial request for a nonpartisan legal opinion on the matter.
“The GAO’s decision today confirms what we have known for over a year: Donald Trump is stealing taxpayers’ dollars that Congress set aside to improve Americans’ health. The administration’s unilateral dismantling of the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality’s grantmaking operations is an illegal impoundment of Congressionally appropriated funds.
“Under Article I of the Constitution, the power of the purse rests strictly with Congress, not the executive branch. Trump’s administration cannot simply refuse to spend the resources we authorized for lifesaving health care research. Republicans must join Democrats in demanding that the Constitution is upheld.”
Background:
The Trump administration’s massive cuts at the Department of Health and Human Services beginning April 1, 2025, disrupted grant funding for health care research across the country, including in Colorado. AHRQ suffered particularly devastating impacts to its grants supporting more efficient, effective, and safe health care. Grantmaking at AHRQ halted: from April 1 to September 5, 2025, AHRQ did not issue a single grant. The agency would typically issue up to 73 grants during a comparable time period.
In September 2025, Representatives Matsui, DeGette, and Beyer sent a request to GAO for their legal opinion on whether disruptions of AHRQ’s grantmaking process represented illegal withholding of funds in violation of the Impoundment Control Act, which regulates the president’s ability to delay or withhold Congressionally appropriated spending. The GAO is often called the “Congressional watchdog” for its role in investigating federal government spending and performance.
Today, after a lengthy nonpartisan investigation, the GAO announced its findings that the Trump administration did illegally withhold—or impound—$78 million Congress directed to support healthcare research.
title: MATSUI, DEGETTE, BEYER STATEMENT ON ILLEGAL IMPOUNDMENT OF HEALTH RESEARCH FUNDS

U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Jahana Hayes (D-CT-05) introduced the Title IX Take Responsibility Act, legislation that would hold schools accountable for mishandling reports of sexual assault and provide survivors a stronger path towards justice.
The legislation amends Title IX, a U.S. federal civil rights law passed as part of the Education Amendments of 1972 that bans sex-based discrimination in any education program or activity receiving federal money. The bill would reform how schools handle sexual assault and harassment by replacing outdated legal loopholes with clear accountability.
"For far too long, outdated legal loopholes have allowed educational institutions to turn a blind eye to reports of sexual assault, leaving survivors without justice or support," said Congresswoman Dingell.
"Title IX was enacted to protect students, not to shield institutions from accountability when they fail to keep campuses safe. This bill closes these gaps and ensures that every student has access to a safe learning environment free from abuse."
"One incident of sexual violence is one too many," said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes.
"I am committed to protecting students, supporting survivors, and ensuring college campuses are safe learning environments for all. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act will put the responsibility on educational institutions for any mishandling of sexual assault reporting and failure to prevent further assaults. This legislation should be considered immediately, and I thank Congresswoman Dingell for partnering on this effort." 
Under current Supreme Court precedents, schools can only be held liable if high-level officials had "actual notice" and reacted with "deliberate indifference," creating an incentive for institutions to turn a blind eye. This bill eliminates that defense by holding schools legally responsible if they knew or reasonably should have known about the abuse and failed to take effective action. It also expands access to justice by allowing survivors to hold schools accountable in federal court for monetary damages and legal fees.
The legislation is endorsed by Volare, Ujima, End Rape on Campus, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence (NAESV), Just Solutions, YWCA, and the National Organization for Victim Advocacy (NOVA).
“Survivors should not have to sacrifice their education because an institution failed to respond meaningfully to sexual harassment or violence. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act strengthens survivors’ ability to enforce their rights and recognizes that students should be able to access meaningful support without being required to pursue an investigation. Survivors deserve options that protect their safety, well-being, and ability to continue their education,” said Volare CEO Bridgette Stumpf.
“YWCA USA is unwavering in our pursuit of a world where all women and girls can thrive. To meet that mission, it is essential that every student can learn in an environment free from sexual violence. Sadly, we know that violence does occur. The deeply disturbing reports from Cornell University underscore that passing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act is an essential and overdue step that would hold our educational institutions more responsible for protecting students from the start and accessing swift, meaningful pathways to justice and healing,”
 said Kate Kasper, VP of Public Policy and Advocacy, YWCA USA.
"Schools must take sexual misconduct more seriously. We're abandoning survivors and ignoring the enormous impact of sexual violence on their educational attainment, health, and quality of life. This is unacceptable. The National Alliance to End Sexual Violence applauds Representatives Dingell and Hayes for re-introducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. We must have more accountability,"
 said Monika Johnson-Hostler, President & CEO, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence.
“I’m grateful to Reps. Dingell and Hayes for reintroducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. At moment when the Dept of Education is rolling back protections under Title IX and leaving survivors of sexual violence vulnerable, this bill would strengthen protections and where appropriate, hold institutions accountable,”
 said Lisalyn Jacobs, CEO of Just Solutions.
“Survivors should never have to choose between their safety and their education. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act affirms survivors’ rights to support, to make their own choices about reporting, and to seek justice when their access to education is harmed. It also gives schools clear standards that reflect what effective, survivor-centered response looks like. NOVA strongly supports this bill,” said Claire Ponder Selib, Executive Director, National Organization for Victim Advocacy.
Bill text can be found HERE.
title: Dingell, Hayes Introduce Bill to Hold Schools Accountable for Mishandling Reports of Sexual Assault

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) released the fourth and final installment of $3.3 million in previously approved funding for the Disaster Case Management Program (DCMP), completing the release of federal funding previously awarded to support survivors of the January 2025 Eaton and Palisades Fires

On September 30, 2026, following sustained pressure from Reps. Chu and Sherman and Sens. Schiff and Padilla, FEMA released the second and third installments of DCMP funding, totaling $6.6 million, on the same day the program was set to face a major funding cliff.

Rep. Chu, who has led congressional efforts to secure federal disaster assistance, tax relief, and long-term recovery resources for Eaton Fire survivors, repeatedly pressed FEMA to release the outstanding DCMP funds. She has also urged FEMA to approve California’s separate request for supplemental funding needed to sustain the program and ensure survivors can continue receiving case management services.

Rep. Chu released the following statement:

“I am relieved that FEMA has finally released the full amount of previously approved funding for the DCMP. This money was already approved and set aside for survivors. There was no reason to withhold it and jeopardize critical recovery resources for thousands. Now, Californians can keep getting help navigating temporary housing and loan assistance without fear of being left to fend for themselves mid-process. And hundreds of case managers can keep supporting survivors without worrying about losing their jobs. However, FEMA must do the right thing and approve the State of California’s appeal for additional supplemental funding to sustain DCMP through the full 24-month timeframe that FEMA itself approved.

Further, President Trump must still fully fund Governor Newsom’s disaster supplemental request with no strings attached so our communities get the full federal recovery support they have waited far too long to receive. I will keep fighting until every survivor gets every dollar they are owed to rebuild and recover.”
title: Rep. Chu Commends FEMA Release of Final Installment of Wildfire Survivor Case Management Funding

Last Friday, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) commented on the news that Canada is fast-tracking a new oil pipeline project that would increase oil tanker traffic in Larsen’s district: 
“This project is not ready for prime time, and speeding up the review process will only make that worse,” said Rep. Larsen in the Washington State Standard. “Canada’s plan to fast track this new oil pipeline project puts sensitive marine habitats at risk and raises the chance of a devastating spill occurring before the U.S. and Canada can put updated plans in place.” 
On July 2, the Government of Alberta announced a proposed new oil pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific Ocean that would transport 1 million barrels per day to an export terminal at Roberts Banks in British Columbia. Last Thursday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney designated the pipeline, now known as the Pacific Link, as a project of national interest, enabling a speedier regulatory review that could see pipeline design and construction underway by next fall. The new pipeline will increase tanker traffic in Haro Strait and Boundary Bay in the Salish Sea, and with it the risks for catastrophic oil spills impacting sensitive marine environments.  
“The people I represent have serious concerns about this new pipeline and how it could harm the Salish Sea,” continued Rep. Larsen. “They deserve answers to their questions and updated spill response plans that account for more oil tanker traffic, and I will keep fighting to get them both." 
Last month, Rep. Larsen’s staff observed a joint exercise between the U.S. Coast Guard and the Canadian Coast Guard designed to simulate response efforts and coordination between the two countries in the event of an oil spill in shared waters. 
“This type of collaboration across the border between the U.S. and Canada is even more critical because of Canada’s plans to ship more oil in the Salish Sea with the proposed new Alberta to B.C. pipeline,” said Rep. Larsen. “I have concerns about the potential impacts of this proposed pipeline, including on tanker traffic in the Salish Sea, and I am glad that my staff could observe the exercise to ensure that there are relationships and procedures in place that benefit both countries in the event of a disastrous spill.” 
Rep. Larsen is the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, which has oversight authority over the U.S. Coast Guard. In July, Rep. Larsen sent a letter to Admiral Kevin E. Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard, to insist that the Coast Guard review and update its oil spill preparedness plans in light of the new proposed pipeline. Larsen also pressed Coast Guard officials on their awareness of the new Canadian pipeline and how it would implicate existing oil spill prevention plans at a committee hearing. A video clip from that hearing can be found here, and the recording of the entire roundtable can be found here. 
The Washington State Standard article is available here and below.  
A proposed Canadian oil pipeline to a supertanker terminal at the Port of Vancouver in British Columbia is raising hackles among Washington state’s political leaders.  
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday designated the West Coast Oil Pipeline, now known as the Pacific Link, as a project of national interest. That enables a speedier regulatory review that could see pipeline design and construction under way by next fall. 
In response, Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson on Friday sounded alarms about increased oil spill risk to the Salish Sea in his first public comments on the massive project. 
It would run from the Edmonton region to a new export terminal capable of handling supertankers proposed for Port of Vancouver’s Roberts Bank in British Columbia just north of the U.S. border. Oil could flow through by the early 2030s. 
Once operating, many more oil-filled vessels traveling from the port would pass by the San Juan Islands and Olympic Peninsula on their way to Asia. Project critics fear a spill could easily reach north Puget Sound, the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Washington’s outer coast, threatening sensitive ecosystems and killer whale habitat.  
Ferguson said Friday that he was “disappointed” at the decision because resources needed to respond to a major spill are insufficient today. 
“If a project of this scale is going to proceed, it needs to come with a corresponding commitment to also increase our region’s capacity to prevent and respond to a catastrophic spill,” he said in a joint statement with Casey Sixkiller, director of the state Department of Ecology. 
“If this project proceeds, it is critical that the Canadian government make detailed commitments to safeguard our shared marine waters and fill these gaps in our response capabilities,” he and Sixkiller said in the statement. 
San Juan County council members, northern Washington tribal representatives and others have been pushing Ferguson since July to speak out and engage with the Canadian provincial and federal governments about the crude pipeline and tanker traffic. 
On Tuesday, Ferguson met with Mark Wiseman, Canada’s ambassador to the U.S. in Seattle. It is not known if the two discussed the pipeline and Ferguson’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the meeting. 
Sixkiller dispatched a lengthy letter to Canadian Intergovernmental Affairs Minister Dominic LeBlanc in mid-September in a vain bid to forestall the fast-tracking of the Alberta pipeline permitting. 
U.S. Rep. Rick Larsen of Everett, whose 2nd Congressional District includes the state waters through which the supertankers would travel, was equally vexed. Many questions about the project and oil spill response need answers, he said. 
“This project is not ready for prime time, and speeding up the review process will only make that worse,” he said in an email. “Canada’s plan to fast track this new oil pipeline project puts sensitive marine habitats at risk and raises the chance of a devastating spill occurring before the U.S. and Canada can put updated plans in place.” 
The project comes as Canada looks to strengthen its economic ties beyond the U.S. and as Carney has said the nation is seeking to become an “energy superpower.” 
Smith has said the province chose a southern pipeline route that ends on the shores of the Salish Sea because it can take advantage of the existing Trans Mountain Pipeline corridor as well as established relationships with First Nations. 
Northern Washington tribes, including the Lummi, Samish, Swinomish and Makah, strongly opposed a previous Canadian pipeline expansion. The tribes argue that the large increase in vessel traffic endangers their treaty rights and threatens vital fisheries. 
Maithili Devadas of the Georgia Strait Alliance, an environmental group in British Columbia fighting the export terminal proposed at Roberts Bank, panned Carney’s announcement. 
“It would be reasonable to expect that a project with the potential to shape the environmental, economic, and social future of a region for decades to come would face an especially rigorous level of scrutiny. Instead, this project is being fast-tracked without any concern for its long-term impacts on ecosystems, communities and the people who depend on them,” she wrote in an update to supporters Friday.
title: Larsen: New B.C. Oil Pipeline is “Not Ready for Prime Time”

text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, released a discussion draft of the Clear Liability for Artificial Intelligence Misconduct (CLAIM) Act. The legislation would give those harmed by AI agents a clear path to recovery by holding developers responsible when their systems engage in conduct that would be unlawful if committed by a person.
 
“When someone breaks the law and hurts you, you can take them to court. That shouldn't change just because the wrongdoer is an AI agent,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “Developers have already built systems capable of acting on their own and causing real damage. The CLAIM Act makes sure they answer for what their systems do.”
Specifically, the CLAIM Act:
    - Holds developers liable for AI misconduct. If an AI system injures a third party through conduct that would constitute negligence, an intentional tort, or a crime if committed by a person, the developer is liable. Liability does not apply where the user or a company that modified the system intended the conduct or was negligent.
- Resolves uncertainty around AI and intent. Courts would presume an AI system acted with the state of mind a person taking the same actions would have had. Developers could not argue that AI is incapable of intent.
- Establishes a federal cause of action. Injured parties may bring claims in federal or state court.
- Preserves state law. The bill sets a federal floor and does not preempt any state law. Existing state claims and state AI laws remain fully available.
The risks the CLAIM Act addresses already exist. In July, AI agents undergoing an evaluation by OpenAI escaped their test environment and hacked into Hugging Face, another AI company. No one instructed them to do so. Leading experts have called the incident a warning shot for a future of increasingly capable AI agents acting outside their users’ control.
Under current law, third parties harmed by a misaligned AI agent face significant hurdles. Many serious harms, including hacking and fraud, require proof of intent, and courts have not settled whether an AI system’s conduct can meet that standard. Negligence and product liability claims typically require showing that a company failed to take a specific precaution or ignored a safer design. Because AI alignment remains an unsolved technical problem, developers can argue the harm occurred despite their best efforts, leaving injured parties without a remedy.
The CLAIM Act complements the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which Trahan introduced with Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) to address catastrophic risks from the most advanced AI models. FRONTIER establishes transparency, independent verification, and incident reporting requirements. The CLAIM Act adds a robust liability regime that rewards developers who invest in making their systems safer.
Trahan is releasing the CLAIM Act as a discussion draft and welcomes feedback from experts, industry, advocates, and the public. In addition to comments on the draft legislation, the office welcomes answers to important questions related to the CLAIM Act and AI liability located HERE.
Comments can be submitted to MA03Leg@mail.house.gov.
A copy of the bill text can be accessed HERE.
A one-pager is available HERE.
title: Trahan Unveils CLAIM Act Discussion Draft to Hold AI Developers Accountable for Harms Caused by Their Agents

MATSUI, SACRAMENTO COUNTY ANNOUNCE $1 MILLION IN FEDERAL FUNDING FOR FLORIN ROAD SAFE STAY COMMUNITY
SACRAMENTO, CA — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) held a press conference with Sacramento County leaders and Five Keys to announce $1 million in federal funding for the Florin Road Safe Stay Community.
The federal investment will support the installation of modular sanitation facilities to replace the site’s current mobile units, as well as the creation of permanent outdoor gathering space for guests and their pets. These improvements will help strengthen day-to-day operations and make the site more stable, functional, and supportive for the people it serves.
“This investment will build real restrooms and showers to replace temporary ones and create permanent outdoor space where folks can spend time together,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “Clean, reliable restrooms are a matter of basic dignity, and they keep people healthy. A place to sit outside with a neighbor or a case manager is where trust starts. And trust is what gets someone to say yes to the next step.”
Sacramento County’s latest point-in-time count found more than 7,400 people experiencing homelessness, while also showing more people in shelters than ever before. The Florin Road Safe Stay Community opened three years ago and provides private cabins, meals, showers, laundry, pet accommodations and on-site case management to help people experiencing homelessness move toward permanent housing.
“This infusion of critical funding comes at a pivotal moment in Sacramento County’s mission to continue its success in addressing homelessness in impactful and unique ways,” said District 2 Sacramento County Supervisor Patrick Kennedy. “We’re grateful to Congresswoman Matsui’s tenacity in working for Sacramento, working for the important work of addressing homelessness when funding is rapidly dwindling and we’re grateful for her continued advocacy in Washington.”
“At Florin Safe Stay, we are providing people with something critically important: a safe place to begin again,” said Heather Calomese, president and CEO of Five Keys. “But shelter is not the finish line. It is a bridge from the street to safety, from crisis to stability, and ultimately, from homelessness to a place to call home. Every person who walks through our doors deserves to be treated with dignity, to be seen and to have a real pathway forward.”
The Florin Road Safe Stay Community is operated by Five Keys in partnership with Sacramento County. The $1 million in federal funding is part of Matsui’s ongoing work to deliver federal resources directly to Sacramento-area projects that address local needs.

ICYMI: Congressman Pat Ryan Hosts Hudson Valley Restaurant Owners for Discussion on Rising Costs & Impacts of Proposed Sysco-Restaurant Depot Merger
Mid Hudson News: Ryan and restaurant owners dish on Sysco at diner
Ryan hosted Hudson Valley restaurant owners, caterers, and small food distributors to discuss how corporate consolidation is raising prices and making it harder to run their small businesses
The discussion comes after Ryan called on FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson to block the proposed $29.1 billion merger between Sysco and Restaurant Depot, arguing the merger would reduce competition, drive up operating costs for restaurants, and make dining out more expensive
NEWBURGH, NY – Yesterday, Congressman Pat Ryan – co-chair of the Congressional Monopoly Busters Caucus – hosted a roundtable conversation at Alexis Diner with Hudson Valley restaurant owners, caterers, and small food distributors to discuss how corporate consolidation is raising prices and making it harder to run their small businesses.
Participants discussed how the proposed merger between Sysco and Restaurant Depot – two of the largest suppliers Hudson Valley independent restaurants rely on – would bring a dramatic, negative impact to their businesses.
The conversation followed a letter Ryan sent to Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chairman Andrew Ferguson last week, demanding the FTC block the proposed $29.1 billion merger and raising the alarm on how it would reduce competition, drive up operating costs for restaurants, and make dining out in the Hudson Valley more expensive.
“When the largest food distributor in the country seeks to acquire one of its biggest competitors, it’s all of us – our small restaurant and diner owners, food truck operators, caterers, and customers – who will be forced to pay the higher price,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Hudson Valley restaurants are part of what makes our community so special. We should be making it easier, not harder, for them to succeed. Keeping prices competitive is essential to the success of these restaurants, which is why we’re going to fight with everything we’ve got to make sure the FTC blocks this harmful deal and protects the independent businesses that keep our Hudson Valley communities thriving.”
“We're grateful that Congressman Ryan is standing with independent restaurants and bars by urging the FTC to fully investigate the proposed merger between Sysco and Restaurant Depot,” said Erika Polmar, Executive Director of the Independent Restaurant Coalition. “Restaurants already operate on margins of just 3 to 5 percent, and when one company controls more of the food supply chain, owners lose bargaining power and are left with higher prices, fewer options and lousy terms, costs that either land on the menu or eat into already meager margins. Restaurants are New York's second-largest private employer, and letting Sysco absorb the supplier independents rely on most would threaten the neighborhood businesses that anchor communities across the state.”
Read more:
Mid Hudson News: Ryan and restaurant owners dish on Sysco at diner
By Jeanine Agnolet
TOWN OF NEWBURGH – A handful of small, independent restaurant owners, food educators, chefs and a farmer sat around a table at the Alexis Diner in Newburgh on Monday to express their concerns to Congressman Pat Ryan (D, NY -18) about the proposed merger of the food industry giant Sysco Corporation and Restaurant Depot.
Above the frenetic sounds of a hectic lunch crowd with plenty of hot coffee, they candidly described what they said was the disaster that will strike if Sysco is successful in acquiring Restaurant Depot, which has a warehouse in the Town of Newburgh.
“The merger will drive the food prices up, and it will drive small restaurants right out of business,” said Tom Costa, chef and owner of North Plank Road Tavern in the Town of Newburgh and an active member of the Independent Restaurant Coalition. “Right now, I can run out to Restaurant Depot, and I can get three pounds of Faroe Island salmon, but if I have to order a case of it from Sysco, I risk losing some of it before I actually sell it. Restaurant Depot is a godsend for the small, independent restaurant, which is a dying breed.”
Congressman Ryan held the roundtable discussion to get feedback from local restaurant owners and food service providers.
Last Friday, Ryan, who co-chairs the Congressional Monopoly Busters Caucus, sent a letter to Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, urging him to block the proposed $29.1 billion merger.
Ryan says the appeal to prevent the acquisition has bipartisan support.
“I cannot overstate how big of a deal this is as one of the biggest mergers in this country in the past decade,” said Ryan. “At a time when costs are already exorbitantly high, this is incredibly problematic.”
Ryan said there are nearly 2,000 food service and accommodation businesses in his district, most of them with less than 20 employees.
“There are over 30 thousand food workers in these three counties—a huge source of employment across our communities, so this affects everyone,” said Ryan.
Sysco is the single biggest distributor of food in the nation, serving over 700,000 customers globally, including schools, hospital systems and other organizations that have high volume.
Earlier this year, it announced plans to purchase Restaurant Depot, one of the nation’s largest food wholesale cash-and-carry warehouse companies, that sells to independent restaurant owners, caterers and non-profits.
Restaurant owners contend the proposed merger would reduce competition, drive up operating costs and make dining out more expensive.
Rei Peraza, director of Operations and Executive Chef for Rossi & Sons, prides himself on the fact that he has never utilized Sysco.
“Sysco has an algorithmic pricing system. The more you buy, the better your pricing is, and that’s why it doesn’t work for a lot of small, mom and pop operations. I don’t think Sysco and the way they do business has ever been good for small businesses,” said Peraza.
With Sysco, the identities of restaurants get lost. You’re using the same chicken fingers and the same toilet paper as everyone else. As a whole, they have very little to offer in quality products outside of convenience.”
In 2013, Sysco attempted to acquire US Foods, but the Federal Trade Commission sued to block the merger and won.
Assemblyman Jonathan Jacobsen says he intends draft a letter to State Attorney General Letitia James, urging her to take action and enforce the current laws that prohibit monopolistic practices.
“It’s wrong in the insurance, healthcare and pharmaceutical industries, and it’s wrong here,” said Jacobsen.
“With this merger, we’ll be out priced, and this will be catastrophic,” said Gaby Pereyra, owner of Yara Farm in Middletown, New York and director of Operations for the Chester Agricultural Center. “It would be impossible for small farmers to be able to sell to small restaurants or suppliers.”
Ryan says he is hopeful that the merger can still be stopped, despite the fact that negotiations are in the final stages.
“Sysco has a pricing structure based on volume,” said Tom Costa. “It may be smart but it’s going to kill the little guy.”
Ryan’s letter to FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson is included in full below, and can be viewed here.
Dear Chairman Ferguson,
I am writing to urge the Federal Trade Commission to conduct a rigorous review of Sysco Corporation's proposed acquisition of Restaurant Depot, and to formally oppose the merger unless substantial evidence is shown that the merger will not lessen competition in the markets on which independent restaurants and small food service operators rely. This issue is of personal interest as many of my constituents rely on the Restaurant Depot Warehouse located in my district in Newburgh, New York. In addition, as independent restaurants are forced to raise prices, those high prices are either absorbed, decreasing profits, or passed along to consumers. My constituents are already drowning in skyrocketing prices, and this acquisition will only make it more difficult both for small businesses working hard to make a living and for customers trying to afford the basics, like a warm meal from a local restaurant.
Restaurant Depot exerts indirect but consequential competitive pressure on Sysco by serving as an outside option for independent, price-sensitive operators who want to avoid rising delivery fees. Independent restaurant operators, including the 30,000 restaurant workers in my district, depend on low-cost product sourcing to operate. While Sysco has defended the acquisition, characterizing the two companies as possessing “minimal overlap” in customers, the truth is that this acquisition would establish Sysco’s total control over two unique channels of distribution that independent restaurants have historically used as substitutes for each other.
This acquisition would make Sysco the largest player in the cash-and-carry market, on top of its existing leadership in the broadline distribution market. This consolidation of market power will have severe and devastating consequences for independent restaurants, food service operators, and other small businesses who rely on competitive markets to keep prices low for their customers. With folks feeling intense financial pressure across the board right now, we should be working together to bring down costs, instead of fueling high prices. I’ll continue to stay in close contact with local businesses negatively impacted by rising prices and help them fight for fair practices.
As you look into the details of the merger, I urge the Federal Trade Commission to closely review the potential impact on the food service industry, including the small businesses and consumers who patronize our beloved independent restaurants.
On behalf of the hardworking independent restaurants and constituents who would be impacted by this merger in my district and around the nation, I urge the Commission to investigate this matter and take decisive action to protect competition, consumers, and small businesses.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04), member of the House Foreign Affairs and Appropriations Committees, released the following statement on the third anniversary of the October 7th attack:
“Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists launched a brutal, barbaric — most inhumane — attack on the people of Israel. Homes, Kibbutzim, and families were burned. Families torn apart. Unspeakable crimes committed against women, children, and seniors. More than 1,200 people were killed and 250 taken hostage, including American citizens.
The cruelty and brutality of this attack demanded universal, international condemnation and American support for our ally and friend Israel.
I have traveled to Israel several times since October 7th, to meet with grieving Israeli families and government leaders. I met twice with Prime Minister Netanyahu, urging him to pursue justice — a just war — not vengeance, to be a partner for peace.
Today, thanks to the tireless advocacy from the families and to American leadership, all the living hostages have been reunited with their loved ones. The dead have been returned to be buried with dignity. Around the world, Jewish people just celebrated their first Rosh Hashanah without any hostages held in Hamas’ custody. But the scars of October 7th run deep and are lasting. The families of those who were killed, and those who were taken, will carry that grief for the rest of their lives. We all will.
Meanwhile, the region remains in turmoil. Millions of Gazans are still displaced and vulnerable, struggling to find the food, water, medicine, and shelter they need to survive. More than 70,000 innocent Palestinian civilians have been killed and thousands more wounded, so many of them children. and Israeli violations of the ceasefire are alarmingly common. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers continue to encroach on Palestinian land, using violence to injure, kill, and drive out Palestinian families, jeopardizing any chance at peace.
We owe it to all those who died, on that day and in the devastating war since, to build a better future.
My prayer, and my work as a member of Congress, remains focused on supporting these essential pillars of peace: disarming of Hamas, a durable ceasefire to enable the mass distribution of humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza; a safe and secure future for Israel as a democratic home for the Jewish people; self-determination and dignity for the Palestinian people to rebuild their lives and create a democratic, sovereign state of their own; and a commitment by leaders around the world to these principles, that we might truly end the cycle of violence.
In this work, I am guided by the Jewish teaching of “Tikkun Olam”— the call to repair the world — and by the Scripture which tells us: blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
Today, we remember the suffering of October 7th. Tomorrow, we must continue the work, with mercy and moral clarity, each doing our part to make peace.”
Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.

SAN BRUNO, CA –Despite bipartisan and bicameral support for preserving America’s national archives, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) gave a dismissive response to federal lawmakers who are working to protect local public access to historic records.
Before providing any justification or opportunities for the public to weigh in, NARA recently announced it would be closing its San Bruno and Chicago facilities, which are two of just 13 regional archives across America. Over one hundred community advocates, researchers, genealogists, and local families gathered at a rally and press conference Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) hosted in August to emphasize the importance of retaining culturally and historically significant records in the Bay Area.
U.S. Reps. Mullin and Judy Chu (CA-28) led a bipartisan coalition of 37 federal lawmakers in writing to NARA response letter, NARA failed to fully acknowledge concerns about the public losing physical access to local archival records, or a 2009 agreement to keep regionally-sensitive immigration files in San Bruno. NARA also did not explain how it made decisions about where to transfer non-immigration related files, and provided no insight into how the fragile 100+ year-old records would be cared for while moved across the country.
NARA didn’t definitively answer questions about the future of its local workforce, many of whom are experts in their field. While it cited an estimated $4.7 million in annual savings by shuttering the building, it didn’t justify the need to find such savings – which is less than the taxpayer funding President Trump wants to spend on renovating his living quarters at the White House this fiscal year alone.
The national archives in San Bruno house records from not only California but also Nevada, Hawaii, Pacific Island territories, and Tribes. These records hold deep value to the local community including Angel Island immigration files, Chinese Exclusion Act and Japanese Internment records, Native American and indigenous history documents, and even the notable Wong Kim Ark files, on which the recent birthright citizenship case at the Supreme Court hinged. NARA said it plans to move the immigration files to Kansas City – suggesting it expects Bay Area community members who deeply care about their ancestors’ records to travel over 1,500 miles if they want see them in person.
In August, Rep. Mullin also introduced the National Archives Protection Act, which is co-authored by Reps. Chu; Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), whose district includes the Seattle archives; and Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), whose district includes the Chicago archives. The bill would prevent NARA from closing any of its facilities including archives, records centers, and research rooms, without Congressional approval. Following the House bill, a Senate companion version was introduced on Sept. 30 by Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), along with U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Alex Padilla (D-CA), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).
After facing community pushback – and months after quietly notifying congressional offices of its plans – NARA announced it would host two virtual listening sessions for Tribal Nations on Oct. 13 and 15. Reps. Mullin and Chu encourage all Tribal members interested in joining to visit NARA’s website for instructions on signing up for a listening session at www.archives.gov/research/news. Reps. Mullin and Chu are urging NARA to conduct more public input sessions and engage with additional stakeholders who have an interest in maintaining the physical archives within the communities they represent.
“NARA’s response to federal lawmakers is extremely disappointing and dismissive toward the sincere concerns from the public about losing direct access to irreplaceable community and family records. These archives aren’t just boxes of paper — they hold the stories, memories, and history of generations of Americans. Families whose ancestors immigrated through Angel Island can track their lineage, those whose loved ones served in the Navy and were stationed in the Pacific can learn about their legacy, and Native Americans whose history is documented over generations are all able to learn more by visiting this national archive,” said Rep. Mullin. “NARA has a responsibility to ensure these tangible records are carefully preserved and accessible to the people they represent. I will continue to fight against these closures and encourage everyone – from federal lawmakers and Tribal leaders, to community advocates and researchers – to keep up the pressure and consider all legal means to protect these historic resources.”
“NARA’s response falls far short of addressing the real concerns of the communities who rely on these archives,” said Rep. Judy Chu. “For all Californians, and particularly the AANHPI community, these records are more than files and boxes. They tell the stories of families who endured the Chinese Exclusion Act and the incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II, and they are where descendants go to learn what their loved ones lived through. Moving these records across the country would force families to travel thousands of miles and spend significant time and money simply to access their own American history. NARA has offered no convincing reason to put that history out of reach, and it has a responsibility to protect these records and keep them accessible to the communities they belong to. We will keep fighting the closures of the San Francisco and San Bruno facilities, and we will not let up until these irreplaceable pieces of AANHPI history are kept with the communities whose stories they tell.”
The letter regarding the San Bruno archives was signed by U.S. Reps. Mark Amodei (NV-02), Ami Bera (CA-06), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Ed Case (HI-01), Judy Chu (CA-28), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), , Laura Friedman (CA-30), John Garamendi (CA-08), Jesús García (IL-04), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Steven Horsford (NV-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Susie Lee (NV-03), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Doris Matsui (CA-17), Grace Meng (NY-06), Dave Min (CA-47), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Brad Sherman (CA-32), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-29), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Dina Titus (NV-01), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Norma Torres (CA-35), Maxine Waters (CA-43); and Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam B. Schiff (D-CA), Jacklyn Rosen (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL).

Examining Webull's China Links
A new bipartisan investigation by the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, led by Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) and Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI), finds that stock brokerage Webull Financial has not been transparent about its links to China. In addition to finding that the company’s practices exposed American investors’ data to surveillance risks in China, the investigation also documents how the company is controlled by China-linked executives and its China-based subsidiary receives subsidies and cash rewards from Chinese government authorities.
“Whether it’s this trading app or other brokerage apps, custodians of Americans’ financial data and savings should strive for transparency with the customers they serve. Webull should be forthright about its connections to the PRC, rather than seemingly seeking to minimize them,” said Ranking Member Khanna.”
"Webull’s China-based operations put American investors and their data at risk. China’s national security law compels all Chinese citizens to comply with demands for information from the CCP, and a stock brokerage storing data in China is no different,” said Chairman Moolenaar. "Using technology providers in mainland China and an opaque China-linked ownership structure, Webull exposes its data to our foremost adversary. Investors should heed this information when choosing who they do business with.”\
The report titled, Free Trades, Hidden Ties: Exposing Webull’s China Links, makes six findings:
- Webull’s data practices expose American investors to PRC legal and surveillance risk.
- Webull misrepresented where key employees worked and how they were supervised.
- Webull’s governance is dominated by PRC-linked control.
- Webull’s regulatory controls were weaker than its assurances suggested.
- Webull’s subsidiary accepted PRC government funding conditional on CCP loyalty while its affiliates expanded in China.
- Webull’s clearing and custody safeguards are concerning.
Policy Recommendations
The investigation also makes five policy recommendations as a result of its findings:
- Codify the Securities and Exchange Commission Cross-Border Task Force.
- Enact Inspectability Requirements for Broker-Dealer Operations — a Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act for Broker-Dealers.
- Create Foreign-Adversary Data Protections for Brokerage Records.
- Regulate Conflicted Clearing and Self-Custody Arrangements.
- Bring Foreign-Controlled Broker-Dealers Within Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) Jurisdiction.
Background
Webull is a stock trading platform that operates in the U.S. and purports to be an ordinary American broker-dealer; in reality, Webull's corporate and technology framework is tied directly to China, and the company has routinely distorted the facts about its personnel and operations.
In 2024, Moolenaar and then-Ranking Member Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) sent a letter to Webull regarding Webull's troubling ties to the PRC and the risks those ties may pose to the security of American user data.
In the 2024 letter, the lawmakers described that while operating in the United States, Webull has retained close ties to a network of Chinese technology companies, particularly Fumi Technology and Hunan Weibu. Webull has not only entered technology-sharing agreements with these companies, but also shares personnel with them. Additionally, Webull entities enjoy grants from the Chinese Communist Party that flow through Webull's Chinese sister company, Hunan Weibu, intended to support Webull's operations abroad. The lawmakers expressed that these entities, and related links to the Chinese Communist Party, raise concerns about Webull’s independence, the security of U.S. investor data, and its ability to comply with U.S. financial regulations.
Read the full report HERE.

title: Examining Webull's China Links
