Aurora Sentinel: Rep. Crow introduces bill to extend TPS protections for Ukrainian immigrants
AURORA | Aurora Democratic Congressperson Jason Crow is behind a House bill that would extend through 2029 temporary immigration protections for Ukrainian nationals living in the United States.
Crow’s bill would extend Temporary Protected Status, or TPS, for Ukrainians currently in the U.S. The protections are scheduled to expire Oct. 19, 2026, according to a press statement from Crow.
“Russia continues its illegal and unprovoked attacks on Ukraine,” Crow said in a statement. “America must continue to stand with the people of Ukraine.” The legislation would make the extension part of federal law rather than leaving the protections subject to presidential action, the release said.
President Donald Trump and his administration has created intense worry and consternation among immigrants living in the United States and benefiting from TPS protections.
“I think that TPS should be a part of a long overdue comprehensive immigration reform by Congress but until then, we owe it to those who are in the country under TPS to extend their status,” Aurora Mayor Mike Coffman said in a statement. “It would be heartless to force the Ukrainians back into a war zone. So I applaud Congressman Crow’s efforts to extend their status, although having been a member of Congress for 10 years, I know how difficult it will be to pass and… to have President Trump sign it into law when he already has the authority to extend it, unilaterally, without Congressional approval. “
On Sept. 9, Trump let expire TPS protections for hundreds of thousands of immigrations, primarily from Venezuela and El Salvador. The Supreme Court earlier this year ruled that, under current U.S. law, the president has authority to end TPS protections for protected groups without justification.
TPS allows nationals of designated countries experiencing armed conflict, natural disasters or other extraordinary conditions to remain temporarily in the United States and obtain work authorization. The program requires recipients to undergo screening, according to the release.
Crow introduced the bill with representatives Bill Keating, D-Mass., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa. In the Senate, the legislation was introduced by senators Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska; Chris Coons, D-Del.; and Bill Cassidy, R-La.
Crow serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Armed Services Committee, according to the release.
He has been a supporter of U.S. assistance to Ukraine since before Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022. Crow traveled to Kyiv in December 2021 and later advocated for U.S. military and humanitarian assistance to Ukraine, according to his office.
The legislation would apply to Ukrainian nationals already covered by TPS and extend their protections through June 2029.
The measure does not address another TPS warranty, covering immigrants from Sudan, also set to expire Oct. 19.
Colorado is home to about 17,000-18,000 Ukrainian immigrants, according to the U.S. Census records. The Aurora-Denver metro area is home to as many as about 5,000 of those immigrants, according to Census records.
Temporary legal protections for about 200,000 immigrants from El Salvador — including more than 4,000 in Aurora — was in limbo Wednesday as a deadline neared for the Trump administration to decide if they should end, as it has done for hundreds of thousands from Venezuela, Haiti and other countries.
The Temporary Protected Status designation expired in September, but the statute does not give a specific time for when that happens. If the Department of Homeland Security takes no action, protections are automatically extended for six months. This rare reprieve happened in May, when the protections were automatically extended to about 11,000 Lebanese, allowing them to stay and work in the U.S. for another 180 days.
DHS said in a statement in early September that it will announce a decision on El Salvador “at the appropriate time” and that protections would remain in place until then.
The push against Salvadoran immigrants drew a rebuke from Coffman, a Republican.
“I fully support the Trump administration’s successful effort at controlling our borders to combat illegal immigration,” Coffman said earlier this year in a social media post. “But this is not a question about illegal immigration because the Salvadorans, living in Aurora under TPS, came here legally and have had children and even grandchildren here, own homes in our city, and have not only started but expanded small businesses here.”
About 200,000 people from El Salvador have lived in the U.S. since 2001 under TPS, which allows people already in the country to remain with work permits for renewable periods of up to 18 months, if the secretary of homeland security determines conditions are unsafe for return. They are eligible for work permits.
Crow agreed with Coffman at the time that the situation of the El Salvadoran immigrants and refugees stands apart.
“Immigrants and asylum seekers who come here legally – including through Temporary Protected Status – work, pay taxes, and contribute greatly to Colorado,” Crow said. “It’s important for Coloradans to remember how we got here. President Trump and Republicans cut healthcare and food assistance to give tax breaks to billionaires and hire thousands of poorly trained ICE agents. Their aggressive immigration tactics and mass deportations have hurt our economy, terrorized our communities, and separated families. Coloradans deserve a secure border, an orderly asylum process for those fleeing violence, and a path for workers, families, and children to earn citizenship.”
During President Donald Trump’s second term, Homeland Security has ended TPS for more than 1 million people from 14 countries, including El Salvador, Venezuela, Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Afghanistan and Syria. Only about 103,000 from three countries remain protected with termination dates in October for Ukraine and Sudan, and November for Lebanon.
The Trump administration obtained a major victory when the Supreme Court ruled in June that Homeland Security acted within its authority by ending TPS for about 350,000 Haitians and 6,000 Syrians. The impact of the decision extends far beyond Haitians and Syrians, potentially affecting nearly 1.3 million people from 17 countries on TPS.
TPS was created by Congress in 1990 to prevent deportations to countries suffering from natural disasters or civil strife.
It was granted to El Salvador following two devastating 2001 earthquakes that left hundreds of thousands of people homeless. Just before leaving office, President Joe Biden extended TPS for El Salvador for 18 months to Sept. 9, 2026.
The vast majority of Salvadoran TPS holders have children born in the U.S. Many have lost their jobs and fear being detained, separated from their American family members, and deported to a country they barely know.
— The Associated Press contributed to this story.
title: Aurora Sentinel: Rep. Crow introduces bill to extend TPS protections for Ukrainian immigrants

Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement marking the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack in Israel carried out by Hamas.
“Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists committed an atrocity that forever scarred Israel and the Jewish people. We honor the hostages and their families, those murdered, including the Americans among them, and stand with those whose lives were forever changed. We also recognize the enduring anguish of Jewish communities in the United States and around the world. For those who lived through October 7 or lost loved ones, its trauma is not confined to an anniversary—it is lived every day. There can be no justification for October 7. I remain steadfast in my commitment to Israel’s security and its right to protect its people from terrorism.
“We also recognize the immense suffering, loss, and displacement Palestinian civilians have endured since October 7. Their lives and dignity matter. Acknowledging their suffering does not diminish the unique horror of October 7 or Hamas’ responsibility for its crimes. Our humanity requires us to mourn innocent lives and work to protect them.
“Honoring the victims requires more than remembrance. It requires sustained work to prevent such atrocities from happening again, to confront terrorism, protect civilians, and pursue diplomacy that enables Israelis to live in security and Palestinians to live in freedom and dignity. Neither people’s children should be condemned to inherit endless war. May the memory of those murdered on October 7 be a blessing. May their families find comfort, and may their memory strengthen our resolve to prevent further suffering and pursue peace."
###
title: Meeks Marks the 3rd Anniversary of the October 7th Terrorist Attacks in Israel

“DON’T MESS WITH NEW YORK”: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND NEW YORK DELEGATION INTRODUCE BICAMERAL LEGISLATION TO REVERSE TRUMP’S DEVASTATING CUTS TO HEALTHCARE AND RESTORE COVERAGE FOR 450,000 NEW YORKERS
“Don’t Mess With New York”: Congressman Pat Ryan and New York Delegation Introduce Bicameral Legislation to Reverse Trump’s Devastating Cuts to Healthcare and Restore Coverage for 450,000 New Yorkers
Congressman Pat Ryan and the entire New York Democratic Delegation introduced legislation to reverse the Republican cuts to health care and restore coverage for 450,000 New Yorkers.
In NY-18, 15,656 Essential Plan enrollees were impacted by cuts to health care funding in Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Congressman Pat Ryan joined the entire New York Democratic delegation in introducing the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, legislation to restore health coverage to the nearly 450,000 New Yorkers who were kicked off of the Essential Plan under the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act. In NY-18, 15,656 Essential Plan enrollees were impacted.
Specifically, the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act would repeal the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s premium tax credit eligibility restrictions, fully restoring funding for the Essential Plan. In addition to restoring the program, the legislation would provide all states with the option to expand health coverage through the Affordable Care Act’s Basic Health Plan.
“For over a year now, we’ve felt the devastating consequences of Trump and Republicans’ health care cuts right here in the Hudson Valley. Trump and spineless rubber-stamp Republicans in Congress cut $1 trillion from your health care and food assistance to fund a tax cut for billionaires – and they specifically targeted New York’s Essential Plan, ripping healthcare from more than 15,000 people in our district,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “It’s cruel, un-American, and the exact opposite of everything our community stands for. On behalf of the 450,000 New Yorkers kicked off their insurance, we’re fighting back. I’m incredibly proud to join our entire state Democratic delegation in introducing this legislation to reverse the cuts, restore your coverage, and send a clear message to Trump: Don’t mess with New York.”
Congressman Ryan was an early, strong critic of President Trump domestic spending agenda – calling it a “Big, Ugly Betrayal” of the American people. Trump’s agenda rips health care coverage away from more than 17 million Americans, has caused a massive hike in insurance premiums for millions, and has already closed, significantly reduced services, or forced mass layoffs at countless hospitals nationwide. 77% of respondents to Ryan’s survey on ACA premiums said they’d already received notice their bills would increase.
This legislation is cosponsored by the entire New York Democratic delegation including: Senators Schumer (D-NY) and Gillibrand (D-NY), Leader Jeffries (NY-08), and Representatives Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Clarke (NY-09), Espaillat (NY-13), Gillen (NY-04), Goldman (NY-10), Kennedy (NY-26), Latimer (NY-16), Mannion (NY-22), Meeks (NY-5), Meng (NY-6), Morelle (NY-25), Nadler (NY-12), Riley (NY-19), Ryan (NY-18), Suozzi (NY-3), Tonko (NY-20), Torres (NY-15), and Velázquez (NY-07).

Reps. Davids (D), Crane (R) Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Eli Crane (R-AZ-02) introduced bipartisan legislation to improve how unused housing vouchers are managed and distributed. The legislation would allow Tribes to voluntarily give back vouchers they do not plan to use, so the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) can redirect assistance to Tribal communities facing a shortage.
"Native veterans hold a special place in my heart,” said Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation of Wisconsin. “My mom and grandfather both served in the Army, and as a Native person, I know how much our communities value the veterans who have served our country. Tribal Nations know best what their communities and veterans need, and respecting Tribal sovereignty means giving them the flexibility and resources to meet those needs. I'm grateful to work with Rep. Crane on this bipartisan effort to ensure more Native veterans get the housing they need after returning home.”
"The Tribal HUD-VASH program helps house Tribal veterans in need, but the current system is not as efficient as it should be,” said Representative Eli Crane (R-AZ-02). “Some Tribes have leftover vouchers they cannot use while others lack the resources to take care of our veterans. Our legislation aims to resolve this longstanding issue by getting unused vouchers into the hands of Tribes that can put them to use. This is a sensible approach that makes better use of existing support without expanding the size and scope of the federal government. As the representative for more than half of the Tribes in Arizona, I'm honored to advocate for these heroes by reforming and modernizing this process. I appreciate Rep. Davids' willingness to work across the aisle. We've made real progress together before, and I look forward to building on that success with this bill.”
Native American veterans experience some of the highest rates of homelessness in the United States. To address this, Congress created the Tribal HUD-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (Tribal HUD-VASH) demonstration program, which provides rental assistance and supportive services to Native veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
Although the program has helped many veterans secure stable housing, it lacks a clear process for Tribes to return vouchers they cannot use or to request additional ones. As a result, valuable housing support sits idle while veterans in other Tribal communities wait for help.
The new Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act directs HUD to establish a voluntary program for reallocating unused Tribal HUD-VASH vouchers to Native veterans who need them most. Under the bill, Tribes and Tribally Designated Housing Entities (TDHEs) can notify HUD via digital, phone, or mail correspondence if they have surplus vouchers or request additional assistance for their communities without impacting their future allocations.
Required to launch within 180 days of enactment, the program creates a streamlined process to strengthen Tribal HUD-VASH and expand Native veterans' access to earned housing assistance. Within that same timeframe, HUD must submit a congressional report detailing voucher usage and shortfall metrics, distribution recommendations, and an assessment of whether to increase overall program funding.
This is not the first time Davids and Crane have partnered on legislation to assist Tribal communities. Davids previously introduced the Native American Entrepreneurial Opportunity Act, which would bolster U.S. Small Business Administration outreach to Tribal entrepreneurs navigating the unique complexities of running a business on a reservation. Crane co-led the measure, and it has twice passed the House with strong bipartisan support.
title: Reps. Davids (D), Crane (R) Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans

Rep. Sykes Announces $33,000 for Canal Fulton-Lawrence Township Fire Department
CANAL FULTON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Canal Fulton – Lawrence Township Fire Department is receiving two Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) grant awards that will fund new firefighting equipment and a community fire safety training tool. Congresswoman Sykes supported both grant applications with letters of support.
The City of Canal Fulton received the following awards:
- $17,055.55 in federal funding for a regional fire hose replacement, with a local share of $852.78, for a total project investment of $17,908.33. The project will replace attack and supply hose within the departments' shared response system.
- $16,737.14 in federal funding for a fire extinguisher training system, with a local share of $836.86, for a total project investment of $17,574.00. The project will provide an augmented-reality training system that allows hands-on public education without live fire, smoke, chemical discharge, or cleanup.
Together, the awards provide $33,792.69 in federal funding toward a total investment of $35,482.33 in public safety projects.
“Our firefighters and EMS crews show up to keep our neighbors safe every day, and they must have the tools to do their jobs safely. I am proud to have supported Canal Fulton's grant applications, and I congratulate Chief Yerian and the entire department on these well-earned awards,”said Congresswoman Sykes.
“Receiving these FEMA awards is tremendous news for the Canal Fulton community and our regional fire service,” said Shawn Yerian, Fire Chief of the Canal Fulton – Lawrence Township Fire Department. “The funding will allow us to replace outdated fire hose that our firefighters rely on every day, while also providing a new fire extinguisher training system that addresses one of the most frequent safety-training requests we receive from local businesses.
“These are important investments in both firefighter safety and community education, and they are projects we would not have been able to move forward with at this time without federal assistance. We are extremely grateful for Congresswoman Sykes' support of our applications and her continued support of local fire and EMS services. Her assistance helped make it possible for us to bring these resources back to the community we serve.”
Congresswoman Sykes congratulates Chief Yerian and the entire Canal Fulton - Lawrence Township Fire Department on these awards and thanks them for their service to the community.
title: Rep. Sykes Announces $33,000 for Canal Fulton-Lawrence Township Fire Department

Rep. Sykes Announces $493,000 for TRIO Programs at the University of Akron
AKRON, OHIO — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced the Department of Education has awarded the University of Akron $493,314 as part of the TRIO talent search program. This grant will be awarded annually for five years, beginning in 2026, and is expected to serve nearly 900 students each year.
“Programs like TRIO provide deserving students with the opportunity to pursue higher education,” said Rep. Sykes. “I congratulate the University of Akron for supporting first generation college students participating in the TRIO program who will go on to make a meaningful impact in our community. I am a proud supporter of TRIO and other programs that help our families in Ohio’s 13th Congressional District reach higher heights.”
“The University of Akron Educational Talent Search Program is honored to continue this important work for another five years.” said Dr. Fedearia Nicholson, Vice Provost for Student Pathways and Dean of the Williams Honors College. “This investment from the U.S. Department of Education will create meaningful opportunities for Akron and Summit County students to prepare for college, careers, and the workforce. We are grateful to Congresswoman Emilia Sykes, Provost Gwen Price, Dr. Sandie Crawford and Akron Public Schools for their leadership, partnership, and continued support. I also want to recognize and thank our dedicated ETS team, Meiyah Hill, Amber Lambing, Shananne Lewis, and Roy Rosario, whose commitment to our students and families makes this work possible. Together, we are investing in the future of our students and our community.”
The TRIO Program is mandated by Congress and helps students from disadvantaged families receive the support they need to send their children to college. Two-thirds of TRIO students must come from families with combined incomes of no greater than 150% of the federal poverty line, and the student’s parents cannot have attended college. Schools that offer TRIO programs give students tutoring, counseling, financial guidance, and other forms of assistance.
title: Rep. Sykes Announces $493,000 for TRIO Programs at the University of Akron

190 Members of Congress Slam HHS Effort to Dismantle Head Start
WASHINGTON –One hundred ninety Members of Congress demanded that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.
In the House, the letter is led by Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08), Early Childhood and Elementary and Secondary Education Subcommittee Ranking Member Bonamici (D-OR-01), and Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13). In the Senate, the letter is led by Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Sanders (I-VT), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA), and Senator Ben RayLuján (D-NM).
The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.
“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”
Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely. These actions serve the Trump Administration’s goal to end the Head Start program as laid out on page 482 of Project 2025.

Crow Introduces Bill to Extend Temporary Protected Status for Ukrainians
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and House Armed Services Committee, introduced legislation that will protect Ukrainian nationals already in the U.S. against the threat of deportation by extending their Temporary Protected Status (TPS).
Crow’s bill provides certainty and stability for Ukrainians currently in the U.S. by extending TPS for this group through June 2029. TPS for Ukrainian nationals is currently set to expire on October 19, 2026, despite continued threats facing the country from Russian aggression. Passing Crow’s legislation would ensure that temporary protections for Ukrainian nationals are codified into law past October and not solely up to the whims of any President.
TPS allows foreign nationals who cannot return home due to violence, conflict, and instability to live and work in the U.S. Under TPS, individuals are rigorously and continuously vetted before and after they receive this status.
Crow introduced the bill alongside Congressmen Bill Keating (D-MA) and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA). It was introduced in the Senate by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Chris Coons (D-DE), and Bill Cassidy (R-LA).
“Russia continues its illegal and unprovoked attacks on Ukraine. Vladimir Putin is attacking Ukrainian schools, homes, hospitals, and energy infrastructure across the country with drones, ballistic missiles, and aerial bombs. Millions of Ukrainian women, children, and refugees have fled the violence fearing for their lives. America must continue to stand with the people of Ukraine,” said Congressman Crow.
Congressman Crow has been a strong supporter of the Ukrainian people. In December 2021, just before Russia’s full-scale invasion, Congressman Crow led a delegation to Kyiv to reaffirm America’s commitment to Ukraine. When the invasion began, he immediately called for the U.S. to send military and humanitarian support to Ukraine, for international sanctions against Russia, and for a stronger NATO alliance to meet these new security threats. Weeks later, as Ukrainians fled their homes, Congressman Crow and other members advocated for an expedited immigration status for Ukrainians to the U.S. Crow has visited Ukraine several times since Russia’s invasion. The Congressman has been one of the earliest and strongest supporters of military, development, and humanitarian assistance for Ukraine. He voted for, and strongly advocated for, every supplemental package provided to Ukraine.
Full text of the bill is available here.
###
title: Crow Introduces Bill to Extend Temporary Protected Status for Ukrainians

Ranking Member Khanna Joined by Democratic Lawmakers to Raise Alarm Over DOE Cancellation of Transmission Corridors, Warns Decision Could Undermine U.S. Manufacturing and Competitiveness with China
WASHINGTON – Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, joined Rep. André Carson (D-IN), Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA), Rep. Paul Tonko (D-NY), and Rep. Mike Levin (D-CA), to raise serious concerns about the Department of Energy’s decision to abandon three proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors (NIETCs), warning that the move could undermine U.S. manufacturing, increase electricity costs for American families, and weaken the nation’s ability to compete with China.
In a [democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/2026.10.06-letter-to-doe-on-nietc-cancellations.pdf]letter to Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Tuesday, the lawmakers questioned the Department’s August 12 decision not to move forward with the Lake Erie-Canada Corridor, Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and Tribal Energy Access Corridor. He also pressed the Department to explain how it plans to address the nation’s urgent transmission needs and accelerate permitting for critical grid infrastructure.
The letter comes as the Department’s own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study found a “pressing need” for additional transmission infrastructure driven in part by expanding domestic manufacturing, large industrial loads, data centers, and a growing economy.
“Arbitrary cancellations like these set back the U.S. in the strategic race with the CCP, hamstring a U.S. manufacturing buildout, and drive up costs for American families,” the lawmakers wrote.
The Members further raised concerns about the impact of inadequate transmission capacity on American consumers. As electricity rates continue to rise, transmission constraints are driving up wholesale power costs and limit the ability of regions to bring new generation online, putting additional pressure on families and businesses already struggling with higher energy bills, the lawmakers wrote.
The Members are calling on Secretary Wright to provide detailed answers to the following by October 26, 2026:
- Please provide a detailed account of any analysis conducted by the Department of the opportunity cost of cancelling the Lake Erie–Canada Corridor, the Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and the Tribal Energy Access Corridor, including projected effects on ratepayer costs, grid reliability, and industrial electricity supply in the affected regions.
- Did the Department assess the impact of these cancellations on potential manufacturing and energy-intensive development in the regions associated with these cancelled corridors? Please provide a detailed account of that analysis.
- How does the Department reconcile these cancellations with the findings of its own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study?
- What stakeholder feedback did the Department evaluate when deciding to cancel these NIETC designations and did the Department engage with utilities, regional transmission organizations, or the North American Electric Reliability Corporation?
- What steps, if any, will the Department take to address the transmission needs in these three corridors, or in other transmission constrained areas across the country (especially those identified in the 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study)?
Read the full letter to Energy Secretary Wright HERE.
###
title: Ranking Member Khanna Joined by Democratic Lawmakers to Raise Alarm Over DOE Cancellation of Transmission Corridors, Warns Decision Could Undermine U.S. Manufacturing and Competitiveness with China

Meeks (NY-05), Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, led 10 Members of Congress in demanding answers from the State Department about its decision to revoke Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti’s diplomatic visa.

“This unnecessary escalation is the latest of a series of actions that has driven a rupture in our relationship with the largest democracy and economy in South America. At a time when the Trump Administration claims to be prioritizing the Western Hemisphere, this misguided decision further damages America’s reputation in the region and pushes Brazil closer to the hands of our adversaries,” wrote the lawmakers.

They cited State Department officials’ meetings with former President Bolsonaro, sanctions against Supreme Court Justice de Moraes, and statements questioning the integrity of Brazil’s elections as actions threatening the country’s democratic institutions and electoral processes.

Maryland Delegation Members Push for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives April McClain Delaney, Steny Hoyer, Sarah Elfreth, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Glenn Ivey, and Johnny Olszewski were joined by Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) in requesting $11 million for U.S. Cyber Command as Congress works to complete the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense appropriations. In the letter to Appropriations Committee leadership, the lawmakers stressed the importance of the health and wellbeing of the service members and civilian employees of U.S. Cyber Command, as well as the importance of their work to our national security. The $11 million program increase would fund U.S. Cyber Command’s high-performance team training, an operation aimed at improving care for service members, including helping commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, care, and resilience practices.
The lawmakers begin, “We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent military operations missions.”
“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” they continue.
On the need for funding for High Performance Team Training at Cyber Command, the lawmakers note, “The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.”
“Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families,” the lawmakers conclude.
The full text of the letter is available here and below.
Dear Chairman Cole, Ranking Member DeLauro, Chair Collins, and Vice Chair Murray:
We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training under Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations, as Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act. Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions.
As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear.
Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively “deployed in place” for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.
These challenges are particularly relevant at Fort Meade, where U.S. Cyber Command, the National Security Agency, military cyber components, and other national security organizations operate within a highly secure and interconnected environment. Although Maryland has a significant network of military, federal, and civilian health resources, traditional centralized-care models do not always give cyber personnel timely access to appropriately cleared professionals in the facilities where they work.
Congress and the Department have already recognized this gap. Congress previously directed a review of the psychological and occupational demands placed on cyber operators, and the Department subsequently acknowledged that existing resources did not fully meet the needs of the U.S. Cyber Command. The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) also expanded mental health services intended to address the U.S. Cyber Command’s unique requirements by integrating behavioral health professionals with security clearances within cyber units. Nevertheless, dedicated support teams and embedded care have not been implemented consistently across the force.
The requested $11 million would help U.S. Cyber Command close this gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, identify concerns earlier, and help commanders establish sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices. Models used in other high-demand military communities, including special operations and remotely piloted aircraft units, and dedicated intelligence commands demonstrate the value of treating psychological health and human performance as readiness requirements. Cyber Command noted that without this funding, burnout and force degradation will increase.
This represents a modest investment compared with U.S. Cyber Command’s broader annual budget and the strategic value of its highly trained workforce. Recruiting, clearing, and developing cyber operators takes years. Losing experienced personnel harms Maryland families, disrupts operational teams, increases replacement and training costs, and reduces the Nation’s ability to defend critical systems and conduct cyber missions.
Accordingly, we respectfully request that the final Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act retain the following program increase:
12D CYBERSPACE OPERATIONS
High Performance Team Training ........................................ $11,000,000
Preserving this funding would demonstrate Congress’s commitment to the health and readiness of the cyber workforce at Fort Meade, Maryland, and across the Nation. It would also help ensure that the Department establishes an enduring system of prevention, care, and operational resilience rather than relying solely on short-term interventions following a tragedy. One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again.
We appreciate your continued leadership and support of Maryland’s servicemembers, federal employees, and families.

text:
Rep. Mike Levin Pushes Administration to Adopt Critical Reforms to Improve Access to SNAP Benefits for Veterans
Washington, D.C.—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) applauded a new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report outlining recommendations to improve veterans’ access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). In January 2024, Rep. Levin served as the Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity with Chair Derrick Van Orden (WI-03) and requested GAO to examine how states with reported high and low rates of food insecurity have targeted veterans in the state annual outreach plans. On October 1, 2026, GAO published the report, “Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Federal Actions Needed to Help Veterans Access Benefits,” which highlights the importance of conducting veteran-specific SNAP outreach to increase awareness and use of food resources.
According to a 2023 RAND report, more than one million veterans faced food insecurity each year from 2015 to 2020. Eligible veterans can use SNAP benefits to access healthy foods, but they’re less likely to participate than non-veterans. In the report, GAO reviewed states’ efforts to target SNAP outreach to veterans and work with veterans’ organizations to help connect veterans to the program. GAO also examined state and federal efforts to improve the type of SNAP outreach conducted to veterans. The report makes four recommendations for the Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to more effectively tackle veteran food insecurity.
“More than one million veterans face food insecurity in this country. That is one million too many. That is why, when I served as Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity, I asked GAO to investigate how states and the federal government can better help veterans get the support they need. I am encouraged by the report’s findings on successful state outreach efforts, but I am deeply troubled that USDA has still not updated its website to inform veterans about new requirements that could result in them losing their benefits,” said Rep. Levin. “One of the many reasons I opposed H.R. 1 was because it eliminated the work requirement exemption for veterans and created additional barriers to accessing food assistance. I am also concerned that, following staffing cuts in 2025, USDA has failed to fill critical positions that support coordination with the Department of Veterans Affairs on veteran hunger. That is unacceptable. USDA must take these findings seriously and act quickly to address the gaps identified by GAO. I plan to work with my colleagues to hold the Administration accountable for implementing GAO’s recommendations as quickly as possible and ensuring veterans can access the support they have earned.”
GAO made three recommendations to USDA and one to VA, including:
- The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure Food and Nutrition Administration’s (FNA) SNAP eligibility website includes up-to-date information about exceptions to the SNAP time limit.
- The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure FNA develops and disseminates additional SNAP outreach materials tailored to veterans, in collaboration with Veterans Health Administration (VHA).
- The Secretary of Agriculture should ensure a formal mechanism is in place to collaborate with VA on efforts to address veteran food insecurity. This could include reviewing the memorandum of agreement (MOA) and updating the agreement as needed.
- The Secretary of Veterans Affairs should ensure a formal mechanism is in place to collaborate with VA on efforts to address veteran food insecurity. This could include reviewing the MOA and updating the agreement as needed.
Rep. Levin will continue working with the relevant federal agencies to ensure they implement GAO’s recommendations and address reducing barriers for veterans seeking access to SNAP.
###
title: Rep. Mike Levin Pushes Administration to Adopt Critical Reforms to Improve Access to SNAP Benefits for Veterans

Resolution Honors Captain, Crew, Passengers Who Saved All Lives
Calls for a Full Investigation
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10), and Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2) introduced a bipartisan resolution honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on the flight.
“Captain Machchhar is a hero. While gravely wounded, he fought off a terrorist attack and saved every soul on that plane, including 27 children and four Americans,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Congress must honor his extraordinary courage, and we must be clear that this was an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international air travel. I’m proud to lead this resolution with Congressman McCaul and Congressman Bacon, and we wish Captain Machchhar and everyone injured a full recovery.”
“I’m proud to co-lead this resolution, which condemns the attempted terrorist attack, calls for a full investigation, and honors the brave crew and passengers. The world owes a debt of gratitude to these heroes — especially Captain Smit Machchhar, who sustained injuries fighting the attacker and still managed to unlock the cockpit door and allow others to land the plane,” said Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10). “Were it not for his extraordinary courage, this story could have ended in horrific tragedy. I wish Captain Machchhar, the crew, and all the passengers healing and strength as we await a comprehensive investigation into this harrowing incident.”
On September 30, Flight 1073 departed Dubai for Tel Aviv carrying approximately 174 passengers and six crew, including 4 U.S. citizens and 27 children. Midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain with the aircraft’s emergency crash axe and tried to seize the controls, sending the plane plunging more than 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Despite grave injuries, Captain Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and unlocked the cockpit door so off-duty pilots could enter and land the plane, and so crew and passengers could restrain the first officer. The aircraft landed safely in Saudi Arabia with everyone accounted for. On October 3, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the investigation had determined the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act.
The resolution:
- Honors Captain Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft;
- Commends the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down;
- Wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery;
- Condemns the attack as an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international civil aviation;
- Calls for a full and expeditious investigation by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.
###
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Flydubai Flight 1073 Heroes

WASHINGTON – After President Trump personally directed that taxpayer funding be used for a series of political ads, he has reportedly reversed course. U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), and House Natural Resources Committee top Democrat Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), led 30 of their colleagues in calling on House and Senate Armed Services Committee leaders to reject the Hunt Amendment’s provision (Section 2835) in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which would grant unprecedented eminent domain authority to the federal government to benefit Sable Offshore Corporation.
 “The NDAA has long served as a bipartisan vehicle to strengthen our national security and support our servicemembers. However, we are deeply concerned by the inclusion of Section 2835, which would grant extraordinary eminent domain authority to the federal government to circumvent established environmental protections for the benefit of a single private company. Given the sweeping implications of this provision, we believe this policy rider does not belong in the NDAA and, therefore, should be removed from the final conference agreement,” wrote the lawmakers. 
 The lawmakers explain how this provision would jeopardize the California coastal economy and do little to strengthen our nation’s energy security. 
“California’s coastal economy supports roughly 511,000 jobs and generates over $51.3 billion in GDP from marine-economy activities — largely in tourism and recreation. Another oil spill from a corrosion-prone pipeline that has spilled before would jeopardize the economic security of everyday Americans that rely on our coastal economy for their livelihoods,” the lawmakers continued. “In addition, there is no evidence that this provision would meaningfully advance our nation's energy security. Recent spikes in gasoline prices driven by market uncertainty surrounding the war in Iran underscore that global oil markets—not a single offshore project—continue to dictate prices at the pump.”
The letter goes on to highlight the unprecedented nature of Section 2835, which would grant the federal government extraordinary powers to seize property for the sole benefit of a single private organization. 
“The NDAA should not be used to circumvent established permitting processes or create special authorities for individual projects that have failed to secure the approvals required under existing law. The federal government's power of eminent domain is among its most significant authorities and should be exercised only when there is a clear and compelling public purpose—not to resolve private infrastructure disputes or increase the profitability of a single company—at the expense of communities who have to live with the consequences of an oil spill,” said the lawmakers. 
The full letter is available HERE.
Joining Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, and Huffman the letter is co-signed by U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (D-CA-43), Dave Min (D-CA-47), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Mike Thompson (D-CA-04), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA-11), John Garamendi (D-CA-08), Gil Cisneros (D-CA-31), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Derek Tran (D-CA-45), Mike Levin (D-CA-49), Juan Vargas (D-CA-52), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Laura Friedman (D-CA-30), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12), Kevin Mullin (D-CA-15), Mark Takano (D-CA-39), Ami Bera, M.D. (D-CA-06), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Scott Peters (D-CA-50), Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Pete Aguilar (D-CA-33), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37), George Whitesides (D-CA-27), Luz Rivas (D-CA-29), and Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51). 
Background
Sable Offshore acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024. The pipeline had been out of service since the 2015 Refugio oil spill. In March 2026, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the Defense Production Act and ordered Sable to restore pipeline operations. 
Carbajal has been a leader in opposing the Sable pipeline’s forced restart. 
In September 2026, Carbajal led a bicameral group of colleagues in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright to challenge the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along the California Central Coast. The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority.
In July 2026, Carbajal spoke on the House floor against the NDAA’s Hunt amendment, which would grant the federal government unprecedented access to California-owned public lands associated with the Santa Ynez Unit and Las Flores Pipeline System.
 In May 2026, Carbajal, Schiff, and members of the California congressional delegation launched an inquiry into Sable’s efforts to restart oil drilling off the California coast and demanded answers on the company’s collaboration with the Trump administration to invoke the DPA in relation to this project.
Last year, Carbajal, Schiff, Padilla, and members of the California congressional delegation demanded answers from the Trump administration on its involvement in Sable’s attempts to restart the pipeline.
title: Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, Huffman Lead Colleagues in Urging Removal of Hunt Amendment from Annual Defense Bill

Reps. Cisneros, Castro Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
WASHINGTON D.C. — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.
Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most-watched and financially successful productions.
El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.
“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”
“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country,” said Congressman Castro. “Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”
“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”
“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”
“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen,” said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. “Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”
“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”
“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”
Read the full text of the resolution here
Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.
###
title: Reps. Cisneros, Castro Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers

ICYMI: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Urges HUD to Implement Whole Home Repairs Law
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) joined U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) and U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) in a letter to U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner urging an establishment of a Whole Home Repairs program through the Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes.
The Members wrote:
“Almost 7 million Americans live in homes that are in need of significant repair, with deficiencies including leaky roofs, faulty wiring, and mold. This is an issue that disproportionately affects America’s seniors, many of whom would like to downsize but do not want to sell the home at a steep discount due to the updates required. As we saw in Commonwealth of Pennsylvania’s successful Whole Home Repairs program, providing grants for repairs allowed seniors to sell larger homes to growing families.”
The Whole-Home Repairs Act was signed into law with the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The Whole Home Repairs pilot program will provide renovation and repair grants to homeowners and small landlords. This will help ensure America’s aging homes do not fall out of the housing supply.
The Members continued:
“The language in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act authorizes you to operate a Whole Home Repairs program through 2031. We want to show the nation that repairing America’s crumbling homes is not a red or blue issue. Creating greater access to housing is an American issue. Any delays will mean millions of American families may never realize the benefit of this program. We were proud to help the Whole Home Repairs bill become law, and we stand ready to support you in making it a reality for Americans.”
Read the full text of the letter here.
title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Urges HUD to Implement Whole Home Repairs Law

Rep. Chu, Tri-Caucus Leaders Demand HHS Withdraw Harmful English-Only Head Start Proposal
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), Chair Emerita of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), CAPAC Chair Grace Meng (NY-06), Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) Chair Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) Chair Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Rep. Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), and Rep. Juan Vargas (CA-52) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary 
Head Start is a critical program that provides high-quality early childhood education and comprehensive support services for low-income children and their families. While the Members urge HHS to withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety, their letter focuses specifically on its harmful changes to language-access protections. Nearly 40 percent of children enrolled in Head Start are dual-language learners, representing almost 290,000 children nationwide, and 30 percent of enrollees come from families whose primary home language is not English.
In the letter, the Members explain that dual-language instruction helps children learn English and prepare for school:
“We share the goal of ensuring that every Head Start child develops strong English-language skills. But requiring English-only instruction is not supported by the evidence and risks undermining that very goal. For many children, Head Start is their first experience in a classroom. Providing an environment in which young children can understand, communicate, and participate supports their ability to learn and successfully transition into school.
The Members also warn that the proposed rule conflicts with Congress’s explicit directives in the Head Start Act:
“Congress directed the Secretary to establish standards ensuring that children with limited English proficiency make progress toward acquiring English while simultaneously making meaningful progress in other developmental domains, including through “culturally and linguistically appropriate instructional services” (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(a)(1)(B)(x)). Congress further directed the Secretary, when revising Head Start standards, to ensure that revisions do not eliminate or reduce the quality, scope, or types of educational, parental-involvement, health, or other services required under longstanding Head Start standards (42 U.S.C. § 9836a(a)(2)(C)). And the Head Start Act explicitly requires agencies to ensure teachers receive literacy training “in methods to promote vocabulary development and phonological awareness (including phonemic awareness) in a developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate manner and support children’s development in their native language” (42 U.S. Code § 9843(d)(2)(B)). Eliminating longstanding language-access protections appears directly at odds with these congressional directives, and the Department has not adequately explained how its proposal can be reconciled with them.”
The Members detail how eliminating bilingual staffing requirements could undermine parents’ ability to participate in their children’s education and jeopardize accurate developmental screenings and assessments:
“Congress recognized that informed and engaged parents are essential to children’s success and required Head Start programs to conduct family needs assessments and communicate with parents, to the extent practicable, in a language they understand (42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(J)(vii); 42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(K); 42 U.S. Code § 9836a(f)(2)). Eliminating language-access staffing requirements without providing an adequate alternative could make it more difficult for parents to understand their children’s progress, participate in their education, communicate with teachers and staff, and access the comprehensive services Head Start provides.
We are particularly concerned about the consequences for developmental screenings and assessments. The Head Start Act requires measures used by Head Start programs to be developmentally, linguistically, and culturally appropriate; valid and reliable in the language in which they are administered; administered by appropriately trained staff; and accompanied by appropriate accommodations for children with limited English proficiency (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(b)(2)). These protections are critical. A screening or assessment administered in a language a young child does not sufficiently understand risks mistaking normal second-language development for a developmental delay or, conversely, failing to identify a genuine disability or developmental concern. Either outcome could delay appropriate early intervention at precisely the age when it can make the greatest difference.”
Finally, the Members warn that the proposal would impose significant disruption and costs on Head Start providers while weakening services for hundreds of thousands of children:
“The scale of the disruption caused by the proposed rule’s language-access changes would be substantial. Almost 290,000 dual-language learners nationwide could be affected […] Although the proposal is titled Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs, affected programs could be forced to change curricula, replace classroom materials, and retrain or replace teachers, resulting in an estimated $99 million in costs.”
“HHS should not reverse decades of evidence-based practice, impose new costs on providers, and weaken language-access protections for hundreds of thousands of children without a compelling evidentiary or legal basis for doing so. Accordingly, we strongly urge HHS to withdraw the proposed English-only instruction requirement and retain the longstanding language-access protections that allow Head Start programs to effectively serve dual-language learners and their families. Congress expressly directed Head Start to support English-language acquisition through culturally and linguistically appropriate services, and HHS should uphold, not undermine, that mandate.”
Read the full letter HERE.
title: Rep. Chu, Tri-Caucus Leaders Demand HHS Withdraw Harmful English-Only Head Start Proposal

Congresswoman Lee Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect High-Risk Faith-Based and Community Organizations
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and María Elvira Salazar (R-FL) introduced the bipartisan Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act, which would make it easier for nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist attack to access federal grant funding for target hardening and physical security enhancements.
“We can all agree that our children should be able to go to school and that families should be able to worship without fear. As hate crimes rise throughout the country, nonprofit organizations, churches, synagogues, mosques, and religious schools are diverting their scarce resources away from serving their communities to pay for security cameras, guards, and emergency trainings,” said Congresswoman Lee. “No organization should be forced to choose between keeping their members safe or their financial stability. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will help nonprofit organizations fund security improvements and overall preparedness, so they can keep those they serve safe amid increased violence and harassment.”
“Every American should be able to worship without fear. When a church, synagogue, or other place of worship is approved for a federal security grant, it should be able to spend the money to improve security immediately. The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act gets security dollars out the door faster and helps protect our communities,” said Congresswoman Salazar.
Congress created the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) in 2004 to help nonprofit organizations prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from terrorist or extremist attacks. The program funds target hardening, physical security improvements, and related preparedness activities for nonprofits at high risk of terrorism or hate-motivated violence.
Under current law, nonprofit organizations selected to receive an NSGP grant through a competitive application process must pay out of pocket for approved critical security upgrades and then wait months—or even years—to be reimbursed. This places these organizations in an impossible situation: cut into their limited budgets to ensure the safety of those they serve without any idea of when they might see that money or forgo critical security upgrades to ensure they can continue their work unabated.
The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would amend the current law to require that NSGP awards be issued to approved nonprofits in advance, rather than as a reimbursement for costs already incurred. By allowing advance payments, FEMA could better support approved nonprofits that lack upfront capital, speed implementation of needed security measures, and strengthen protection for vulnerable communities.
“Synagogues and nonprofit are paying out of pocket for essential security, then waiting months or years to get their money back,” said Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL CEO and National Director. “Providing funding upfront to institutions already approved for security grants would help ease that financial burden and allow them to make critical security improvements sooner. We thank Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for advancing this commonsense solution to get security dollars where they’re needed, when they’re needed.”
“According to American Jewish Committee’s (AJC) State of Antisemitism in America 2025 Report, 28% of American Jews say that at least one Jewish institution they are affiliated with has been a target of antisemitic incidents in the last five years. As threats against Jewish institutions continue to rise, we applaud Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for introducing the Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act,” said Julie Rayman, AJC’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Political Affairs. “By removing a financial barrier that can delay or prevent needed security upgrades, this legislation will help at-risk institutions better protect the communities they serve.”
“Counties are on the front lines of keeping communities safe, but too often they are left filling the gap when nonprofits can’t afford to pay upfront for critical security upgrades,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would allow approved nonprofits to receive funding upfront, helping them strengthen security sooner rather than delaying upgrades due to lack of capital. That means safer facilities, stronger coordination with local law enforcement and more resilient communities. Counties urge Congress to advance this bipartisan legislation quickly.”
“The Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) is an important resource for houses of worship to better secure themselves against acts of hate and prepare for all kinds of emergencies, but the logistical burdens of the process can pose barriers to applicants. This important proposal to disburse funds up front rather than requiring a reimbursement-based model removes one such major hurdle. With these kinds of improvements, as well as timely and apolitical execution by the Department of Homeland Security, NSGP can continue to serve more of our nation's most vulnerable communities in a time of increased threats.” – Mannirmal Kaur, Senior Federal Policy Manager, The Sikh Coalition.
The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act is endorsed by Jewish Nevada, American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), National Association of Counties (NACO), Secure Community Network, and The Sikh Coalition.
More information on the bill is here.
title: Congresswoman Lee Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect High-Risk Faith-Based and Community Organizations

Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers
For Immediate Release
October 6, 2026
Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers 
NORTH LAS VEGAS – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) sent a joint letter to the Social Security Administration, calling on the agency to process pending applications submitted by Clark County Family Services (CCFS) to obtain Social Security Cards for youth in foster care. The letter comes after months of unanswered attempts by CCFS, County Commissioners, and both Rep. Horsford’s and Sen. Cortez Masto’s offices to work with SSA to rectify the issue. 
In December 2025, SSA notified CCFS that Social Security number applications required certain accompanying documentation to be physically certified by the custodian of record. For children in foster care, the custodian of record is the State of Nevada, which has operated digitally since 2010 when the Eighth Judicial District Court of Nevada mandated electronic filing for civil and family cases. This discrepancy between state law and federal agency policy makes it nearly impossible for CCFS to comply with SSA’s rule.
“Once again, the people are caught up in bureaucracy,” said Rep. Horsford. “Our priority is ensuring people have access to the services they are entitled to and can live their lives to the fullest. Our foster youth are among the most vulnerable in our community and SSA’s unwillingness to acknowledge our local laws shows this Administration’s regard for Nevadans.”
Over 1,300 foster youth in Clark County are currently unable to receive their Social Security Cards, severely restricting their livelihoods and quality of life.
“Without Social Security numbers, these youth can’t receive federal healthcare coverage, secure permanent placement in loving families, or even get their first job,” said Sen. Cortez Masto. “The Trump Administration must immediately process outstanding Social Security number applications and work with Clark County to remedy these documentation issues, so Nevada’s foster children don’t have to proceed any longer with their lives on pause.”
Since the initial notice in December, CCFS has provided documentation from the State of Nevada to SSA consistent with the state’s mandated electronic records and has offered to obtain any necessary information from the state to authenticate these records that may be used in other states. To date, there has been no response from SSA to this request.
“Clark County is grateful to the leadership of Senator Cortez Masto and Congressman Horsford as they work on our behalf to address this pressing issue which is impacting over 1,300 children in our care,” said Kevin Schiller, Clark County Manager. “Our most sacred responsibility is ensuring our most vulnerable children are cared for and we are being inhibited from doing this in the current state with the Social Security Administration.”
The full text of the letter can be found HERE.
title: Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers

WASHINGTON, DC (October 6, 2026) — Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Kennedy Jr. regarding the Teen Pregnancy Prevention (TPP) grants that were canceled by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
“I am concerned that HHS is still holding funding for these important grants that support locally delivered, evidence-based programs that reach young people where they live, often in communities with limited access to health education and services, including rural areas,” the Congresswoman wrote.
“HHS must have a plan to ensure that this vital program continues (...) HHS must immediately reinstate funding for TPP Program grantees that your department cut off earlier this year,” Congresswoman Foushee continued.
“I request that you immediately share HHS's plan to allocate funding for the TPP program with funds obligated by Congress and ensure that grantees, including North Carolina, will continue to offer important evidence-based education and not see their funding and program implementation further interrupted,” the Congresswoman concluded.
Duke University, located in North Carolina’s Fourth Congressional District, was a recipient of a Teen Pregnancy Prevention grant in 2023.
In July, 79 members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) and the Democratic Caucus, sent a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, demanding the reversal of the Trump Administration’s cancellation of 53 active Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program (TPP) grants that the Department claimed were no longer aligned with the agency’s priorities.
Recent decisions by the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia blocked HHS from establishing new grants with new funding conditions. 92 members of Congress, including Rep. Foushee, recently stated in a letter to HHS, that this funding must be reinstated for TPP grantees that were cut off earlier this year.
The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: Rep. Foushee Demands Answers From Secretary Kennedy Regarding Cancellation of Teen Pregnancy Prevention Grants

García, Colleagues Issue Joint Statement Condemning Israel’s Persecution of Palestinian Healthcare Workers
CHICAGO — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), along with Congressmembers Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Summer Lee (PA-12), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), and Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) released a joint statement condemning the Israeli government’s systematic persecution of Palestinian healthcare workers, and called for their immediate release from arbitrary detention.
“Over the last three years, the Israeli government has systematically destroyed the health system in Palestine, murdering at least 1,700 Palestinian doctors, nurses, paramedics, and other healthcare workers and destroying dozens of hospitals. It has arrested and arbitrarily detained hundreds of Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 16 physicians who continue to be held in inhumane conditions. Among them is Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, whom the Israeli government has arbitrarily detained since 2024 and tortured to the point of near-death after previously murdering his son and brutally attacking his hospital,” said the Members.
“Israel’s systematic annihilation of medical facilities and healthcare workers is not an accident or unfortunate consequence of war; it is an intentional policy designed to further occupation, apartheid, and genocide against the Palestinian people. We demand the immediate release of Dr. Abu Safiya and all other arbitrarily detained healthcare workers and Palestinian prisoners. And we demand an end to U.S. arms transfers to Israel, including the Trump Administration’s latest $2.8 billion sale of bombs. Congress must block this sale and pass the Block the Bombs Act to finally end our government’s shameful complicity in Israel’s mass atrocities.”
Congressman García also recently led a letter condemning the violence by Israeli settlers, police and military in the village of al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank, and called for the release of Marwan Barghouti who has been detained and tortured in Israeli prison for over 20 years.
