October 6, 2026
WATCH: Pressley, Wu, Breadon Condemn USPS Service Cuts and Proposed Closure of Allston Post Office
Proposal for Allston Branch Also Coincides with USPS Announcement to “Temporarily” Close USPS Field Corner Office Later This Month
Today, Pressley Joined Markey, Mass. Colleagues Demanding USPS Cease Campaign of Post Office Closures in the Commonwealth
ALLSTON – Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) joined Boston Mayor Michelle Wu, Boston City Council President Liz Breadon, and elected officials at a rally to condemn the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) actions to reduce service for residents across the city and plans to permanently close the Allston Post Office. The City of Boston also sent USPS leadership a letter notifying them of the City’s strong opposition to the agency’s reversal of its prior commitment to restore postal services in Allston.
If closed, 87,000 residents of Allston-Brighton will be served by one post office location in Brighton. This proposal also coincides with USPS announcing this week that it will, purportedly temporarily, close the USPS Fields Corner branch later this month.
“The USPS belongs to all of us and is a vital lifeline for folks in Allston who depend on it for everything from daily medications and Social Security checks to mail-in ballots and staying connected to loved ones,” said Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley. “That’s why we’re not letting them off the hook while they go back on their word and rip away this essential resource by permanently closing the Allston branch. I’m proud to stand with Mayor Wu and Councilor Breadon and our colleagues to fight back.”
“The reversal of the Post Office’s prior commitments to reopen the Allston USPS branch is an abdication of responsibility not only to Boston, but to all families,” said Mayor Michelle Wu. “This post office serves grandparents buying stamps to mail birthday cards to their grandchildren, parents sending care packages to students away at college, and residents and small businesses who rely on this location to conduct business. I thank Councilor Breadon for her work and leadership in bringing our community together as we continue to urge United State Postal Service leaders to keep their word and prevent the permanent closure of this vital resource for our community.”
“USPS’s proposal to permanently close the Allston Post Office is an unacceptable reversal of a promise made to our community by USPS,” said Boston City Council President Breadon. “For the past seven years, the 87,000 residents of Allston-Brighton have been served by only one post office location; Newton, which has a population of 88,000, has 10. Our neighborhood will continue to fight for the reestablishment of the Allston Post Office, fair treatment from USPS, and the fulfillment of commitments made.”
At today’s rally, the elected officials invited Allston residents to join them in contesting the closure. This proposal also coincides with USPS announcing last week that it will, purportedly temporarily, close the USPS Fields Corner branch later this month. People interested in submitting public comments can email allstonpostoffice@boston.gov. People should include their name and home address with their comments. The deadline for this initial period is Sunday, October 11 and there will be future opportunities for residents to engage on this issue in the coming months.
Congresswoman Pressley, Mayor Wu, and City Council President Breadon were joined at the press conference today by Scott Hoffman, National Business Agent, American Postal Workers Union; Tony D’Isdoro, President Allston Civic Association; George Huynh, Executive Director VietAID; State Senator Will Brownsberger; State Representative Kevin Honan; City Councilor-At-Large Ruthzee Louijeune; City Councilor-At-Large Erin Murphy; City Councilor-At-Large Henry Santana; City Councilor John FitzGerald, District 3; and President Mark Sideris, Watertown.
“The USPS has asked the Allston community to engage in a charade that operational performance will be enhanced by the permanent closing of the Allston Post Office,” said Tony D’Isidoro, President of the Allston Civic Association. “They’re not fooling anyone! This new business model will fail because it will not be applied fairly across the country.”
“Every day, we see how much our neighbors rely on the post office to apply for benefits, renew passports, update their address, receive important documents, and send packages home to family. For seniors and residents who don’t drive or are more comfortable in their own language, a nearby post office is a lifeline,” said George Huynh, Executive Director of Vietnamese American Initiative for Development (VietAID). “Allston has gone seven years without one. Fields Corner is now facing the same uncertainty, and we cannot afford to wait seven years. We urge USPS to commit to a clear timeline for a permanent location in Fields Corner and to restore the post office here in Allston. Every neighborhood in Boston deserves a post office close to home.”
“It’s bad enough that the Post Office degrades service levels, but here they want to take the post office away lock, stock, and barrel,” said Scott Hoffman, National Business Agent, American Postal Workers Union. “It’s a slippery slope type condition if we let them pull a post office after making promises to the community and to workers, then all is lost. This is a brazen move.”
Footage from the press conference is available here.
Photo Credit: Boston Mayor’s Office
In early September 2026, the United States Postal Service (USPS) announced its intent to study the permanent closure of the Allston Post Office Branch. This proposal has sparked concern and frustration among residents and elected officials. If closed, all 87,000 residents of Allston-Brighton will be served by only one post office location in Brighton.
The Allston Post Office Branch was previously located at 47 Harvard Avenue in Allston. Due to structural issues with its building, USPS suspended service at this location in 2019. In 2021, the former Allston Post Office site was purchased by Boston-based real estate firm Eden Properties. A mixed-used residential project was later approved for the site and is currently under construction. As part of this redevelopment, Eden Properties worked with USPS to reestablish the Allston Post Office Branch in a ground-floor commercial space designed for use by the post office.
In June 2025, USPS sent a letter to Mayor Wu stating its final decision to relocate and reestablish the Allston Post Office. In early September 2026, however, Allston residents received notification via letter from USPS announcing its intent to permanently close the Allston Post Office Branch.
A transcript of the Congresswoman’s remarks is available below and the full video is available here.
Transcript: Rep. Pressley Condemns USPS Plan to Close Allston Branch
October 5, 2026
Allston, MA
In serving on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, I was conducting a lot of oversight in the fight to send Postmaster DeJoy on his way. And I thought when we did that that we might be getting on a path to what the people deserve, and certainly the dedicated postal workers deserve. Instead, we find ourselves here.
But the reason why, in the midst of this, I still have hope, is because I believe in the power of pressure.
I believe in the power of organizing. I believe in the power of solidarity.
I was looking at Representative Honan and remembering the fight to save our branch libraries when we all came together and understood that they are a public good, a lifeline to and for the community, and so this is that same kind of fight. This is about livelihoods. This is about lives. This is about commerce. This is about connectivity. So that’s what brings us all here today.
I’m so grateful for the leadership of everyone who has been named and who has not been named, I’m so grateful to our mayor for convening us, and certainly grateful to our Council President, President Breadon, who has been indefatigable, and that is what we need to be in this fight.
Folks were shuddering a little bit. Maybe it’s a little chilly. It’s hot one second, cold the next. Yeah, welcome to perimenopause.
But the point is, the point is, you might be a little uncomfortable, but deal with it, so that we are never complacent in our advocacy.
I grew up in a family of proud letter carriers, postal workers, nurses, first responders. That was how we built the middle class. These good union jobs. They take pride in that work, no matter the weather, no matter the season, no matter the ingratitude, so that’s what brings us here today.
So I thank you all for showing up, for giving a damn, to show your support for reopening your neighborhood’s post office, which has been closed since 2019.
It is a shame, and the reason why we have to agitate, resist, and give our feedback, we see this is a very slippery slope because they’re trying to bring the same pain to Dorchester, which is why solidarity is so essential in this moment.
But everyone here, your advocacy, your love of community is inspiring. Now, while this injustice has gone on for too long, you refuse, you accept it as an inevitability, and let it be quietly swept under the rug.
So again, I say thank you to everyone, and especially to Scott Hoffman and all of our brothers and sisters at the American Postal Workers Union, who stand up every day for their members, as well as service and reliability for our neighbors.
For the past seven years, Allston residents have gone without retail post office services and had to travel to Brighton, to Brookline, or Cambridge to do their daily business. In that time, USPS has made commitments to my office, my colleagues’ offices, and the folks living in this community that they were searching for a new location and would indeed reopen.
There have been ups and downs, but finally, finally, it appeared we were close to having the branch reopen. A lease had been agreed to, construction plans were in place with the developer. Now we are told that this plan is to keep this branch permanently closed.
This is unconscionable. This is unacceptable.
With last week’s announcement of the quote-unquote “temporary” closure of the Fields Corner Post Office, I find it hard to believe that this is just a coincidence. And to be clear, these efforts to close our local branches are all part of a coordinated campaign.
Y’all are tired of me saying it as the co-founder of the Stop Project 2025 Task Force, but it was all laid out. It was not a blueprint. It was a playbook. They want to privatize the USPS. They want to privatize these essential services that our constituents need every single day.
The USPS has been serving our communities for 250 years, delivering our mail, our checks, our prescriptions, and our ballots.
The dedicated carriers who are out on our sidewalks six days per week are members of our community. They know our neighbors, and they are the way folks most often interact with the federal government.
These services are not nice to haves—they are must haves. And you, along with every other community, has come to depend upon them and rightly deserve them.
These efforts to degrade and undermine the postal service are intended to exhaust you and your neighbors, so that you’ll give up and do your business somewhere else. Hell no, we won’t go. But the services provided by USPS are a public good and should not be left to billionaires and for-profit private corporations to play games with.
Today, I’m proud to stand with Allston and everyone here, calling for the Postal Service to keep their word to this community.
They must reverse the decision, work to reopen the Austin branch, and restore daily service.
If they intend to follow through with this closure plan, they must give the community a way to have their voice heard, not simply hold a midday Zoom meeting when folks are at work or at school.
The 87,000 Allston-Brighton residents, our neighbors in Fields Corner, folks in Somerville, Grove Hall, and Mission Hill all need and should have an accessible and conveniently located post office to do their business.
So we will not stop advocating for what you deserve.
Again, I believe in the power of pressure, of organizing, and of solidarity.
We will not stop fighting the Republican campaign, because they are the architects of this, to privatize the postal service, and we will not stop fighting until Allston has a post office again.
And now, as someone who comes from a long line of letter carriers, it is my privilege to introduce a man who fights for better service for our friends and neighbors every single day, national business agent for the American Postal Workers Union, Scott Hoffman.
—
Throughout her time in Congress, Congresswoman Pressley has championed for federal resources to support the United States Postal Service and its employees.
- In December 2024, in a House Oversight Committee hearing, Rep. Pressley discussed the essential role that the United States Postal Service (USPS) plays in our communities and questioned USPS Postmaster General Louis DeJoy about the widespread delays and service failures that have severely impacted her constituents in the Massachusetts 7th.
- In October 2024, Rep. Pressley joined postal workers from the American Postal Workers Union (APWU) for a rally in Boston to sound the alarm about the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) substandard performance and service to communities.
- In August 2024, Rep. Pressley joined Senator Markey on a letter urging USPS to re-open postal facilities and improve service, spotlighting a larger statewide problem with postal service in Massachusetts.
- On December 16, 2022, Rep. Pressley joined Reps. Lynch and Raskin in leading their colleagues on a letter urging the extension of COVID-19 workers’ compensation benefits for postal workers.
- On February 25, 2021, Rep. Pressley called for postal banking to advance racial and economic justice during a House Committee on Oversight hearing.
- On February 19, 2021, Rep. Pressley urged President Biden in a letter to replace Postmaster General Louis DeJoy and appoint a diverse United States Postal Service Board of Governors.
- On August 22, 2020, Rep. Pressley delivered remarks on the House floor slamming Republican attacks on the United States Postal Service and shared constituent stories.
- On August 21, 2020, Rep. Pressley and Rep. Payne lead their colleagues in a letter pushing party leadership to stand firm on postal service funding.
- On August 25, 2020, Rep. Pressley questioned Postmaster General Louis DeJoy and the United States Postal Service Board of Governors Chairman Robert Duncan about the harmful impact policy changes at USPS had on the workforce during a House Committee on Oversight hearing.

Pappas Meets with NH CAP Leaders on Rising Energy Costs and LIHEAP
Yesterday Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) hosted a roundtable with leaders of New Hampshire Community Action Partnership agencies for a discussion on the impact of rising energy costs on Granite Staters and the importance of the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).
New Hampshire households could pay $2,300 for home heating oil this winter because of President Trump’s war with Iran, a 31% increase. The cost of groceries rose 2.9 percent overall this year, and families paid $310 more for food during President Trump's first year in office compared to 2024. In total, American families have spent over $3,800 more on goods and services since President Trump took office.
“Electricity prices are up, natural gas and home heating oil prices are up, and diesel fuel is hitting record highs. Granite Staters don’t need federal data to tell them this: they are feeling it with every electric and gas bill. As we enter the colder months, tackling the rising cost of energy could not be more urgent,” said Congressman Pappas. “My new legislation would lower energy costs by increasing federal support for heating assistance, expanding eligibility to more families, and lowering gas and diesel costs. I will continue fighting to lower costs for families and put more money back in their pockets.”
Pappas recently introduced three new bills to lower energy costs.
The LIHEAP Act would expand the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), one of the most successful programs aimed at reducing energy costs for working families.
The American Homes First Act would increase funding for LIHEAP by redirecting $1 billion from President Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ slush fund.
The Consumer Fuel Prices Relief Act would provide federal fuel tax relief until the end of September 2027 by pausing the gas tax, the diesel tax, and the aviation fuel tax, while ensuring the benefit is immediately passed on to consumers in full. The legislation builds on his bicameral Gas Prices Relief Act of 2026, introduced in March, which would have suspended the federal gas tax through October 1, 2026. The legislation safeguards and maintains funding for roads, bridges, and gas spill remediation, and holds corporations accountable if they fail to pass along savings to individual consumers.
Background:
LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 households in New Hampshire, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff and President Trump’s repeated efforts to fully defund the program have put this assistance at risk. 
In September 2026, Pappas led 116 of his Congressional colleagues across the aisle in urging for LIHEAP funds to be delivered to states as soon as possible, and no later than November 1st. He previously led 89 of his Congressional colleagues in calling for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025, and has repeatedly led bipartisan calls for the Trump administration to distribute LIHEAP funds in a timely manner.
Pappas is a fierce advocate for efforts that lower energy costs for Granite Staters and programs that help low-income families pay their bills. He has previously introduced, cosponsored, or called for the passage of the following legislation:
- Pappas leads the bipartisan Energy Burden Tax Credit Act, which would provide a refundable tax credit to families struggling with high energy costs, saving households hundreds of dollars a year on energy.
- Pappas leads the bipartisanInvesting in State Energy Act, which would ensure funds from the Weatherization Assistance Program and State Energy Program are distributed without delay to state agencies and local partners that implement these cost-saving energy initiatives.
- Pappas leads the bipartisan Transmission Facilitation Program Reauthorization Act, which would reauthorize funding for DOE’s program providing states and municipalities with federal support for projects developing new transmission lines or upgrading existing transmission lines, helping accelerate project timelines and increase grid capacity.
- Pappas leads the Heroes Home Energy Savings Act, which would reauthorize and increase funding for the Weatherization Assistance Program Enhancement and Innovation Grant to spur innovation in weatherization and provide active-duty and reserve military families with grants to help lower their energy costs.
- Pappas leads the bipartisan Bolstering Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve Act, which would require the Department of Energy (DOE) to conduct a long-range strategic review of the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve (NEHHOR) and report to Congress on opportunities to strengthen it.
- He supports the bipartisan Banning Oil Exports to Foreign Adversaries Act, which would prohibit the sale or export of our nation’s Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) to foreign adversaries including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, closing a dangerous loophole that threatens U.S. energy and national security
- He supports the Energy Independence and Affordability Act, which would reinstate clean energy tax credits established by the Inflation Reduction Actand repealed by Republicans last year. These credits would help individuals, families, small businesses, and manufacturers save money on clean energy, including purchasing clean vehicles or making upgrades such as installing rooftop solar.
- He supports the bipartisan Weatherization Enhancement and Readiness Act of 2025, which would reauthorize and improve the Weatherization Assistance Program and guarantee the program can continue to provide weatherization services to tens of thousands of homes every year, saving households hundreds on their energy costs.
- He supports the bipartisan LIHEAP Staffing Support Act, which would set a minimum staffing level within HHS to administer LIHEAP.

Dân Biểu Derek Trần giới thiệu dự luật giảm chi phí nhà ở cho các gia đình Nam California
Dự luật mới đề nghị khoản tín dụng thuế dành riêng cho người thuê nhà nhằm giảm gánh nặng trước chi phí sinh hoạt ngày càng tăng tại California
WASHINGTON, DC – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) giới thiệu Dự Luật Hỗ Trợ Chi Phí Sinh Hoạt Nhà Ở cho Người Thuê Nhà (COST) Act, để hỗ trợ cư dân tại Nam California đang phải đối mặt với chi phí nhà ở ngày càng tăng. Dự luật thiết lập các khoản tín dụng thuế dành cho người thuê nhà, tiếp nối nỗ lực của Dân Biểu Derek nhằm giúp người dân có thêm cơ hội tiếp cận nhà ở với chi phí hợp lý.
“Chi phí nhà ở trên cả nước, đặc biệt tại Nam California, đã tăng đến mức báo động. Nhiều gia đình phải chật vật mới đủ tiền trả tiền thuê nhà, chưa nói đến việc tiết kiệm cho tương lai,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Dự luật này sẽ mang lại sự hỗ trợ thiết thực và kịp thời cho những người thuê nhà đang gặp khó khăn, giúp họ trang trải tiền thuê nhà, có thêm ngân sách cho các chi phí sinh hoạt hằng ngày, hoặc thậm chí dành dụm để mua nhà. Tôi tự hào dẫn đầu nỗ lực này vì các gia đình khắp nước Mỹ.”
Các gia đình tại Nam California phải đối mặt với mức chi phí nhà ở thuộc hàng cao nhất cả nước. Tại Orange County, tiền thuê nhà trung bình hiện vượt $3,200 mỗi tháng, tăng gần 40% kể từ năm 2017.
Dự luật đề nghị một khoản tín dụng thuế hoàn lại ở mức căn bản 8% dành cho các gia đình có tổng thu nhập từ $150,000 trở xuống, với mức hỗ trợ tối đa $333 mỗi tháng cho mỗi gia đình, tương đương $4,000 mỗi năm. Riêng tại Địa Hạt 45 của California, hơn 75,000 gia đình có thể được hưởng lợi từ chính sách này.
Trong khi những giải pháp khác nhằm giảm chi phí nhà ở có thể cần nhiều thời gian để thực hiện, dự luật này sẽ trực tiếp giúp người thuê nhà có thêm tiền để trang trải thực phẩm, thuốc men, chi phí chăm sóc trẻ em, và các nhu cầu thiết yếu khác.
Nỗ lực lập pháp này tiếp nối những hoạt động của Dân Biểu Derek Trần nhằm giải quyết vấn đề nhà ở trong khu vực:
- Dân Biểu Derek Trần đã vận động thành công $250,000 ngân sách liên bang để hỗ trợ xây dựng 2,700 căn nhà ở giá phải chăng lâu dài khắp Orange County.
- Dân Biểu Derek đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật Saving the American Dream Act, nhằm thành lập một lực lượng đặc nhiệm liên cơ quan để giải quyết cuộc khủng hoảng nhà ở, và Dự Luật Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act, hỗ trợ tài chính cho việc xây dựng thêm các khu nhà ở nhiều căn.
- Ngoài ra, Dân Biểu Derek đã bỏ phiếu ủng hộ Dự Luật 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, được ký thành luật vào Tháng Bảy, 2026, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng nhà ở và giảm bớt các thủ tục hành chính không cần thiết.
Toàn văn dự luật có thể được xem TẠI ĐÂY.

Washington, D.C. — Rep. Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, demanded answers from Jared Kushner, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Affinity Partners, on the apparent conflict of interest regarding the hundreds of millions of dollars his corporation has invested in Israeli firm Phoenix Financial, which is invested in Israeli military companies. Kushner simultaneously has a special envoy role in President Trump’s Middle East conflict, serving as a key envoy in the region; a status which allows him to dodge financial disclosure requirements.
“Jared Kushner is helping negotiate Middle East policy for his father-in-law, even as his firm is the top investor in Phoenix Financial. Phoenix Financial holds up to $456 million in companies that supply Israel’s military, including its largest arms manufacturer. Kushner’s apparent conflicts of interest throughout the region pose serious security threats, which must be investigated,” said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.
In the letter to Jared Kushner, Ranking Member Robert Garcia wrote, “Oversight Democrats are investigating the unprecedented and dangerous ways in which President Trump and his family have profited directly from their access to power. Public reporting has revealed that while you have been acting as a key envoy in the Middle East, including a purported attempt to negotiate a ceasefire to end the conflict in Gaza, your firm, Affinity Partners, is the largest shareholder in an Israeli company with more than $456 million invested in nine companies that supply Israel’s military, including its largest arms manufacturer. Your dual role as your father-in-law’s Middle East and Gaza negotiator while investing in a company that makes profits investing in arms manufacturing presents significant conflicts of interest, all while you avoid disclosing your financial entanglements to Congress or the American people. Since you continue to conduct foreign policy on behalf of the Trump Administration while having raised billions of dollars in capital provided to Affinity Partners by Gulf monarchies, I request detailed information about your business dealings in the Middle East to understand whether your significant financial gains have come at the cost of Americans’ safety and security.”
In March 2026, Ranking Member Robert Garcia demanded answers from the White House following reports that Jared Kushner had been soliciting billions of dollars from Middle Eastern state sovereign wealth funds for his private equity firm, Affinity Partners, while simultaneously co-leading the Trump Administration’s negotiations in the Middle East.
In August 2025, Ranking Member Garcia sent letters to President Trump’s son-in-law, Michael Boulos, his associate James Frangi, and Saudi businessman Abdulelah Allam following reports that Mr. Boulos received $100,000 for leveraging his ties to President Trump to help Mr. Allam recover assets seized by the Saudi government. This letter was part of the Oversight Democrats’ broader oversight of Trump’s family members, including Jared Kushner, whose private equity firm, Affinity Partners, received billions in foreign funding from the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia shortly after Kushner left the White House following the first Trump Administration.
In 2024, Ranking Member Garcia and Ranking Member Jamie Raskin urged Chairmen James Comer and Glenn Grothman to hold a hearing regarding Kushner’s apparent influence peddling and quid pro quos for actions he undertook to reshape U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East and beyond, as senior adviser in President Trump’s first Administration, following reports that Kushner was close to finalizing investments in Albania and Serbia and leveraged relationships he built during his time as a senior adviser in his father-in-law’s White House.

Rep. Carson Seeks Answers on Canceled Naturalization Ceremonies
WASHINGTON, DC—This week, Congressman André Carson (IN-07) led 26 Members of Congress in seeking answers from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) about repeated cancelations of naturalization ceremonies.
In Indianapolis, USCIS canceled at least three naturalization ceremonies since July, citing a “lack of candidates.” But field offices report they have pending naturalization applications that are awaiting action from USCIS.
“Citizenship is a life-changing milestone, and people who have spent years following the law deserve a government that honors its commitments,” said Rep. Carson. “Canceling naturalization ceremonies without a clear explanation leaves families in Indianapolis in limbo and undermines trust in the process. These families deserve more than canceled ceremonies and unanswered questions. USCIS must explain these cancellations and ensure eligible applicants can take their oath without unreasonable delay. I will keep pressing this administration for answers and accountability.”
“We are concerned that lawful permanent residents are experiencing delays in the final stages of their naturalization across the country,” the lawmakers state in the letter. “Applicants who have spent years complying with immigration requirements should not face unexplained or unreasonable delays after becoming eligible for citizenship because of the political or ideological whims of a particular administration. These delays prevent lawful permanent residents from fully exercising the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, including voting, obtaining a U.S. passport, pursuing certain employment opportunities, and petitioning for family members. Congress has made it clear that the fair and timely processing of eligible citizenship applicants is a priority.”
Rep. Carson and his colleagues requested a response from USCIS by October 7, 2026, including the number of pending naturalization applications, how long those applications have been pending, and how many applicants have completed naturalization interviews but are still awaiting final decisions.
The full letter is HERE.
###
title: Rep. Carson Seeks Answers on Canceled Naturalization Ceremonies

Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) announced an award of $1.5 million in federal grants for the mansion and outbuildings of the fifth President of the United States, James Monroe. Oak Hill, located in Loudoun County, has been preserved for hundreds of years and provides the local community and visitors access to American history and educational programming. Earlier this year, the Virginia General Assembly approved Governor Spanberger’s budget amendment to designated Oak Hill as a State Park. That amendment was championed by Senator Russet Perry and Delegate John McAuliff.
“Oak Hill is an important part of our history and has survived hundreds of years. This funding will ensure it can continue to live on for generations. I am proud that federal funding will help maintain and preserve this historical landmark. I look forward to seeing people of all ages in our community and across the world visit Oak Hill for many years to come,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanayam.
“For more than two years, we fought in Richmond to make Oak Hill a state park and protect more than 1,200 acres of Loudoun County and President Monroe’s historic home. We got it done, and now the work is making sure Oak Hill has what it needs to thrive for the long term. This $1.5 million in federal funding will help us do that, and I’m grateful to Congressman Subramanyam for securing these resources and being a partner in Oak Hill’s future. I’m looking forward to continuing this work and getting Oak Hill State Park open to the public,” said Senator Russet Perry.
"Oak Hill will be an enormous investment in the quality of life and conservation of Western Loudoun by opening up over 1,200 acres of farm and forestland for recreational use. The new funding secured by Congressman Subramanyam and State budget language provided by Gov. Spanberger ensures this land and history will be treasured by generations to come," said Delegate John McAuliff.
“Oak Hill stands as a powerful reminder of our nation’s founding story, and these grants ensure that story will be preserved for generations to come. We’re grateful to Rep. Subramanyam and our federal partners at the National Park Service for recognizing what this site means – not just to Loudoun County, but to the story of our nation as we mark 250 years of independence,” said Heather Richards, Mid-Atlantic Vice President, The Conservation Fund.
Of the $1.5 million in grants for preservation and restoration, $750k from Save America’s Treasures and $750k from Semiquincentennial grants. View the NPS announcements of funding here and here.
###
title: Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill

Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) announced that the Scio Rural Fire Protection District has received a $1.19 million federal grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency to support firefighter safety and fire prevention. Congresswoman Bynum advocated for the funding by writing a letter to FEMA in support of Scio Rural Fire’s grant application.
“When you call 911, you shouldn’t have to wonder if there are enough firefighters to answer,” said Rep. Bynum. “This $1.19 million is a big deal for Scio, Jefferson, and the communities they serve. It means more support for the people running toward emergencies and a stronger response when our neighbors need help most. This is exactly what bringing federal dollars home should look like.”
"These grants are a significant opportunity and an important first step in building the capacity our Fire & Life Safety Division needs," said Albany Fire Chief Chris LaBelle. "A community our size, with the growth and unique industries we have, requires a more proactive approach to risk reduction. This position moves us in that direction and supports our mission to Prevent and Protect from Harm."
"Redmond Fire & Rescue would like to thank Senators Merkley and Wyden and Congresswoman Bynum for their support,” said Redmond Fire Chief Ryan Herrera. "With members of our organization having navigated a past cancer diagnosis, and with the recent passing of Firefighter/Paramedic Michael Kienzle from a Line-of-Duty cancer, this funding marks another meaningful step forward in our commitment to carcinogen reduction and improving the long-term health and safety of our firefighters."
"As costs continue to rise faster than available revenue, small fire districts like ours face difficult choices about how to best use limited resources. Recruiting, training, and retaining volunteer firefighters can too often be delayed as we focus on meeting the immediate costs of providing emergency services,” said Scio Fire Chief Kevin White. "This grant is an important investment in the future of our department and our community. It will strengthen our efforts to recruit and retain volunteers, grow our membership, and ensure we have the people and resources needed to provide the high-quality emergency services our community depends on. We are grateful for this support and the opportunity to build a stronger, more sustainable fire department."
FEMA awarded the funding through its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant Program, which helps fire departments hire additional firefighters and strengthen recruitment and retention efforts.
FEMA also issued funding under the SAFER Grant Program to the following areas:
- More than $2.3 million to Boise Fire Department in Boise, Idaho
- More than $1.7 million to South Kitsap Fire and Rescue in Port Orchard, Washington.
- More than $1.7 million to Spokane County Fire District 9 in Mead, Washington.
- More than $1.1 million to Umatilla Rural Fire Protection District in Umatilla, Oregon.
- $1 million to North Whidbey Fire and Rescue in Oak Harbor, Washington.
###
title: Bynum Secures Over One Million for Scio Rural Fire

Rep. Gillen Announces More Than $500,000 in New Federal Funding for Nassau County Fire Departments
GARDEN CITY, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) announced that four fire departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District have been awarded more than $500,000 total in federal funding for improved equipment, training and recruitment. Three departments were awarded Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG), including the Inwood Fire Department for emergency vehicle acquisition as well as the Bellerose Terrace Fire Department and the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department for operations and safety. Stewart Manor Village received funding through the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant to help recruit and retain more volunteer firefighters.
“Firefighters across Long Island put their lives on the line every day to protect our families and communities. They should have the resources of a modern firefighting force,” said Rep. Gillen. “I’m proud to help secure more than $500,000 in federal funding for Nassau County fire departments to support critical equipment, vehicle and recruitment needs. I will continue working with our local fire departments to deliver federal dollars and ensure they have the tools and support they need to keep our communities safe.”
“The chiefs, officers and members of the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department thank Congresswoman Gillen very much,” said Chief Joseph McHugh, Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department. “This will help keep our members safe and take a big financial burden off of us.”
- The Inwood Fire Department received $220,476 through the AFG program to assist with the purchase of new vehicles for the department.
- The Stewart Manor Village Fire Department received $119,500 through the SAFER program to help recruit and retain trained volunteer firefighters.
- The Bellerose Terrace Fire District received $96,666 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.
- Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department received $72,857 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.
During the FY25 grant application process, Rep. Gillen urged all departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District to apply for funding through the AFG and SAFER programs and wrote letters of support. As a member of the bipartisan Congressional Fire Services Caucus, Rep. Gillen has also pushed for increased funding for the AFG and SAFER Programs to help ensure Long Island fire departments have the federal resources to improve emergency response and support their firefighters.
The AFG program, administered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), provides funding to local fire departments to help obtain needed equipment, protective gear, vehicles and training. The SAFER grant is a federal program administered by FEMA that provides direct funding to local fire departments and volunteer firefighter organizations to help increase or maintain the number of trained firefighters.
###
title: Rep. Gillen Announces More Than $500,000 in New Federal Funding for Nassau County Fire Departments

Deluzio Kicks Off October Town Hall Tour in Penn Hills, PA
PENN HILLS, PA – Yesterday, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) kicked off his October Town Hall Tour with an event open to the public and the press in Penn Hills, Pennsylvania. A large group of Western Pennsylvanians joined him for the first stop of the Town Hall Tour in Pennsylvania’s 17th District.
The event covered a wide range of topics, including corruption, AI, and the cost of living. Constituents had an opportunity to speak directly with their elected representative in Congress, share their opinions, and ask questions. Congressman Deluzio also provided updates from his work down in Washington.
“A lot has happened down in Washington this year, and it is good to be home to hear from the people that Congress’s work impacts the most,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Folks in Penn Hills want to know how we can fight the cost-of-living crisis, end the President’s reckless war in Iran, and restore the American Dream right here in Western Pennsylvania. I’m excited to keep the conversation going and hear from the good people of Carnegie and Beaver Falls next."
Congressman Deluzio has attended more than twenty similar open Q&A events during the 119th Congress (2025-2026). Deluzio’s Town Hall Tour will stop next in Carnegie on Tuesday, October 13th at 5:30pm and in Beaver Falls on Saturday, October 17th at 2:00pm.
Photos are available here.

Neal, Wyden Object to Treasury’s Proposed Boost for Private School Tax Credits
New provision continues Trump’s pattern of ignoring clear Congressional mandates in an effort to benefit the wealthy and well-connected
WASHINGTON, DC— House Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) today objected to the Treasury Department’s recently issued proposed regulations on new Internal Revenue Code section 25F that further Republican attempts to undermine public school systems by directing taxpayer money toward private and religious schools.
In a letter to Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, Ranking Members Neal and Wyden called out the Administration’s actions as a blatant attempt to circumvent the clear rules established by Congress to funnel even more taxpayer funds away from public education and use it to subsidize the private school education of children from wealthy families. Treasury’s baseless interpretation of federal statute would allow married couples filing jointly to potentially claim double the credit that is authorized under the law.
“This interpretation is wildly inconsistent with the longstanding treatment of other provisions that use identical or near-identical language,” Neal and Wyden wrote. “This throws doubt upon Treasury’s interpretation of many provisions of the Code, creates a great deal of uncertainty in the administration of our tax laws, and could balloon the deficit,” Neal and Wyden noted, adding that it could increase the cost of the credit by an additional $150 billion over the next decade.
The Democratic Committee leaders closed by demanding the Administration provide written answers and explanations to how the new interpretation of the law will impact taxpayers, how it came to be and was coordinated internally, which other tax provisions taxpayers might take a return position that is different from previously listed guidance based on new interpretations, and other pressing matters.
Read the full letter to Secretary Bessent HERE.
###
title: Neal, Wyden Object to Treasury’s Proposed Boost for Private School Tax Credits

Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military
WASHINGTON — On Monday, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07), a 25-year Army veteran, introduced the Learning Effective Strategies and Systems Optimization for National Security (LESSONS) from Ukraine Act, legislation requiring the Pentagon to study and apply lessons from Ukraine’s battlefield innovations to U.S. military doctrine and training.
“During my visit to Ukraine, I saw firsthand how the Ukrainians are rapidly adapting to a battlefield where drones and electronic warfare are changing how wars are fought,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will make sure our military learns from what Ukraine has discovered through years of defending itself against Putin’s invasion, from countering drone swarms and operating through electronic warfare to sustaining weapons production under attack. We need to put those lessons to work to strengthen our own military, protect our servicemembers, and ensure we are prepared to deter aggression across the world.”
“Ukraine’s defense against Russia has shown just how rapidly modern warfare is evolving. I saw that firsthand during my trip to Ukraine last month, where drones, electronic warfare, cyber operations, and defense manufacturing are reshaping the battlefield in real time,” said Vindman. "As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our military must constantly learn, adapt, and innovate to maintain our strategic advantage and protect our service members. The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will ensure the Department of Defense learns from Ukraine’s hard-earned experience and applies those lessons to our doctrine, training, and capabilities so our military is prepared for the threats of tomorrow.”
The LESSONS from Ukraine Act would require the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress within 120 days on lessons the U.S. military can draw from the Russia-Ukraine War, including the use of drones and other unmanned systems, electronic and cyber warfare, air defense, operations without GPS or satellite communications, battlefield medicine, and Ukraine’s efforts to expand and decentralize weapons production. The Pentagon would also be required to develop a plan and timetable for incorporating those lessons into U.S. military doctrine and training. Congressman Krishnamoorthi first announced the legislation following an August official visit to Ukraine, where he visited a Ukrainian drone production facility and met with officials about the battlefield and Ukraine’s rapidly evolving defense innovations.
The text of the legislation is available here.
title: Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military

Hoyer, Comptroller Lierman Visit Nonprofit Organizations Across Maryland's Fifth Congressional District
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) and Maryland Comptroller Brooke E. Lierman visited nonprofit organizations in Prince George's and Charles Counties to discuss each group's commitment to serving Southern Marylanders within their communities.
"Maryland's Fifth Congressional District is home to a multitude of nonprofit organizations that deliver critical resources and create opportunities for the region. From Westbrook Horse Farm to LifeStyles of Maryland, each advocate and organization we met with has an invaluable role in shaping the lives of Marylanders. I enjoyed seeing their work up close and discussing their contributions to our communities. I thank each organization for welcoming us, and I will continue to support their efforts during the remainder of my term in Congresss," said Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05).
“The three organizations we visited – all nonprofits but each doing work in its own way - play an essential role in strengthening our communities, supporting Marylanders in need, and creating opportunities for individuals to build better futures,” said Comptroller Brooke E. Lierman. “I am grateful for the dedicated people behind these organizations and the difference they make across our state. From supporting young people to helping individuals find stable housing, to supporting economic development and job creation, the work of these organizations makes Maryland a better place for everyone.” 
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with Brian Westbrook and his father, Roy Westbrook at the Westbrook Farm.
Starting off in Prince George's County, Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman visited the Westbrook Horse Farm in Upper Marlboro, Maryland. Owned and operated by Brian Westbrook, former NFL player and founder of The Brian Westbrook Foundation, the farm's programming provides hands-on skills training, riding lessons, and mentorship for youth to teach them responsibility and instill a greater sense of purpose in their lives. Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman received a tour of the farm and learned more about the community outreach initiatives Westbrook plans to implement in the near future.
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with board members of the
Charles County Military Alliance Council.
Next, Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman met with board members of the Charles County Military Alliance Council for a roundtable discussion. The group discussed strategy and ongoing investments to connect residents and local businesses with opportunities to support defense activities and boost the economy. Congressman Hoyer and the Comptroller continue working to maintain an effective relationship between military facilities, elected officials, and the greater Southern Maryland community.
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with LifeStyles CEO Sandy Washington and
Support Staff at the LifeStyles Headquarters in LaPlata, Maryland.
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman spent the rest of their afternoon at the LifeStyles Inc. headquarters in LaPlata, Maryland to receive an update on the around-the-clock support services provided at this location. During their tour, LifeStyles CEO Sandy Washington highlighted their work to deliver food, clothing, and housing assistance and workforce training for nearly 3 decades. LifeStyles of Maryland has 8 offices and distribution centers across the state to help meet the needs of underserved communities in the region.
title: Hoyer, Comptroller Lierman Visit Nonprofit Organizations Across Maryland's Fifth Congressional District

Pou Statement On Release of Martin Soto from ICE Detention
PATERSON, NJ – Tonight, U.S. Representative Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) celebrated the release of Martin Soto, a resident of the Ninth Congressional District who was held in ICE custody for several months.
“I am so overjoyed that Martin Soto is finally freed from ICE custody,” stated Rep. Nellie Pou, a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security. “Martin was undeniably targeted and mistreated, being moved from Delaney Hall to the Elizabeth Detention Center and held in solitary confinement. For months my office has been pushing ICE to release Martin and tonight justice is finally being done. It should have happened months ago. ICE remains out of control in our state and we must continue to oppose its rampant abuses. But tonight we can be grateful the hard work from so many paid off and Martin is being reunited with his family.”
Initially detained in Newark, Martin Soto was moved to the Elizabeth Detention Center in retaliation for his role in the hunger and labor strike to highlight the deplorable conditions at Delaney Hall. There, Martin experienced harsh retribution including isolation.
Rep. Pou and her staff have been working with the Soto family, advocates, and other elected officials to obtain his release for months.
“I am so happy Martin is finally being released from ICE custody,” said Gabby Soto, wife of Martin Soto. “I want to thank Congresswoman Nellie Pou for all of her work on his case. Her efforts were critical to us finally reaching this moment.”
###
title: Pou Statement On Release of Martin Soto from ICE Detention

text:
RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Leads Los Angeles Delegation and Entertainment Unions in Push for National Film Tax Credit
Bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act brings production jobs back to the U.S.
Levels international playing field against 65 countries that offer incentives America does not match
Above: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.
GLENDALE, CA – Today, October 6, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) led Members of the Los Angeles congressional delegation, and the major unions representing film and television workers at the Alex Theatre in a new push for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. This bipartisan legislation creates a national film tax credit on qualified labor expenses to bring production jobs back home.
A recording of the rally can be found here and here.
For decades, the United States has offered no national filming incentive, leaving American crews to compete against roughly 65 countries that do. The result has been hundreds of thousands of lost jobs for the drivers, grips, electricians, carpenters, caterers, and crew members.
WHAT THE BILL DOES:
- A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.
- Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.
- Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.
- Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.
- Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.
- A one-pager with more details can be found here.
“When a production leaves this country, the stars still work. The crew is who gets left behind,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “65 countries offer incentives we don’t match, and no single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. Our bipartisan bill is built on labor costs, which means it only pays off when American workers get hired. These are good paying union jobs with benefits and pensions, and I won’t stop fighting until they come home.”
“You won’t see the carpenters, electricians and camera crews on screen, but they are the backbone of the film industry,” said Congresswoman Linda T. Sánchez (CA-38). “Many live in my district and have watched their jobs move overseas as other countries use incentives to lure production away. Our bipartisan bill will level the playing field to bring good-paying union jobs back to Southern California and keep them here.”
"Southern California has been the heart of America’s film and television industry, but today, too many productions are leaving the United States for countries offering better incentives," said Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28). "That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which would provide a long-overdue federal tax credit to incentivize production here in the United States. Our creative workforce is the backbone of this industry. It's time we must invest in them and bring American film and television production back home.”
“Movie magic is central to the California story, and we need to keep it that way,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33). “Our state is losing good-paying, union jobs because filming in this country has become far too expensive. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act will bring jobs back to America, boost wages for workers and keep productions at home.”
“California is the heart of film and television production, in large part because of the workers and technicians who bring the magic to life,” said Representative Tran (CA-45). “Yet the U.S. is rapidly losing jobs in this industry to competitors overseas. When productions relocate outside the U.S., it’s the American-based crews that suffer the most. California’s workforce deserves better. This bill incentivizes American-based productions, strengthens California’s production workforce, and brings jobs back to the U.S.—where they belong.”
“Southern California is the birthplace of the modern film and television industry. From the movies and television shows that have entertained audiences around the world to the hardworking people behind them, this industry is a vital part of our community and economy,” said Congressman Lieu (CA-36). “We can’t let the United States’ film industry lose ground to foreign competitors. I am pleased to be an original co-sponsor of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. It’s time to strengthen our domestic film industry and protect American jobs.”
“American performers and entertainment workers should not have to leave the country to find work in an industry that was built here. Film and television are more than entertainment — they are a major American industry that supports hundreds of thousands of good-paying union jobs and generates significant economic activity in communities across the country. For decades, foreign governments have recognized the economic value of production and successfully used incentives to attract these jobs overseas. States across the country have shown what targeted incentives can do to attract and retain production, and a federal incentive would build on those efforts and give the United States a stronger tool to compete. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is an investment in American workers, American industry and American communities. SAG-AFTRA is proud to stand with Congresswoman Friedman and our labor partners in support of this important legislation,” said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.
“The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will benefit entertainment industry workers, as well as the supporting businesses and local economies that rely on a robust domestic entertainment industry. Lawmakers have an opportunity to invest in an important American industry and preserve middle-class jobs, by passing the first-ever federal film and television tax incentive program,” said WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta.
"Let’s not overthink this. The world is a complicated place, but this legislation is a no-brainer. It's going to get people back to work, and everyone just wants an opportunity to work in the industry they love in this country. Everyone will benefit from this – Republicans, Democrats, workers, audiences -- because our industry touches everyone," said Mike Farah, an Emmy-winning producer and a President of the Producers Guild of America.
“I’ve worked aggressively with labor and entertainment industry leaders, and together we've already expanded state-level tax incentives and reduced filming fees locally. A federal tax credit is critical so our local incentives remain competitive with countries that offer larger benefits and have drawn productions out of the United States,” said Mayor Bass. “I want to thank the bipartisan leadership of Representatives Laura Friedman, Brian Jack, Linda Sánchez, and Nathaniel Moran and Senators Adam Schiff and Tim Scott for understanding the importance of investing in an industry that is so critical to Los Angeles and the country. As a former Member of Congress, I'll continue leveraging my relationships in Washington to ensure this bill is passed into law.”
U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (CA-30) was joined by Senator Adam Schiff (CA), U.S. Representatives Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Pete Aguilar (CA-33), Ted Lieu (CA-36), David Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45), Glendale Mayor Ardy Kassakhian, IATSE International Vice President and Director of the Motion Picture and Television Department Mike Miller, SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta, DGA Associate National Executive Director and Western Executive Director Rebecca Rhine, Teamsters At-Large Vice President and Motion Picture Division Director Lindsay Dougherty, LiUNA Business Manager Alex Aguilar, Jr., and producer and three-time Emmy winner Mike Farah.
Below: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.
###
title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Leads Los Angeles Delegation and Entertainment Unions in Push for National Film Tax Credit

Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett (TX-30) sent a letter to Governor Greg Abbott, Attorney General Ken Paxton, and Education Commissioner Mike Morath demanding answers and accountability over the use of excessive force against children in Texas public schools.
“Texas is failing our kids. Our children deserve to go to school in an environment that fosters learning and growth, not environments where ordinary student behavior can end with a child in handcuffs, hogtied, shocked with a Taser, or pepper-sprayed.”
Crockett expressed concern regarding the expansive presence of police in school, putting Texas students in unnecessary contact with the criminal system, further opening the door to the school-to-prison pipeline.
In her letter, Crockett highlights how officers using excessive force to respond to student behavior could ordinarily be addressed through school discipline. The letter cites a New York Times investigation documenting more than 2,600 school-based use-of-force incidents across Texas from January 2022 through December 2025.
Crockett is demanding answers regarding police involvement in routine student discipline, incident reporting, accountability for police misconduct, and potential changes to state law training.
“The number of “incidents” is alarming. Our kiddos should not be treated like criminals. They are the future of this country, and we owe it to them to protect them from cruel and abusive behavior. I am urging our Texas leaders to exercise immediate oversight and ensure accountability for these horrific reported actions. This is unacceptable, and it has to stop.”
The full letter can be found here.
title: Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools

Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce Disaster Declaration from U.S. Small Business Administration for Homeowners, Renters, and Businesses Impacted by September Flooding
Declaration Enables Impacted Individuals, Families, Businesses, and Nonprofits to Apply for Low-Interest Loans to Aid in Their Recovery
Hartford, CT – Today, members of the Connecticut Congressional delegation joined Governor Ned Lamont to announce a disaster declaration from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) for Fairfield County and the contiguous counties of New Haven County and Litchfield County in response to the flash flooding event that impacted the region on September 13, 2026. The approved declaration means that homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits in the impacted counties can apply for low-interest loans from the SBA to aid in their recovery.
“This declaration makes low-interest loans available to homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits so they can recover and rebound from these flash floods,” Governor Lamont said. “I am glad that we’ve been able to secure this funding and encourage anyone who was impacted by this storm to look into this assistance and determine whether it can help you in the recovery process.”
“As communities continue to recover from severe flooding that hit our state last month, I am glad that the Small Business Administration granted our request for a disaster declaration," said Congressman John B. Larson. "This declaration is a crucial step forward, so small businesses, local organizations, and homeowners can get the help they need to repair and rebuild after incurring damage—including in Litchfield County. Our delegation will keep working with the governor and state leaders to ensure the federal government is responsive to the towns and cities that were impacted by this storm.”
“This disaster declaration is a strong step toward bringing federal aid to Connecticut following severe floods last month. This step allows Connecticut state agencies to work with federal partners like the SBA to continue recovery efforts and potentially unlock more federal assistance to rebuild local businesses. I am grateful to the SBA for their swift response to Governor Lamont and our delegation’s request,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal.
“Connecticut communities were hit hard on September 13 by sudden and intense flooding. I encourage all small business owners in the counties covered by this disaster declaration to take advantage of the available assistance from the Small Business Administration,” said Congressman Joe Courtney.
“Extreme weather events like flash flooding are damaging our communities more often and more unexpectedly. I am glad that federal support is on its way through this SBA disaster declaration for the businesses, residents, and communities that were impacted by devastating flash floods last month. I will continue to fight for federal resources so that Connecticut has the support necessary rebuild after disasters like this one,” said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro.
“I’m glad the federal government is stepping up to assist Connecticut residents and businesses, especially those in Fairfield County, in recovering from last month’s flooding. I encourage anyone whose residence or business was impacted by the severe weather to look into these resources. I will continue fighting alongside the rest of Connecticut’s Congressional delegation to bring home the federal support our constituents need to rebound,” said Congressman Jim Himes.
“Extreme weather continues to impact our state. I am pleased to see the U.S. Small Business Administration approve federal assistance for parts of the Fifth District and our state. These federal resources will help alleviate the financial losses of business leaders and homeowners from the recent flooding,” said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes.
The following groups may be eligible for low-interest SBA disaster loans:
- Homeowners: Up to $500,000 to repair their primary residence.
- Homeowners and renters: Up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.
- Business owners: Up to $2,000,000 for the replacement of real property, inventories, machinery, equipment, and other physical losses.
- Businesses and nonprofits: Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2,000,000 to provide necessary working capital until normal operations resume after a disaster.
“We know there are people with uninsured losses. These low-interest SBA loans are a means for people to rebuild and recover from the flooding. Additionally, our Volunteer Organizations Active in Disaster—independent faith-based and nonprofit groups—remain engaged in helping people needing cleanup,” saidConnecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection Commissioner Ronnell A. Higgins.
How to apply for low-interest SBA disaster loans
Under this declaration, the application deadline for physical damage loans is December 1, 2026, and the application deadline for economic injury loans is July 2, 2027.
Applications may be submitted to the SBA through the following methods:
- In-person: A temporary, in-person SBA Disaster Loan Outreach Center will open at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center at 999 Broad Street in Bridgeport beginning October 7, 2026.
  - It will operate Mondays through Fridays from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Saturdays from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; and it will be closed on Sundays.
  - Due to prior engagements, it will have adjusted hours of 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on October 9, 2026; and 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on October 20 and 21, 2026.
  - It will be closed on October 12, 2026, due to the Columbus Day holiday.
  - It is expected to permanently close at 4:00 p.m. on October 21, 2026.
- Online: The MySBA Loan Portal at provides applicants with the ability submit applications online, view loan details, check balances, make payments, and access statements.
For further assistance, applicants can contact the SBA’s Customer Service Center by email at disastercustomerservice@sba.gov or by phone at 1-800-659-2955. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands
The proposed revision of the 2005 Travel Management Rule poses serious risk to conservation and safety on public lands
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 6, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Under Secretary Michael Boren and U.S. Forest Service (USFS) Chief Tom Schultz strongly opposing the Administration’s proposed rule expanding vehicle access to public lands and trails that are already facing maintenance backlogs. Vasquez was joined by 28 of his House and Senate colleagues in his call to keep the 2005 Travel Management Rule in place.
“New Mexicans deserve public lands that are safe and well-managed. Ending the long-established Travel Management Rule would put public safety at risk and open the door to damage that will take generations to undo,” said Vasquez. “Hikers, hunters, and ranchers alike shouldn’t have to worry about more folks driving through the spaces they use for recreation and grazing. Instead of opening more of our public lands to vehicle access in places where access already exists, the Forest Service should focus on maintaining existing trails and roads. This broad reversal is unnecessary."
The USFS and the Bureau of Land Management have separate but similar rules requiring our public land agencies to provide clear, consistent guidance for how public lands are used, including where motorized vehicles, including cars and ATVs, can travel. For those who enjoy our public lands, whether on foot or on wheels, these rules help keep trails open, accessible, and responsibly managed. They also require public input before designating routes, produce Motor Vehicle Use Maps that show visitors where they can go, give rangers clear standards to enforce, and allow exceptions for emergency, military, and law enforcement vehicles.
Changing the 2005 rule, as proposed by USDA, could endanger public safety, reduce quality access to our public lands, and degrade the quality of trails, lands and waters that support our nation’s wildlife and outdoor recreation economy.
The letter demands that any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule preserve the following core principles:
- Maintain the current default of keeping routes and areas closed to motorized use unless expressly designated as open.
- Carry forward criteria that guide local land management decisions and protect critical public land values, including soil, watersheds, vegetation, and wildlife habitat, as well as reduce conflicts between public land uses such as camping, hiking, hunting, and grazing.
- Travel management decisions should continue to be informed by robust public engagement and local input.
- The agencies must retain the ability to protect fish and wildlife habitat, riparian areas, water quality, and cultural resources.
- The agencies should continue to clearly identify where motorized travel is permitted.
- The agencies should consider the long-term cost of properly maintaining, staffing, and administering their transportation system before adding new routes or expanding access.
“This is yet another egregious attack in the systematic dismantling of public lands management of our national forests,” said Paul Sanford, director for equitable access policy advocacy at The Wilderness Society. “Travel management provides the basic guardrails that let hikers, hunters, anglers, and riders share the same forest without chaos; removing those guardrails threatens the freedom of all public lands users to safely enjoy our national forests the way they choose. Paired with the proposed repeal of the Roadless Rule, this destructive agenda sells out future generations’ enjoyment of our forests in order to hand them over for corporate profits.”
“We’re grateful to see Congressional Leaders pushing back on federal agency proposals to gut travel management regulations and prioritize off-road vehicles at the expense of wildlife, cultural sites, desert waterways and other recreationists, proposals that will make visiting Utah’s canyon country worse for everyone,” said Laura Peterson, Senior Attorney at the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance (SUWA). “The Trump Administration’s vision for public lands is not about balance or reasonable access, it is about blanketing landscapes with off-road vehicle routes, transforming quiet, wild places into motorized playgrounds.”
"We stand with Rep. Vasquez and his urgent request to keep the Travel Management Rule intact,” said Taylor Rush, government relations representative at Defenders of Wildlife. "For more than two decades, this rule has protected our cherished wildlife, outdoor recreationists, clean water supply and local communities from the harmful impacts of unmanaged motorized vehicle use. Weakening the framework used to reduce habitat damage and social conflict would result in dangerous degradation of our wild places and wildlife."

title: Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands

LOWELL, MA – Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Congressman Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08) led 24 of their colleagues from Northeastern states in pressing the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran. In their letter, the lawmakers urged the DOE to support an immediate end to the war and prioritize lowering energy costs for the winter, warning that rising prices will force families to choose between heating their homes and paying for basic necessities. 
“Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs,” wrote the lawmakers.
The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year.
In addition to increasing the cost of heating oil, the Trump administration has made or attempted to make heating costs for the upcoming winter even higher by: 
    - Attempting to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.
- Effectively increasing taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.
- Cutting more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families. 
“As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families,” the lawmakers continued. 
“To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP,” the lawmakers concluded. 
The lawmakers were joined by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.); and Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Bill Keating (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Chris Pappas (D-N.H.), Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.).
A copy of the letter sent today can be accessed  HERE.
