Elected leaders who hailed the reopening of the state’s second freestanding birth center earlier this year may have celebrated prematurely.
The Cambridge Health Alliance Birth Center, which closed in March 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic, was scheduled to reopen on July 6 with the aim of welcoming 100 babies in the first year. CHA said the center would serve all patients but have a “special focus on vulnerable and underserved populations who will benefit most from midwifery care and a birth center experience.”
But no deliveries happened this summer, even as supporters of the 2024 maternal health law tried to create new urgency around bolstering access to care and removing healthcare disparities for people of color.
“The Birth Center has been open for prenatal and outpatient visits,” CHA spokesperson David Cecere told the News Service Thursday. “We are anticipating our first delivery this week — they had been on hold as we worked through a leadership transition.”
Cecere said that “unexpected turnover” prompted the center to “hold deliveries until we established a plan to ensure high quality care and an exceptional patient experience.”
A spokesperson for the Department of Public Health, asked whether it was aware of any paused operations or staffing issues, said DPH had called the birth center and was told it was “taking clients.”
CHA has said the reopening would not have been possible without $1 million in state funding, which Cambridge Rep. Marjorie Decker helped secure in the fiscal 2024 budget. The center also received a grant from Beth Israel Lahey Health to help cover training, equipment, and community education and outreach.
The birth center, situated in a Victorian home with three renovated birthing rooms, held an open house on June 17 with more than 200 attendees, according to CHA. Speakers included Decker, U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark, Sen. Sal DiDomenico, Cambridge Mayor Sumbul Siddiqui and Public Health Commissioner Robbie Goldstein.
“Too often we are talking about the closure of maternity services, but today we get to celebrate a spectacular rebirth – and one that I hope will be followed by many more,” Goldstein said in a statement at the time. “Expanding access to community-based, relationship-centered care is key in advancing health equity. The reopening of the CHA Birth Center supports families who deserve more options for culturally responsive maternity care.”
Clark said the reopening was a “signal to women everywhere that we can and will keep making progress on maternal health.”
“We’re going to keep fighting for a healthcare system worthy of every mother in this community and a future worthy of the children who will begin their lives at CHA,” she said.
Michele Helgeson, a member of the Community Coalition for the Cambridge Birth Center, said everything had seemed “very positive” and “very, very upbeat” surrounding the open house. The coalition has met with CHA leaders to advocate for community interests and promote a midwifery model of care.
“There was no indication that there was any reason to stop or pause at that point,” said Helgeson, who added she wants to see CHA conduct community outreach and assure patients about available services at the birth center.
Birth centers are seen as alternatives to hospital deliveries, particularly in low-risk pregnancies. The facilities offer a home-like environment and are staffed by midwives who can provide more personalized care.
The 2024 law removed regulatory barriers to opening freestanding birth centers and created a pathway for certified professional midwives to become licensed. The state started accepting applications for temporary CPM licensure last month, as DPH expects to issue regulations for “standard” licensure in early 2027.
Until the CHA Birth Center returned to the maternal health landscape, Massachusetts was home to only one such freestanding facility in Northampton. But Seven Sisters Midwifery and Community Birth Center faces intense financial pressure due to low reimbursement rates compared to services provided in hospitals, according to owner and clinical director Ginny Miller.
Legislation (S 784) to ensure that certified nurse midwives, certified professional midwives and licensed freestanding birth centers are not paid less than physicians and hospitals delivering the same services has been lodged in the Senate Ways and Means Committee since April.
Kimberly Amsley-Camp was the CHA’s director of midwifery from August 2025 through September 2026, and she managed a staff of 20 certified nurse midwives and nurse practitioners, according to her LinkedIn profile. Working with a “multi-disciplinary” team, Amsley-Camp wrote she “planned and developed reopening of a hospital owned freestanding birth center.”
Amsley-Camp did not respond to a News Service request for comment.
Cecere said consultant and certified nurse midwife Erin Stein is now overseeing “daily operations” of the CHA Birth Center. She’s working alongside Dr. Tara Singh, chief of obstetrics and gynecology, and Allisyn Brady, senior director of OB/GYN.
Helgeson said the coalition wants to meet with CHA leaders and get an update on birth center operations, though she expects that won’t happen until November due to scheduling logistics.
“There is definitely support for the sustainability of the birth center, and that’s really what we’re hoping to achieve in the long run,” Helgeson said. “The opening is important, but we really want it to succeed in the long-term as well.”

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández visitó Vimenti, en el Residencial Ernesto Ramos Antonini en San Juan, donde presentó $1,031,000 en fondos federales que aseguró para desarrollar el Next Generation STEM Learning Lab Accelerator. La iniciativa ampliará las oportunidades de educación STEM para estudiantes de Vimenti School y otras tres escuelas del programa de Escuelas Comunitarias de Servicio Completo.

El Comisionado Residente aseguró los fondos mediante una solicitud de Financiamiento para Proyectos Comunitarios (Community Project Funding) presentada ante el Comité de Asignaciones de la Cámara de Representantes. Los recursos serán canalizados a través de la Oficina de STEM Engagement de la NASA.

“Llevo semanas diciendo que tenemos que priorizar lo básico, y la educación es básica. Nuestros niños fracasan en las materias básicas de español, inglés, ciencias y matemáticas. Este tipo de asignación ayuda a resolver ese problema.”, dijo el Comisionado Residente.

“Agradecemos al comisionado residente, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, y a su equipo, por la confianza depositada en este proyecto. Este logro reafirma nuestro compromiso de seguir identificando y allegando recursos que permitan que más escuelas públicas de Puerto Rico cuenten con espacios, herramientas y oportunidades educativas de excelencia para sus estudiantes, maestros y familias”, expresó Bárbara Rivera Batista, directora ejecutiva de Vimenti.

“Esta subvención confirma lo que puede lograr el modelo de Escuela Comunitaria de Servicio Completo cuando se le brinda el respaldo necesario. Nuestro compromiso es que estos recursos y espacios STEM se queden en cada escuela, sostenidos por sus propios equipos, mucho después de que termine el financiamiento”, indicó Lola Yglesias Quiñones, directora de Expansión de Vimenti.

A través del proyecto, las escuelas podrán desarrollar nuevos espacios educativos con herramientas de robótica y programación, astronomía y ciencias espaciales, ciencias de la Tierra, análisis de datos e inteligencia artificial. La iniciativa también contempla capacitación y acompañamiento para maestros, con el objetivo de fortalecer la capacidad de las escuelas para mantener y ampliar estos programas a largo plazo.

Durante su visita, el Comisionado Residente también sostuvo un conversatorio con estudiantes, familias y maestros sobre el modelo de Vimenti, los resultados que ha alcanzado la organización y la importancia de ampliar el acceso a oportunidades educativas en áreas STEM.

Según datos provistos por Vimenti, durante el año escolar 2023-2024 sus estudiantes alcanzaron un 54% de dominio en matemáticas, frente a un 11% a nivel de Puerto Rico. Entre los estudiantes con discapacidades, el dominio en matemáticas alcanzó un 63%, comparado con tasas de entre 10% y 18% a nivel estatal.

Vimenti atiende a estudiantes y familias mediante un modelo de dos generaciones que integra educación, salud y bienestar, desarrollo laboral, capacidad financiera, emprendimiento y mentoría. De acuerdo con su estudio de impacto de siete años, la organización ha generado cerca de $59 millones en impacto económico mediante sus operaciones y proyecta otros $97 millones asociados a iniciativas futuras.

title: Comisionado Residente entrega más de $1 millón para ampliar educación STEM en San Juan

Reps. Castro, Cisneros Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
WASHINGTON D.C. — Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.
Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most watched and financially successful productions.
El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.
“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country," said Congressman Castro. "Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”
“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”
“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”
“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”
“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen," said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. "Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”
“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”
“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”
Read the full text of the resolution here.
###
title: Reps. Castro, Cisneros Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers

text:
Moore, Bonamici, Frost, Grijalva, and Pocan Blast Regulations Paving the Way for National Voucher Scheme
The Treasury Department recently released regulations on their national voucher scheme, which was established through the Republicans’ Big Ugly Bil (HR 1). That law allowed Americans to receive a tax credit, up to $1,700, for donations to eligible scholarship-granting organizations, including religious schools. These regulations will double the credit amount for married couples. Representatives Gwen Moore (WI-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), and Mark Pocan (WI-02) have introduced HR 9289, the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, which would repeal the H.R .1 voucher scheme.
In states across the country, taxpayer supported voucher programs operate with little oversight and fund private schools who lack civil rights and other protections for students. In Wisconsin, the current voucher program at the state level will cost state taxpayers more than $700 million this year alone. Nearly all the students receiving a voucher in Wisconsin attend private, religious schools. 
Republicans are working to enact and expand this flawed system at the national level. So far, six states have resisted, including Wisconsin. 
“Despite what Republicans claim, these regulations make it clear this voucher scheme is designed to prop up private schools– at the expense of our public schools. Public schools serve every student who walks through its doors. Our tax dollars should not be funneled to schools that can discriminate against students who try to enroll. That is why I am proud to spearhead legislation to reverse this voucher scheme,” said Representative Gwen Moore (WI-04).
"The Treasury Department's school voucher regulations clearly demonstrate that the Trump administration has no interest in supporting public schools or the students they serve," said Representative Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01). "Diverting public resources into private schools - including religious schools -  that can pick and choose which students they enroll is unjust and irresponsible. Alarmingly, the regulations actually prohibit states from implementing additional oversight, reporting, accountability, or civil rights protections. The vast majority of students in this country attend public schools. We should be strengthening public education, not destroying it."
“This voucher scheme sends public money to private schools with less accountability for how that money is spent," said Representative Maxwell Frost (FL-10)."We’ve already seen the consequences in Florida, where the state struggled to track hundreds of millions of dollars in voucher funds and cases of fraud surfaced. Now the Treasury Department and Trump administration want to take that same model nationwide. We shouldn’t be making it easier to lose track of taxpayer dollars; we should be making sure every dollar is accountable to the public.” 
“Arizona’s fraud-ridden school voucher program should serve as a warning to the rest of the country. Instead, the Trump Administration is moving full steam ahead with a national voucher scheme while failing to include even basic safeguards to prevent taxpayer dollars from being wasted or abused. Arizona has already seen where this road leads. That’s why Congress must act to ensure federal taxpayer dollars strengthen the public schools that serve the overwhelming majority of America’s children, not subsidize privatization schemes rife with fraud,” said Representative Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).
“As a proud public school graduate, I know firsthand the value and importance of our public education system,” said Representative Mark Pocan (WI-02). “Fixing this blatant abuse of the tax system will help kids across the country, not just those whose parents are members of Mar-a-Lago. I applaud my friend, Rep. Moore, for spearheading this legislation, and I’m glad to be part of this effort to keep public funds in public schools.”
title: Moore, Bonamici, Frost, Grijalva, and Pocan Blast Regulations Paving the Way for National Voucher Scheme

Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) — the only Virginian on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee — joined Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04) in sending a letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins opposing the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, commonly referred to as the “Roadless Rule.”
Since its implementation in 2001, the Roadless Rule has protected 45 million acres of forest lands across the country, including nearly 394,000 acres in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Under the Trump Administration, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Forest Service filed a proposal in August of this year to repeal the Roadless Rule, which could have devastating impacts on water quality, biodiversity, economic development and more for these regions.
The letter was also signed by U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.), and U.S. Representatives Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) and James Walkinshaw (Va.-11).
“This proposal would strip protections from approximately 84% of Virginia’s roadless areas, opening these lands to road construction, logging, and other industrial activities. The consequences for Virginia’s environment, economy, and public health would be severe, falling squarely on the families and communities we represent,” wrote the lawmakers. “With more roadless acres than any other state east of the Mississippi River, Virginia has an outsized stake in decisions regarding the Roadless Rule. Once lost, these ecosystems and the countless benefits they provide to clean air, clean water, and climate resilience cannot be easily restored, if at all.”
The letter outlines the risks this rescission would pose to Virginia by jeopardizing Virginia’s drinking water and ecosystems, threatening economic activity driven by recreation and tourism activities, increasing wildfire risk and straining public resources.
“For 25 years, the Roadless Rule has demonstrated that protecting America’s national forest lands is both effective and widely supported. Rescinding the Roadless Rule would ignore this overwhelming public consensus while undermining Virginia’s drinking water, biodiversity, local economies, and public safety,” the lawmakers concluded. “We urge the Department to withdraw this dangerous proposal and maintain the Roadless Area Conservation Rule of 2001 in its entirety.”
Read the full letter text here.

title: Vindman Stands Up for Roadless Rule to Protect Virginia’s Natural Resources, Local Economies

Davids Helps Launch Bipartisan Agenda to Cut Red Tape, Boost Local Economies, Lower Everyday Costs for Kansas Families
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids, a member of the Build America Caucus, helped announce the Build More Agenda — a major bipartisan policy platform designed to fix federal gridlock, strengthen local economies, create jobs, and lower everyday prices for hardworking families. By streamlining approval processes for energy, housing, and infrastructure, the roadmap directly targets the bureaucratic delays that slow down construction, drive up utility and housing costs, and prevent critical projects from getting built.
“Kansans don’t want D.C. talking points — they want lower utility bills, homes they can actually afford, and roads that aren't falling apart,” said Davids. “The problem isn't a lack of good ideas; it's the bureaucratic red tape slowing projects down for years. I’m supporting the bipartisan Build America Caucus’ new agenda because it would help cut through government gridlock and start building these projects now, not a decade from now.”
The bipartisan Build America Caucus was established to give pro-growth, pragmatic policymaking a permanent foothold in Congress. Over the past year, the Caucus helped negotiate and pass major bipartisan housing reform legislation and led bipartisan efforts to deliver permitting certainty for energy and infrastructure projects. Spanning seven core policy areas and over 60 legislative proposals, the Build More Agenda builds on those successes, establishing a comprehensive framework to spur domestic production, bring manufacturing home, create good-paying jobs, and lower the cost of living for Kansans.
“Not enough homes or energy, shortages of doctors and daycares, cures that take too long to reach patients, and infrastructure projects that drag on for decades. That’s what life in America looks like today because we’ve lost the ability to build the things we need,” said CaucusCo-Chairs Harder and Maloy. “We used to believe that America was the only place in the world where the boldest dreams could be realized, and we need a new politics of action to restore that national ambition and trust in government. The Build America Caucus was founded a little over a year ago with that goal in mind, and the Build More Agenda is our bipartisan roadmap to make growth and prosperity the cornerstone of American life once again.”
The solution to systemic dysfunction is to build our way to prosperity:
- Lowering Housing Costs: With the nation facing a shortage of five million homes, the agenda reduces regulatory delays, unlocks new project financing, and fully implements the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to expand homeownership options and bring housing prices back within reach for young families and working Kansans.
- Cutting Healthcare Costs & Red Tape: We spend more on healthcare than any other nation, but that care is unaffordable, inaccessible, and archaic. It reallocates physician training investments and slashes mountain-high administrative paperwork, so doctors spend time on patient outcomes rather than bureaucracy — cutting health system waste and lowering out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.
- Cheaper, Reliable Energy: Electricity rates have jumped more than 30 percent in recent years. The platform fixes broken permitting rules, so grid upgrades and energy projects don't take longer to approve than to actually construct, bringing down monthly electricity bills for households and small businesses.
- Building Infrastructure Faster: It establishes dedicated fast-track approvals and smarter federal funding models to ensure roads, bridges, and water systems are completed on schedule and under budget — ending costly construction delays that waste taxpayer dollars.
- Accelerating Medical Cures: America is losing its scientific edge because our scientists spend half their time on paperwork and research dollars aren’t geared toward modern discovery. It saves American medical researchers over one million hours a year spent on bureaucratic paperwork, redirecting resources toward breakthrough science and AI technology to accelerate cures for cancer, Alzheimer's, and chronic conditions.
- Expanding Childcare & Workforce Pipelines: It strengthens workforce development programs that directly match workers to high-paying local jobs, while expanding accessible childcare options so parents can stay in the workforce without breaking their household budgets.
- Modernizing Government to Save Taxpayer Dollars: It cuts redundant D.C. red tape, updates archaic federal technology systems, and builds a skill-focused public workforce that manages taxpayer funds efficiently.
Read the full agenda here. Read a section-by-section here.
“America knows how to build, we just have to get out of our own way and start doing it,” said Rep. Janelle Bynum (D-OR-05). “More homes, better roads and bridges, new technology, and good jobs – this agenda is about turning big ideas into things people can actually see and feel in their communities. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and help get it done.”
“Americans are tired of Washington making it harder and more expensive to build, innovate, and grow,” said Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA-01). “The Build More Agenda brings Republicans and Democrats together around commonsense solutions to cut red tape, lower costs, strengthen American energy, improve access to healthcare, and get critical projects built. I’m proud to work with the Build America Caucus to turn good ideas into real results for the American people.”
“The Build More Agenda reflects what we can accomplish when we work across the aisle to tackle challenges facing American families and businesses,” said Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12). “I’m proud to join my colleagues in the bipartisan Build America Caucus to advance practical solutions that cut unnecessary red tape, lower costs, and help America build faster and smarter. By modernizing infrastructure and creating opportunities for American workers and manufacturers, we can strengthen our economy, make taxpayer dollars go further, and deliver lasting results for our communities.”
“America used to pride itself on accomplishing big things — winning world wars, sending man to the moon, or discovering the next medical breakthrough,” said Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA-50). “Today, our challenges have not gone away, but our capacity to achieve great things has. Our constituents are counting on us to put politics aside and invest in our country’s future to make their lives better. The bipartisan Build More Agenda includes ways to do exactly that: lower costs, create good-paying jobs, strengthen communities, and restore America as a global leader in progress and innovation.”
“Folks in Western and Southern Colorado know how to build things, create jobs, and get things done,” said Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-03). “Too often, Washington just gets in the way. The Build More Agenda is about cutting unnecessary red tape so we can produce more American energy, build the housing and infrastructure our communities need, and bring down costs for working families. Republicans and Democrats aren’t going to agree on everything, but we ought to be able to agree that it shouldn’t take years of paperwork and bureaucracy to build something in this country.”
“A housing shortage is a tax on working people, and they pay it every month in rent,” said Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15). “For decades, we have piled on rules and caps that make it slower and costlier to build homes, and few places have paid a higher price than the Bronx. The surest way to bring down the cost of housing is to bring up the supply of housing. The Build More Agenda is built on that principle, because a pro-growth agenda is a pro–working class agenda. Progress should be measured not by how many projects we regulate but by how many we deliver.”
“Congress passed a housing abundance bill this term,” said Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04). “It's seriously debating a bipartisan energy abundance bill. Build America has momentum in its mission to lower prices by building more, faster & better – next up are unlocks to lower prices in medicine, transportation, and childcare.”
“As a senior member of the Housing, Transportation, and Urban Development Subcommittee, I’m proud to be a member of the bipartisan Build America Caucus. My constituents tell me every day they want to see their representatives in Washington take actions that will make their lives better – lower the cost of housing, healthcare, and energy,” said Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). “At a time of deep political division, we have the unique opportunity to come together as Democrats and Republicans to lower costs and solve the housing crisis.”
“Whether it’s rebuilding a bridge over I-95 in record time or passing landmark housing legislation, we know that government can still get things done, if rarely,” said Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT-04). “I’m in the Build America Caucus because this group of lawmakers fundamentally believes government needs to get things done — not as the exception, but as the rule. Our agenda reflects that belief, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to turn our group’s governing principle into law.”
What they’re saying about the Build More Agenda:
“For too long, we’ve treated a four-year college degree as the default path to a good career. The Build America Caucus’s push to get more apprenticeships and higher-quality workforce training programs off the ground is a critical step forward. If we want to build more in America, we need to make it easier for more Americans to learn how to do the building,” said Zach Boren, Senior Vice President, Apprenticeships for America.
“Getting lawmakers from both parties to agree on what's holding the country back is no easy feat, and we applaud the Build America Caucus for assembling a genuinely bipartisan coalition around these questions. BPC Action has long argued that the problems on this list — the cost of building housing, the time it takes to approve energy projects, and a broken childcare system — are solvable ones. We look forward to working with the caucus and its members as they move from agenda to legislation,” said Michele Stockwell, President, BPC Action.
“Through their work with the Build America Caucus, Reps. Harder and Maloy have asked how we can build more of what Americans actually need and answered it across housing, childcare, energy, and more. We applaud this effort and its goal to build 5 million homes, add millions more new childcare slots, modernize the energy grid, and get infrastructure built faster. This comprehensive plan demonstrates that pragmatic, actionable solutions can still be ambitious. This Agenda, written by a Democrat from California and a Republican from Utah, also shows the strength of abundance solutions in building coalitions. I urge Congress to take action on these solutions,” said Derek Kaufman, President, Inclusive Abundance Action.
“The Build More Agenda is an innovative, bipartisan framework for creating a more abundant future in America. The priorities laid out in this agenda have the potential to make a massive difference in areas from science and innovation to housing, transportation, and energy. For example, we were thrilled to see X-Labs and metascience units highlighted as vehicles to accelerate scientific discovery and increase the return on investment for R&D. Similarly, the Agenda’s focus on reducing land use regulations, building transit at lower cost, and achieving energy abundance is crucial for letting America build again and innovate in the world of atoms,” said Alec Stapp, CEO, Institute for Progress.
“For the past year, the Build America Caucus has worked across the aisle to notch key policy wins, making it easier, cheaper, and faster to build in America. The Build More Agenda strengthens that foundation, with over sixty policy proposals covering seven different policy areas. NAIA looks forward to working with the Caucus to back the builders,” said the New America Industrial Alliance.
“Finding childcare that's both affordable and meets their family’s specific needs is nearly impossible for far too many American parents. This agenda from the Build America Caucus offers an innovative menu of reforms to identify and remove the barriers to a more abundant supply of childcare options that fit family preferences without sacrificing quality or safety,” said Josh McCabe, Director of Social Policy, Niskanen Center.
“The housing affordability crisis is the result of many different factors, and solving it requires an all-hands-on-deck approach. The Build America Caucus agenda delivers this, with solutions that make it easier and less expensive to build housing. Critically, it does the same for transportation infrastructure and buses, because abundant housing and effective transportation options work together to connect people to economic opportunity,” said Kimberly Burnett, Deputy Director of Housing and Transportation, Niskanen Center.
“America's healthcare affordability crisis is fueled by a scarce and consolidated supply side of the market. This agenda from the Build America Caucus rightly targets solutions that increase care availability and cut out the incentives that drive consolidation,” said Lawson Mansell, Senior Health Policy Analyst, Niskanen Center.
“We applaud the Build America Caucus for its energy agenda focused on more power and lower bills. Getting transmission right and having neighboring regions connected is how you build a grid Americans can afford,” said Sarah Iskander, Government Affairs Manager, Niskanen Center.
“Whether it's housing, transportation, energy, or infrastructure, the federal government needs the tools and capacity to deliver for the American people. Meeting those demands requires a government whose systems and processes make delivery possible, and right now ours is not built to keep pace with changes in the workforce, technology, and the public's needs. The Build America Caucus's policy agenda takes this challenge head-on, rightly recognizing state capacity as essential to unlocking a prosperous future for our country,” said Max Stier, President and CEO, Partnership for Public Service.
“Getting the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into law was a major accomplishment, and Congressman Josh Harder and Congresswoman Celeste Maloy deserve a lot of credit for helping build the bipartisan coalition that got it done. Now we have to make it work. That means making sure HUD has the people and resources to implement the law well, while continuing the bipartisan work of finding the next set of solutions to get more homes built. The Build America Caucus’ Build More Agenda carries that work forward by keeping the focus on implementation and putting new ideas on the table. Up for Growth supports that direction, and we look forward to bringing our members and policy expertise to the work ahead,” said Mike Kingsella, Chief Executive Officer, Up for Growth.

REP LIEU JOINS REP. FRIEDMAN, LOS ANGELES DELEGATION, AND ENTERTAINMENT UNION IN PUSH FOR NATIONAL FILM TAX CREDIT
GLENDALE, CA – Today, October 6, 2026, Congressman Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles County) joined U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-Los Angeles County), Members of the Los Angeles congressional delegation, and the major unions representing film and television workers at the Alex Theatre in a new push for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. This bipartisan legislation creates a national film tax credit on qualified labor expenses to bring production jobs back home.
For decades, the United States has offered no national filming incentive, leaving American crews to compete against roughly 65 countries that do. The result has been hundreds of thousands of lost jobs for the drivers, grips, electricians, carpenters, caterers, and crew members.
WHAT THE BILL DOES:
- A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.
- Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.
- Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.
- Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.
- Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.
“Southern California is the birthplace of the modern film and television industry. From the movies and television shows that have entertained audiences around the world to the hardworking people behind them, this industry is a vital part of our community and economy,” said Congressman Lieu (CA-36). “We can’t let the United States’ film industry lose ground to foreign competitors. I am pleased to be an original co-sponsor of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. It’s time to strengthen our domestic film industry and protect American jobs.”
“When a production leaves this country, the stars still work. The crew is who gets left behind,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “65 countries offer incentives we don’t match, and no single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. Our bipartisan bill is built on labor costs, which means it only pays off when American workers get hired. These are good paying union jobs with benefits and pensions, and I won’t stop fighting until they come home.”
“Movie magic is central to the California story, and we need to keep it that way,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33). “Our state is losing good-paying, union jobs because filming in this country has become far too expensive. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act will bring jobs back to America, boost wages for workers and keep productions at home.”
"Southern California has been the heart of America’s film and television industry, but today, too many productions are leaving the United States for countries offering better incentives," said Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28). "That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which would provide a long-overdue federal tax credit to incentivize production here in the United States. Our creative workforce is the backbone of this industry. It's time we must invest in them and bring American film and television production back home."
“California is the heart of film and television production, in large part because of the workers and technicians who bring the magic to life,” said Representative Tran (CA-45). “Yet the U.S. is rapidly losing jobs in this industry to competitors overseas. When productions relocate outside the U.S., it’s the American-based crews that suffer the most. California’s workforce deserves better. This bill incentivizes American-based productions, strengthens California’s production workforce, and brings jobs back to the U.S.—where they belong.”
QUOTES
“American performers and entertainment workers should not have to leave the country to find work in an industry that was built here. Film and television are more than entertainment — they are a major American industry that supports hundreds of thousands of good-paying union jobs and generates significant economic activity in communities across the country. For decades, foreign governments have recognized the economic value of production and successfully used incentives to attract these jobs overseas. States across the country have shown what targeted incentives can do to attract and retain production, and a federal incentive would build on those efforts and give the United States a stronger tool to compete. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is an investment in American workers, American industry and American communities. SAG-AFTRA is proud to stand with Congresswoman Friedman and our labor partners in support of this important legislation,” said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.
“The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will benefit entertainment industry workers, as well as the supporting businesses and local economies that rely on a robust domestic entertainment industry. Lawmakers have an opportunity to invest in an important American industry and preserve middle-class jobs, by passing the first-ever federal film and television tax incentive program,” said WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta.
"Let’s not overthink this. The world is a complicated place, but this legislation is a no-brainer. It's going to get people back to work, and everyone just wants an opportunity to work in the industry they love in this country. Everyone will benefit from this – Republicans, Democrats, workers, audiences -- because our industry touches everyone," said Mike Farah, an Emmy-winning producer and a President of the Producers Guild of America.
Rep. Lieu was joined today by U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (CA-30), Senator Adam Schiff (CA), U.S. Representatives Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Pete Aguilar (CA-33), David Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45), IATSE International Vice President and Director of the Motion Picture and Television Department Mike Miller, SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta, DGA Associate National Executive Director and Western Executive Director Rebecca Rhine, Teamsters At-Large Vice President and Motion Picture Division Director Lindsay Dougherty, LiUNA Business Manager Alex Aguilar, Jr., and producer and three-time Emmy winner Mike Farah.

Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers on FDA Move to Rewrite Vaping Approval Rules, Blasts Weakening of Scientific Standards
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, today demanded answers from Food and Drug Administration Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas over FDA’s September 28 announcement that it is considering new rulemaking to replace the 2021 regulations governing approval of new tobacco products, pressing the agency over whether the move could weaken the scientific standards manufacturers must meet.
Krishnamoorthi is also demanding to know whether FDA discussed potential changes with tobacco manufacturers, industry associations, or parties challenging the current rules before announcing its review, and is seeking communications between agency officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries and representatives, and other parties challenging the framework.
FDA announced its review less than four weeks after Altria subsidiaries NJOY and Helix Innovations sued the agency over the current Premarket Tobacco Product Application framework. FDA itself cited recent litigation challenging the framework, along with the widespread illicit tobacco market, in explaining its decision to consider replacing the rule.
“The widespread sale of illegal products is an enforcement problem,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “It should not become a justification for lowering the evidentiary requirements manufacturers must satisfy before FDA authorizes their products.”
Krishnamoorthi also raised concerns about the review in light of FDA’s recent authorization of flavored e-cigarette products. In May, the agency authorized Glas products in mango and blueberry flavors despite FDA data indicating that fruit-flavored e-cigarettes are the most popular flavor among youth. The letter notes that the FDA Center for Tobacco Products did not require the manufacturer to demonstrate that the flavors provided an added benefit to adults attempting to transition from combustible products, and that former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary reportedly resigned in part amid political interference surrounding the authorization.
FDA then authorized additional JUUL products on August 28, including a JUUL2 menthol product.
“FDA acknowledged that the menthol product carries risks ‘including youth appeal,’ but concluded that its benefits to adults who smoke outweighed those risks,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “Exactly one month later, FDA announced that it may replace the broader framework governing applications for new tobacco products.”
Krishnamoorthi concluded:
“The FDA’s job is to protect public health, not make it easier for tobacco companies to evade rigorous scientific review. The agency should crack down on companies selling illegal products, not use their lawbreaking as a rationale for weakening safeguards governing products seeking FDA authorization.”
Krishnamoorthi requested written responses by October 20, 2026, to the following questions:
- Which specific provisions of the 2021 PMTA rule is FDA considering changing or eliminating, and what evidence supports each potential change?
- Will FDA commit that any replacement framework will not lower the scientific evidentiary bar manufacturers must meet to demonstrate that marketing their products is appropriate for the protection of public health? If not, why not?
- Did FDA discuss potential changes to the 2021 PMTA rule with any tobacco product manufacturer, industry association, or party challenging the 2021 PMTA rule before announcing its review? Please identify each such entity and provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and those entities. Please also provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries or representatives, and any other party challenging the rule concerning the PMTA framework or potential changes to it.
- How does the existence of a widespread illicit market justify changes to the regulatory requirements governing products seeking lawful authorization? What connection has FDA identified between illegal sales and the scientific evidence manufacturers should be required to provide before receiving authorization?
- What additional enforcement actions will FDA take, in coordination with the Department of Justice and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, to remove unauthorized e-cigarettes from the U.S. market?
The full letter is available here.
Congressman Krishnamoorthi has led congressional efforts to combat youth vaping and hold tobacco companies accountable. In 2019, he launched the first congressional investigation into youth vaping, exposing JUUL’s marketing tactics and pushing legislation to ban flavored e-cigarettes and close the synthetic nicotine loophole. He has since led bipartisan efforts urging federal agencies to crack down on illegal flavored vapes and launched an investigation into illicit vaping products from China advertised to children. In 2025, Krishnamoorthi and Congresswoman Celeste Maloy (R-UT), his fellow co-chair of the Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, called on FDA to strengthen enforcement as more than 6,000 flavored products remained on the market. Most recently, Krishnamoorthi helped introduce the bipartisan PROTECT Act to strengthen federal efforts to prevent and reduce youth e-cigarette use.

WASHINGTON, DC — Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) has introduced the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act to reinstate federal funding for New York’s Essential Plan and restore health coverage for nearly 15,000 people in NY-19 and more than 450,000 New Yorkers.
New York’s Essential Plan is a lifeline for working families, providing comprehensive health coverage at affordable rates. However, H.R.1 – Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act – slashed funding for the program, forcing thousands of Upstate New Yorkers to sign up for more expensive private insurance or forgo coverage altogether.
“Upstate New Yorkers work hard, play by the rules, and deserve health care they can actually afford,” Riley said. “Washington politicians handed out massive tax breaks to the wealthy and big corporations, then paid for them by ripping health care away from working families. These cuts will drive up premiums, put more pressure on our rural hospitals, and leave thousands of Upstate New Yorkers without coverage. I’m fighting to reverse them and restore the health care our communities depend on.”
You can read the text of the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act HERE.
This bill builds on Riley’s ongoing push to defend healthcare in Upstate New York:
- April 2025: Supported the Protecting Options for Seniors Act (H.R. 2610) to ensure fairer reimbursement rates for rural hospitals.
- May 2025: Requested over $55 million for rural infrastructure and community health projects for Fiscal Year 2026.
- July 2025: Opposed the “One Big Beautiful Bill” (H.R. 1) that cut Medicaid and threatened hospital closures.
- August 2025: Co-sponsored the Rural Hospital Stabilization Act (H.R. 3063) to provide $500 million in emergency support for rural hospitals.
- November 2025: Sent letters to the CEOs of UnitedHealth Group, Humana, and CVS Health demanding answers for their decision to drop Medicare Advantage plans in rural communities across Upstate New York.
- December 2025: Supported CommonGround2025, a bipartisan proposal to stop premium hikes, protect families’ health coverage, and keep healthcare affordable in Upstate New York.

Rep. Grijalva Statement on Border Patrol Raid Near Lochiel, Arizona
Nogales, Arizona – Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the below statement following reports of a U.S. Border Patrol raid and the toppling of a centuries-old cottonwood tree along the U.S.-Mexico border near Lochiel, Arizona. This comes after a U.S. Forest Service announcement posted on its website – without any prior public input or notification – last week closing roads and restricting public access to miles of lands along the U.S.-Mexico border as they proceed with wall construction.
“Just days after the U.S. Forest Service closed miles of public lands along the border, armed Border Patrol agents conducted a raid that injured protesters and uprooted the last of four century-old cottonwood trees. This is what the militarization of our borderlands looks like – and it’s all because DHS has more taxpayer dollars than it knows what to do with, and is wasting them on a reckless and useless second border wall. Our borderlands are home to unique ecosystems and world-class biodiversity, including some of the last remaining habitat for the Sonoran jaguar in the United States.
DHS and its private contractors have repeatedly shown they cannot be trusted to protect sensitive cultural and environmental sites. That is why public access and oversight are so critical. Instead, DHS is following the same playbook: shut out the public, evade scrutiny, and recklessly bulldoze our lands. Administrations come and go, but unfortunately the damage the Trump administration is inflicting on our irreplaceable borderlands cannot simply be undone.”
title: Rep. Grijalva Statement on Border Patrol Raid Near Lochiel, Arizona

Washington, DC – Congresswoman Julia Brownley (D-CA) joined Congressman Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and Senator Brian Schatz (D-HI) in introducing a resolution standing strong for the American freedom to read, write and learn. The lawmakers’ resolution condemns MAGA’s escalating campaign of book bans in school libraries and censorship targeting the Smithsonian Institution and other public museums, parks and facilities.
The lawmakers’ resolution specifically cites book bans issued by the Trump Administration, MAGA state legislatures, local libraries and schools across America. This year, federal officials, at the direction of President Trump, censored books and educational materials at the Smithsonian Institution and Department of Defense Education Activity schools.
More than 12,000 individual books were banned in America between July 2025 and June 2026, according to a report by PEN America. This includes books like “The Bluest Eye” by Toni Morrison and “MARCH” by former Congressman and Civil Rights Movement hero John Lewis, Andrew Aydin and Nate Powell.
PEN America’s report captures the proliferation of MAGA book bans that specifically target books written by and about outsiders and individuals from marginalized backgrounds. Books with LGBTQ+ characters or themes face a disproportionate risk of being banned.
According to PEN America, from July 2025 to June 2026, 24 States across the country limited access to certain books, including:
- Texas, where at least 8,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 45 school districts;
- Florida, where at least 3,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 35 school districts;
- Ohio, where at least 115 books in total have been banned or restricted in one school district;
- Utah, where at least 100 books in total have been banned or restricted in five school districts; and
- Michigan, where at least 65 books in total have been banned or restricted in two school districts.
The resolution is endorsed by PEN America and the American Library Association (ALA); Authors Against Banned Books; Banned Books Week Coalition; Center for American Progress; EdTrust; EveryLibrary; Freedom to Learn Foundation; Florida Freedom to Read Project; Freedom to Read Project; Hatchette Book Group; Interfaith Alliance; JCRC of Greater Washington; Jewish Community Relations Council of Portland; Jewish Council for Public Affairs; Jewish Federation of Greater Rochester; Lee & Low Books ; Let Utah Read; Macmillan Publishing; National Coalition Against Censorship; National Council for Jewish Women; National Council of Teachers of English; National Education Association; Penguin Random House; PFLAG National; Red Wine and Blue Education Fund; Simon & Schuster; Texas Freedom to Read Project; and the Tucson Jewish Museum & Holocaust Center.
The resolution is also cosponsored in the House by Representatives Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Shontel Brown (OH-11), Andre Carson (IN-07), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Emmanuel Cleaver (MO-5), Jim Costa (CA-21), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jahana Hayes (CT-05), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Betty McCollum (MN-04), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Grace Meng (NY-06), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Scott Peters (CA-50), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Nikema Williams (GA-05) and Frederica Wilson (FL-24).

Rep. McBride, Senator Coons, local leaders assess coastal damage, call for more funding to rebuild Delaware’s beaches following storm
DEWEY BEACH, Del. – U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senator Chris Coons (both D-Del.), joined by the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, local elected officials, and community leaders surveyed damage on Friday morning from last week’s nor’easter that battered Delaware’s coast for four days and caused severe beach erosion, dune damage and flooding in communities all along the coast. The storm damaged homes and businesses, caused road closures, and shut down beaches. Following their assessment of the damage, Senator Coons and Representative McBride called for additional federal support to help Delaware’s coastal communities recover and replenish their beaches.
Rep. McBride and Senator Coons were joined on Friday by officials from the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, Dewey Beach Town Manager Bill Zolper, Dewey Beach Mayor Bill Stevens, South Bethany Mayor Edie Dondero, Bethany Beach Mayor Ron Calef, State Sen. Russ Huxtable and State Rep. Claire Snyder-Hall.
“Delaware’s beaches are critical to our communities, our economy, and our way of life, and we need to make sure they have the resources they need to recover from this storm and prepare for the next one,” said Senator Coons. “I’m going to keep fighting for the funding Delaware needs to rebuild and recover. That means working with our local leaders, DNREC, the Army Corps and our entire congressional delegation to make sure we’re doing everything we can to protect our coast.”
“The damage Senator Coons and I saw is a stark reminder that investing in the resilience of our coastal communities is not optional,” said Rep. McBride. “We cannot prevent these storms from happening, but we can take action to keep people safe and help our communities withstand their impacts. That’s why I’ve been working with partners at every level of government to strengthen our coastline, combat coastal erosion, and ensure Delaware is prepared when severe weather strikes. I’m grateful to Mayor Stevens, our first responders, local leaders, and everyone who stepped up to keep our neighbors safe during the nor’easter. I’ll keep working to make sure Delaware has what it needs to recover from this storm, prepare for the next one, and protect our beaches for generations to come.”
Earlier this year, Senators Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester and Representative McBride helped secure $10 million for beach replenishment along the Delaware coast from Cape Henlopen to Fenwick Island and are working with the Army Corps of Engineers to make that funding available as quickly as possible. Senator Coons is also working with the federal delegation and DNREC to secure an additional $30 million in federal beach replenishment funding this year to help address the state’s ongoing coastal needs.
###
title: Rep. McBride, Senator Coons, local leaders assess coastal damage, call for more funding to rebuild Delaware’s beaches following storm

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) reintroduced legislation to create a Science Advisory Board at the Office of Justice Programs (OJP) within the Department of Justice (DOJ). The Board will be responsible for integrating scientific knowledge into crime-reduction efforts, as well as for using research, data, and evidence to guide the OJP’s grants, programs, and activities. The Improving Justice Programs through Science Act is cosponsored by Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05).
The Science Advisory Board was originally chartered by the Obama Administration in 2010 and provided OJP with guidance in proactive criminal justice reform efforts, including developing trauma-informed care, building trust between police and communities, and understating youth brain development and its implications for juvenile justice programs. The Board also made numerous contributions to the public safety investments of OJP, including guidelines for implementing and evaluating place-based crime reduction interventions and a tool for police departments to enhance communications with communities about their operations and successes.
“Americans want our criminal justice system to do its job — make all of us safer not just by punishing criminals today, but also by preventing crime in the future,” Rep. Dean said. Reducing recidivism and protecting our communities requires a deliberate strategy built on the best available data and science. The Improving Justice Programs through Science Act would create a Science Advisory Board to advise on evidence-based criminal justice policies and ensure that we are getting the highest quality data to inform future decisions. This is about getting the most out of our tax dollars, and making our streets safer today, tomorrow, and years from now.”
“In order to do justice, particularly with respect to juveniles, it is important that we have access to the best current research and information,” Rep. Scanlon said. “Advances in science which can promote both public safety and rehabilitation, and reduce recidivism, must be incorporated in our criminal justice system. I’m proud to join Rep. Dean in introducing this bill to make our justice system more effective and fair.”
- Meet on a regular basis to discuss the relationship between science, research, and ongoing criminal and juvenile justice departmental activities;
- Coordinate with other Federal, State, local, tribal, territorial, and private sector partners; and
- Advise the Assistant Attorney General on policy development, program implementation, and evaluation; identify research needs and opportunities and make policy recommendations.
The Improving Justice Programs through Science Act is endorsed by American Psychological Association, American Political Science Association, American Sociological Association, Consortium of Social Science Associations, Council of Professional Associations on Federal Statistics, and Union of Concerned Scientists. Congresswoman Dean previously introduced the Improving Justice Programs through Science Act during her first term, in the 116th Congress, as well as the 117th Congress.
Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.
title: Congresswoman Dean Reintroduces the Improving Justice Programs through Science Act

text:
RELEASE: Gottheimer Calls on the NJDEP to Rescind Eviction Notices for Andover-Aeroflex Airport
Fights to Protect Woman-Owned Flight Academy and Aircraft Maintenance Small Businesses; Flight School Trains Military Pilots, Only Location within 100 Miles — Even Trained Harrison Ford; Double Standard: NJDEP Throwing Out Small Businesses Because of Safety Concerns, but Allowing Forest Fire Service to Remain in Hangar; Utter Confusion: Will Cost State $4 M to Make Repairs They Want and $8M to Demolish Hangars; Calls on State & NJDEP Commissioner to Tour the Airport & Reconsider Draconian Decision; Airport Boosts Local Sussex County Economy —Would be a Devastating Blow if Closed
Above: Gottheimer visits Andover-Aeroflex Airport with Woman-Owned Small Business Owner, Damian DelGaizo, and Andover Mayor Thomas Walsh Jr.
ANDOVER, NJ — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) toured and then spoke at Andover-Aeroflex Airport after the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) moved to evict the woman-owned Andover Flight Academy, the airport’s aircraft maintenance shop, and several other aircraft owners from their hangars. The flight school teaches military pilots how to land on short runways and in open fields. Gottheimer announced he is sending a letter to Governor Mikie Sherrill and NJDEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak urging them to rescind the eviction notices, which were mailed last week by the NJDEP Commissioner to the small business owners. Gottheimer is asking the NJDEP to work with the Governor’s office, tenants, local leaders, and his office on a plan that will keep these small businesses at Aeroflex. Gottheimer is also calling on the NJDEP Commissioner to come and tour the facility with him and provide further explanation for the closure.
Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.
Gottheimer sent this letter to the Governor and NJDEP Commissioner, Ed Potosnak.
“I’m frustrated, and so are the people standing next to me,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I’m not going to let you guys get thrown out. It’s not happening. We’re going to fight this thing.”
New Jersey’s own site claims that it would cost $4.7 million to make repairs the state wants to the hangars and $8 million to demolish them. The state is planning to demolish the location — costing taxpayers double.
- Multiple discrepancies were identified in the NJDEP’s reasons for issuing evictions. The agency falsely reported that the building lacked running water — a claim that would also make the location unsuitable for the NJ Forest Fire Service — but Gottheimer found the water was working just fine (VIDEO).
- NJDEP also claims that the evictions will create necessary additional space for the NJ Forest Fire Service, which was “sharing space and had their items placed in a corner of the hangar.” But, upon touring the facility, there appeared to be ample available space within the Forest Fire Service’s designated individual hangar area (VIDEO).
- The NJDEP claimed that the flight school office was in disrepair, but that could not have been further from the truth (VIDEO).
New Jersey is short on hangar space, and pilots wait years on lists for a spot. The Andover Aeroflex is one of only two remaining airports in Sussex County, New Jersey, and the only site within 100 miles that trains pilots on how to land on shorter runways and in open spaces. The school also draws in many pilots from around the country to learn, like actor Harrison Ford (VIDEO), which also greatly helps the local economy.
Many of the planes at Aeroflex are antiques with fabric skins that the sun and rain would wreck if left outside. If the flight school and the shop are lost, the airport loses the small businesses that bring in pilots and revenue, and the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA) has warned this puts the whole airport at risk of becoming a glorified parking lot.
Gottheimer criticized the NJDEP’s lack of transparency through this entire process. His office has repeatedly requested information and a timeline from the department and has received almost nothing in return. In his letter, Gottheimer asks Governor Sherrill, a former Navy helicopter pilot, to rescind the eviction notices and direct the NJDEP to work with her office, the tenants, local leaders, and his office on a plan that keeps these businesses at Aeroflex.
Additionally, the NJDEP says the hangar is unsafe, yet still allows the New Jersey Forest Fire Service to use it, a double standard that makes no sense. And the numbers don’t add up. The state’s own engineering assessment calls for roughly $4.7 million in renovations. Their assessment claims the demolition would cost $8 million — nearly twice the price. Construction of a replacement building for the Fire Service would be more than $11 million. A licensed engineer who walked the property found the buildings in fair condition with no outstanding code violations, and said targeted repairs would cost only about $267,000.
Gottheimer is calling for no evictions until a clear timeline is set with a solution that does not hurt small businesses and families, and for the NJDEP Commissioner to tour the facility and see firsthand the status of the airport.
Gottheimer was joined by Andover Mayor Thomas D. Walsh Jr., Andover Flight Academy Founder Damien DelGaizo, and Andover Flight Academy Owner Justine Pasniewski.
Below: Gottheimer visits Andover-Aeroflex Airport.
###
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Calls on the NJDEP to Rescind Eviction Notices for Andover-Aeroflex Airport

Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, along with Representatives Nydia Velázquez (D-NY), Brad Sherman (D-CA), Gregory Meeks (D-NY), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Al Green (D-TX), Emanuel Cleaver (D-MO), Bill Foster (D-IL), Joyce Beatty (D-OH), Juan Vargas (D-CA), Ayanna Pressley (D-MA), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), Ritchie Torres (D-NY), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), Nikema Williams (D-GA) and Sam Liccardo (D-CA), sent a letter to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chairman Paul S. Atkins strongly opposing the Commission’s proposal to eliminate the March 2024 climate-related disclosure rules.
In the letter, the lawmakers warn that eliminating the rules would deprive investors of critical information about the financial risks companies face from climate change at a time when climate-related events are becoming increasingly more common and disruptive to businesses and the broader economy. They argue that the SEC has a responsibility to ensure investors have consistent, standardized information necessary to evaluate these risks and make informed decisions with their money.
“Stripping away these rules denies investors the information they need to accurately assess a company’s long-term value and to make sound, well-informed decisions with their hard-earned money,” the lawmakers wrote.
The lawmakers also dispute the Commission’s argument that the SEC exceeded its statutory authority in adopting the rules. They point to the SEC’s longstanding authority under federal securities laws to determine what information public companies must disclose to investors, as well as the Commission’s decades-long history of requiring disclosures in response to evolving market risks and economic conditions. The letter notes that the SEC has required various forms of environmental disclosure dating back to the 1970s and argues that climate-related disclosures fall within the Commission’s traditional role of ensuring investors have relevant information when making investment decisions.
The lawmakers added, “…nothing in the governing statutes, case law, or legislative history has changed since March 2024, and Congress has amended neither the Securities Act nor the Exchange Act. The only thing that has changed is the composition of the Commission.”
The letter also pushes back on arguments that climate disclosures are unnecessary or immaterial to investors. The lawmakers point to data showing that companies actively managing climate risks can realize significant financial benefits, while 80 percent of investors want the opportunity to invest in companies that consider environmental sustainability. Investors and financial institutions representing hundreds of trillions of dollars in assets have also sought climate-related information from companies to inform their investment and financing decisions.
The lawmakers conclude by urging the Commission to maintain the existing disclosure framework and withdraw its proposal to rescind the rules.
Full list of signers includes: Nydia Velázquez (D-NY), Brad Sherman (D-CA), Gregory Meeks (D-NY), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Al Green (D-TX), Emanuel Cleaver (D-MO), Bill Foster (D-IL), Joyce Beatty (D-OH), Juan Vargas (D-CA), Ayanna Pressley (D-MA), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), Ritchie Torres (D-NY), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), Nikema Williams (D-GA), Sam Liccardo (D-CA).
Read the full letter HERE.
Background:
    - June 16, 2021 — Passed climate-risk disclosure legislation through the House. Then Chairwoman Waters led House passage of a broader ESG disclosure package, which would require public companies to disclose financial and business risks associated with climate change. Read Waters' floor statement on passage of the legislation. 
- March 21, 2022 — Applauded the SEC's proposed climate-disclosure rule after years of Committee action. Then-Chairwoman Waters joined committee Dems in a letter to commending the SEC's proposed rule requiring climate-related disclosures by public companies. Waters highlighted that, under her leadership, the Committee had already held four hearings on the issue and advanced legislation from Committee Democrats over the previous two Congresses. Read Waters and Committee Dems statement on the proposed SEC rule. 
- October 6, 2023 — Pressed SEC Chair Gary Gensler to quickly finalize the rule. Waters urged Gensler to finish the long-awaited climate-risk disclosure rule, warning that climate change and transition risks threatened Americans' investments, retirement savings, businesses and broader financial stability. She argued that investors needed consistent and comparable information to understand those risks. Read Waters' letter urging Gensler to finalize the climate-risk disclosure rule. 
- March 7, 2024 — Supported the SEC's final climate-disclosure rule while pushing for stronger protections. After the SEC finalized the rule, Waters welcomed the creation of standardized climate-risk disclosures but criticized the Commission for significantly weakening its original proposal. She specifically raised concerns about the treatment of Scope 1 and 2 emissions and the elimination of Scope 3 requirements, while emphasizing the real financial consequences of climate change for investors, homeowners and renters. Read Waters' statement on the final SEC climate-disclosure rule.
- April 10, 2024 — Defended the climate rule against Republican attacks in a full Committee hearing. At a Republican-led hearing titled “Beyond Scope: How the SEC's Climate Rule Threatens American Markets,” Waters defended the rule as a commonsense investor protection, arguing that climate change affects companies' financial health and investors have a right to understand how the companies they own are responding to those risks. Read Waters' opening statement defending the SEC climate rule. 
- June 5, 2024 — Led 36 lawmakers with Senator Elizabeth Warren in pressing the SEC to defend and enforce the rule. Waters and Warren led 36 lawmakers urging the SEC to remain focused on climate risk despite litigation challenging the rule. They called on the Commission to enforce its existing climate-risk guidance while the rule was stayed, use every available resource to defend the rule in court and robustly implement it once the stay was lifted. Read the Waters-Warren letter and Committee release. 
- September 17–19, 2024 — Fought Republican legislation restricting the SEC's disclosure authority. Waters opposed H.R. 4790, warning that it would restrict the SEC's authority to determine what information public companies must disclose, including environmental and climate-related information, and undermine investors' access to information about the companies they own. She testified against the legislation before the Rules Committee on September 17 and opposed it again on the House floor on September 19. Read Waters' September 17 testimony against H.R. 4790. Read Waters' September 19 floor statement. 
- December 29, 2025 — Demanded SEC oversight after Chairman Paul Atkins abandoned the climate-rule defense. Waters called for a long-overdue oversight hearing with Atkins amid sweeping changes at the SEC, including the Commission's retreat from climate-risk disclosure. The request put the Administration's reversal of climate-related investor protections squarely within the Committee Democrats' broader oversight of Atkins' leadership. Read Waters' request for an SEC oversight hearing. 
- February 11, 2026 — Confronted Atkins directly over halting the SEC's defense of the climate rule. When Atkins finally appeared before the Committee, Waters criticized his SEC for having “halted the SEC's defense of the climate disclosure rule” even as the California wildfires demonstrated the material financial risks associated with climate change. She placed the decision within a broader critique that Atkins' SEC was prioritizing Wall Street and billionaires over investors. Read Waters' February 2026 opening statement confronting Atkins.
###
title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters and Committee Democrats Blast SEC Push to Eliminate Climate Risk Disclosures

Congressman Don Davis Introduces Bill to Ban Federal Candidates from Betting on Their Own Elections
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) introduced the No Betting on Your Own Race Act, which would ban federal candidates seeking elected office from trades tied to their own races.
The No Betting on Your Own Race Act would prohibit federal candidates, their spouses or dependent children, and authorized campaign committees from buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of, or holding contracts tied to the candidate’s election.
"We don't want our athletes to bet on their games. A candidate running for federal elected office should be treated exactly the same and should not be allowed to trade on their own election," said Congressman Don Davis. "The No Betting on Your Own Race Act aims to prevent market interference, insider trading, as well as candidates and their family members from cashing in. To establish consistency and ensure all federal candidate campaign committees understand this, Congress must pass this common-sense legislation."
Violators will incur a $10,000 civil penalty for each violation. If there is a net financial gain, the penalty will be three times the gain, or $10,000, whichever is greater. The new law also provides that a candidate who is running for office at the federal level must be notified during the filing period.
The legislative text can be found HERE.
title: Congressman Don Davis Introduces Bill to Ban Federal Candidates from Betting on Their Own Elections
