Scott Statement on the Trump Administration’s National School Voucher Scheme
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s new proposed rule, entitled “Federal Scholarship Tax Credit.”
“America's public school system is founded on the promise that all students should have access to a high-quality public education. Today, the Treasury Department issued a proposed rule to implement the massive federal voucher scheme that was included in the Republicans’ ‘Big Ugly Bill.’ The program effectively diverts billions of taxpayer dollars away from public schools through the voucher program to subsidize private school education. Today’s proposal goes even further by prohibiting states from adding requirements to ensure the program meaningfully benefits public schools and the students who attend them. It also prohibits states from adding additional requirements to ensure students do not face discrimination when accessing educational services.
“Voucher schemes are inefficient, ineffective, and an expensive tool to privatize public education. If just 20 percent of eligible donors participate in the voucher scheme, the cost to the taxpayer would be roughly $37.6 billion — more than all federal spending on Title I and the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) combined. Meanwhile, data from existing state voucher programs shows that most students who benefit from those programs are already enrolled in private schools. Yet ninety percent of America’s children attend public schools. Despite this, public education has gone underfunded for decades. Without long term, sustained federal investment, schools and educators lack the resources they need to teach all students effectively.
“Moreover, when federal dollars go to public schools, schools are required to use that money to serve all students equally without discrimination. By funneling these dollars into private schools, taxpayers are unwittingly paying for schools that neglect underprivileged communities, are permitted to ignore civil rights laws, and can freely discriminate against students without accountability.
“Public dollars should be spent on public education. Just imagine what we could do if this money were used to improve all of America’s public schools instead. Democrats are committed to investing in public education for all communities — not just the privileged few.”
###
title: Scott Statement on the Trump Administration’s National School Voucher Scheme

WASHINGTON – Yesterday, members of Maryland’s Congressional Delegation and Baltimore City Mayor Brandon Scott held a meeting at the United States Capitol to discuss their work on a range of priorities for Baltimore residents, including affordable housing, transportation, public safety, healthcare, and more.

This work is all the more important as the Trump Administration continues to attack our communities and essential programs that serve the City. SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) is introducing a new policy framework that reins in artificial intelligence (AI) by requiring every AI company to hold a federal charter to do business in the U.S. The AI charter is modeled after existing regulatory frameworks, combining the round-the-clock federal oversight, strict safety mandates, and structural separation built into national bank charters with the rigorous pre-release federal testing required for nuclear materials and dangerous weapons. The charter would ensure that the public’s interests come first and that the government has broad authority to hold AI companies accountable before they create harm rather than addressing abuses after the fact. AI companies that don’t agree, don’t comply, or put the public in danger get shut down.

“The crux of this bill is simple: if you want to be an AI company in this country, you have to obtain a public charter that has a broad set of terms and conditions to operate and ensure public benefit without the harms,” said Jayapal. “For too long, we’ve allowed a few Big Tech companies to dominate the market. They have used mass surveillance to steal private information, labor, and creative work, building trillion-dollar empires on our tracked personal lives. AI corporations and Big Tech are now following that same playbook. My National AI Charter Act framework gets at the root of the problem by disrupting the way the AI market is structured to give a very few companies all the power over our data and what happens with it and instead establishes clear rules of operation for these AI companies and prioritizes safety over profits.”

To date, traditional Big Tech policies have tried to patch up problems around the edges after harm is done, treating data privacy, children’s safety, worker rights, market concentration, and all the rest as separate issues. That approach hides the full scope, reach, and systemic impact of Big Tech’s surveillance monopolies. The fragmented response has allowed their lobbyists to divide the broad coalition of their victims, narrow fights to single-issue bills that they stall, make the case for self-regulation, and ignore the root profit drivers incentivizing their bad behavior.

The National AI Charter Act takes a fundamentally different approach by addressing the full scope of AI harms comprehensively upfront. The charter would be required to operate AI and its terms and conditions would be mandatory. At its core, the charter framework recognizes that AI risks are connected and driven by underlying market structures, surveillance business models, and profit motives. AI companies would be banned from building empires, releasing risky models, stealing through surveillance, exploiting workers, or causing harm. Gating market access to companies that comply with these requirements would break Big Tech’s grip on AI and protect the public from dangerous AI models.

The framework’s new legal authorities to hold AI companies accountable would build on those that already apply. They would not preempt or replace federal, state, and local laws, nor would they prevent or impede law enforcement agencies from enforcing those laws against AI companies or their executives. Instead, they would strengthen the hand of prosecutors and plaintiffs by proactively confirming the many ways these laws apply to AI, rather than leaving it to judges to interpret case by case. Most importantly, making this illegal conduct a charter violation would create a powerful additional enforcement tool with serious, mandatory consequences.

The National AI Charter Act framework’s comprehensive approach would bolster existing law enforcement by:

Taking power back from billionaires and putting the public and workers first: The handful of billionaires and tech giants that control AI’s future are locked in a dangerous race to the bottom. The framework separates AI companies from Big Tech monopolies and bans their predatory commercial surveillance so that AI isn’t baked into the core Internet platforms everyone uses or trained with data harvested by tracking everything people do online. It also claws back Big Tech’s ill-gotten gains from their monopoly data to fund direct payouts to all Americans.

Preventing harm up front instead of chasing it afterward: AI harms can spread too fast for after-the-fact enforcement to stop them, and fines don’t remedy the damage or truly deter it from happening again. The framework’s upfront charter requirements are not just rules to follow; they are a mandatory price of entry into the AI industry and the condition for remaining in it. Companies must continuously comply or get shut down.

Drawing bright lines on the full range of AI dangers: AI’s dangerous capabilities cannot be prevented with technical rules that quickly become obsolete; they have to be comprehensively banned outright. Under the framework, AI systems capable of going rogue, creating catastrophic hazards, replacing skilled work, exploiting children, or causing other serious public harms are outlawed and cannot be released.

Putting the government in charge of safety at every stage: AI companies have admitted the risks of their own systems while still insisting they should police themselves. The framework replaces the AI industry’s failed self-regulation with round-the-clock federal oversight, testing in government facilities and approval to release, adversarial stress tests, and a government-controlled kill switch.

Imposing strict liability on AI companies and executives: As long as the price of causing harm is likely to cost less than the potential profits, AI companies will keep taking reckless risks. The framework reverses these incentives by holding AI companies and their executives strictly liable for lawbreaking, with loss of charter and criminal penalties for the most serious violations.

“At the end of the day, the American people are feeling a loss of control, of their personal data, of their jobs, of their ability to even know what they see online is real,” Jayapal added. “This legislation would restore a level of control and ensure that every search made online isn’t tracked, every family photo posted isn’t training an AI model, and every piece of our lives isn’t monetized by corporations.”

A wide range of experts have weighed in on the need for a comprehensive approach:

“The public has paid an extraordinary price for big tech’s self-regulation. Representative Jayapal’s framework learns from those mistakes. For generations we have required banks, drug makers, and nuclear operators to meet public terms before they do business, and AI companies should be no different,” said Lina Khan, Director, Center for Law and the Economy, and former Chair of the Federal Trade Commission.

“This legislative framework meaningfully advances the ball to establish a comprehensive set of reforms to address the potential for societal harms from AI,” said Jonathan Kanter, former Assistant Attorney General of the Department of Justice’s Antitrust Division.

“We really need a framework like this to start getting to the big question of how Americans want to regulate AI,” said Tim Wu, Julius Silver Professor of Law, Science and Technology, Columbia Law School.

“Innovation and safety are not opposing concepts; they’re two sides of the same coin—which is why regulation is vitally important. AI is rapidly transforming our classrooms, workplaces, and economy, but Big Tech must be held accountable for their business models, just like every other industry in the country. If these companies want to win the trust of the American people, they must respect the rules of the road. Representative Jayapal’s framework does exactly that by establishing preemptive guardrails that compel AI firms to serve the public interest, not just the narrow interests of shareholders,” said Randi Weingarten, President, American Federation of Teachers.

“The comprehensive approach being pioneered by Representative Jayapal’s National AI Charter Act gets to the root of the extreme harms of unregulated and out-of-control AI. The mandatory requirement to be chartered and operate only under strict guardrails and associated liability will hold companies accountable and ensure that protecting the public is considered first as tech is created. Public Citizen applauds this move to fight concentration and to defend children, workers, and the general public from pervasive harm,” said Lisa Gilbert, Co-President, Public Citizen.

“I’m thrilled that Representative Jayapal is taking such a leading role in addressing the enormous societal risks posed by increasingly powerful and uncontrollable AI systems. Efforts like the National AI Charter Act to address the full scope of AI harms are more important today than ever before,” said Anthony Aguire, President and CEO, Future of Life Institute.

“Big Tech companies have continually pulled the rug out from under families, workers, and small businesses to build powerful and unaccountable Big Tech monopolies that dictate to us how we should live our own lives. Enough is enough. We are proud to support the National AI Charter Act because it will establish desperately-needed rules of the road, punish AI companies that release dangerous products, and create the clear public benefit that the American people are calling for,” said Sacha Haworth, Executive Director, Tech Oversight Project.

“The same billionaires who walked away with huge tax breaks last year are now racing to take over AI. For years they’ve lobbied every attempt at regulation to death. Representative Jayapal’s plan goes after the source of their power: their monopolies, their surveillance, and their stolen data. It’s the first plan big enough to match the problem, and it puts families back in charge,” said Kristen Crowell, Executive Director, Families Over Billionaires.

“This is not a time for half measures. We are facing serious challenges, if not crises, on every possible front in this country, and we need leaders who are putting forward proposals that meet the moment. This framework puts humans at the center of the debate about AI and regulation and puts power back in the hands of people over the technology that shapes their lives,” said Shaunna Thomas, Executive Director, Guardrails Action.

“We have a long history of governing banks, utilities, critical infrastructure. In all of these, we have leverage over market interests, and the ability to gate access to the market on the condition that the public interest is protected. We need commensurate leverage over large AI companies, and this is the right lineage to draw upon,” said Amba Kak, Co-Executive Director, AI Now.

“Rep. Jayapal is right: if you want to run an AI company in this country, you should have to accept the public’s terms. For too long, Big Tech has acted first and answered for the harm later, if ever. A national charter would change that. We also support her proposal to structurally separate the AI stack. And we urge Congress to consider building on the authorities existing agencies already have. There’s more work ahead to make sure this framework can stand up to Big Tech’s lawyers and lobbyists, and we look forward to doing it with her,” said Nidhi Hegde, Executive Director, American Economic Liberties Project.

“We are in the midst of a reckoning on AI as working families and communities across the country are rightfully standing up and sounding the alarm on the growing harms that this technology is posing on our day to day lives. For too long, Big Tech CEOs have been able to divide and distract policymakers while they use the public’s own data to raise prices, push millions of working people into debt, and rake in record profits. It is long past time for policymakers to break Big Tech’s grip on AI and we applaud Congresswoman Jayapal for unveiling the National AI Charter Act Framework which marks a critical first step in reining in Big Tech and protecting families,” said Mike Pierce, Executive Director, Protect Borrowers.

“It’s unacceptable that Big Tech continues to abuse our data, turbocharge scams, and act with impunity. This framework reflects the interconnectedness of the harms that AI companies are already causing and the necessity of strong, robust enforcement mechanisms that can provide meaningful protections for consumers,” said Susan Weinstock, CEO, Consumer Federation of America.

“We welcome Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s leadership to address AI’s real harms. We’re encouraged to see a comprehensive, structural approach with sharp guardrails and bright lines. For too long, a handful of tech giants have written the rules and remade society to suit themselves. It’s high time the public wrote the future instead,” said Stacy Mitchell, Co-Executive Director, Institute for Local Self-Reliance.

“For far too long, the tech oligarchs and those whom they directly or indirectly fund have sought to normalize how the modern technology sector prefers to operate. Congresswoman Jayapal rightly recognizes as illegitimate those practices that tech oligarchs have long celebrated as creative and adventurous even as they violate longstanding laws and norms. In a democracy, it is publicly elected figures who are responsible for leading the future, not the oligarchic class,” said Jeff Hauser, Executive Director, Revolving Door Project.

“AI poses very real risks to safety, privacy, workers, competition, and more. This range of harms requires a comprehensive, structural policy response. In many critical industries, we mandate charters to do business, impose bright-line bans on problematic conduct, subject firms to independent inspection, and use other common-sense tools to reduce risks. The U.S. needs to deploy these same tools to keep powerful firms accountable and to put the public’s interest first in AI,” said Asad Ramzanali, Director of AI & Technology Policy, Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator.

“This is a smart framework that recognizes how powerful AI companies are already putting the public at risk, exploiting data, and consolidating control over critical technologies and markets. Adopting the charter model offers a sweeping yet adaptable way to welcome innovation while imposing enforceable obligations for safety and fair competition, placing necessary checks on private power, and ensuring corporations develop AI in the public interest,” said Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media and Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute

“AI companies and their executives are threatening working people’s health, safety, and pocketbooks in their reckless race for profits. Congresswoman Jayapal’s National AI Charter framework would take on these threats in a comprehensive way by putting the public interest first and making the existence of AI firms contingent on their compliance with strong safety and privacy requirements alongside worker, consumer, and investor protections,” said Maya Jenkins, Senior Policy Analyst, Americans for Financial Reform.

An outline of the framework can be found here.

The framework was developed, in part, following a hearing that Jayapal hosted on the dangers of surveillance AI conducted by Big Tech.
title: Jayapal Introduces Legislative Framework Establishing National Charter System to Rein in AI

Yesterday, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16), joined by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Mark Pocan (WI-2) and Dina Titus (NV-1), sent a letter to Department of the Navy Secretary Hung Cao requesting more information on the use of swine in hyperbaric diving experiments.

The full letter can be found here or below:

Secretary Cao:

We are writing to express our strong concern regarding the Department of the Navy funded research projects involving the use of swine in hyperbaric diving experiments, specifically the recent study conducted at Duke University utilizing animal models to test breathing gas switches involving carbon tetrafluoride.

While we recognize the vital importance of ensuring the safety, health, and operational readiness of our divers and submariners, we remain deeply troubled by the continued reliance on animal testing when novel scientific methods and advanced models exist and should be fully exhausted. Specifically, the research recently published titled "Isobaric counterdiffusion of carbon tetrafluoride breathing gas to prevent severe decompression sickness" subjected juvenile swine to extreme pressure profiles, rapid decompressions, and severe physiological distress to evaluate decompression sickness mitigation, leading to mortality for some of the swine.

As advocates for animal welfare standards, we question whether the Department has thoroughly exhausted non-animal methodologies. We request that the Department of the Navy provide responses to the following questions within 30 days:

Have there been insistences on where alternative methods are the preferred method to live, animal testing? If so, what were the reasonings behind those decisions and the effectiveness of the results?

What specific validation protocols are used to ensure that all non-animal testing alternatives are fully exhausted before any animal models are approved for use?

Does the Navy enforce protocols or data-sharing agreements to prevent redundant animal testing on the same research questions across different laboratories or research groups

How many total studies are planned under this overarching research initiative, and what is the projected timeline for concluding all associated animal testing?

What specific military or operational necessity required the use of live pigs rather than advanced computer or lab-based modeling for this research? What total amount of federal funding from the Department of Defense has been allocated to institutions for animal testing over the past five fiscal years?

What specific steps are being taken by the Navy to transition toward non-animal methods?

Our national security and the health of our service members are paramount, but we must achieve these goals ethically and responsibly. We look forward to your prompt response and to working together to ensure taxpayer funds support both naval innovation and high standards of animal welfare.
title: Congresswoman Escobar Sends Navy Letter Requesting More Information on the Use of Swine in Diving Experiments

CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) and Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12) announced $11,023,181 in federal funding to upgrade thousands of feet of lighting and pavement on Runway 10L/28R at the Pittsburgh International Airport (PIT), further modernizing Western Pennsylvanians’ go-to airport.

The U.S. Department of Transportation awards this money through the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The multi-phase funding will help extend the service life of the runway, minimize Foreign Object Debris (FOD), improve aircrafts’ ride quality, and make the airfield safer at Pittsburgh International Airport.

“We in Western Pennsylvanians should be able to rely on the safety and reliability of our infrastructure,” said Congressman Deluzio. “That’s why I am excited to announce another round of federal funding that will help make the Pittsburgh Airport one of the safest and most modern airports in the world.”

“Pittsburgh International Airport is one of the gateways to Western Pennsylvania, and the infrastructure behind it has to be safe, reliable, and ready for the people and workers who depend on it every single day,” said Congresswoman Lee. “This more than $11 million federal investment is exactly what public dollars should be doing: coming back home, strengthening the things our communities rely on, supporting good jobs, and making sure a major piece of our regional economy is built to last. I’m glad to see this funding headed home to Pittsburgh International Airport, and I’ll keep fighting to bring federal investment back to Western Pennsylvania.”

“Airports across the country are part of national critical infrastructure and federal support is key in helping to keep the national airspace moving. Pittsburgh International Airport is an important economic driver for our region and this grant helps to fund airfield improvements at PIT including runway paving and upgrading lighting infrastructure. Thank you to Congressman Deluzio and our entire federal delegation for their continued support,” said Pittsburgh International Airport CEO Christina Cassotis.

###
title: Deluzio, Lee Announce $11 Million More in Federal Funding for Safety Upgrades at Pittsburgh Airport

WASHINGTON – Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN), Chair of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, Rep. John Garamendi (D-CA), Co-Chair of the Ethiopian American Caucus and member of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, and Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), member of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, released the following statement on hostilities in Ethiopia:

“We are deeply alarmed by increasing violence in Ethiopia, including the Ethiopian military strike last week on an aid convoy delivering assistance in Tigray.

"The 2022 Pretoria Agreement that silenced the guns in Northern Ethiopia committed all parties to ceasing hostilities, protecting civilians, allowing humanitarian access to those affected, and undertaking comprehensive transitional justice to hold those responsible for human rights abuses and violations responsible. Unfortunately, this agreement has not been upheld, and these conditions have not been met.

"This increased conflict threatens the entire country and the region as a whole, which is already reeling from the previous war in Northern Ethiopia and the devastating conflict in Sudan. Ordinary civilians are bearing the brunt of this violence.

"We urge all parties in Ethiopia to immediately recommit to peace negotiations and uphold their responsibilities under the Pretoria Agreement. Ethiopia’s neighbors and the international community must work to defuse tensions and facilitate peace.

"We also urge the U.S. State Department to work with all parties to end the violence and hold those responsible accountable. The people of Ethiopia deserve peace and justice.”

###
title: Omar, Garamendi, McGovern Release Statement on Hostilities in Ethiopia

Representative Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Schumer Introduce Bicameral Legislation to Restore Health Coverage for 450,000 New Yorkers
Press Release
Because of Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, over 450,000 New Yorkers lost Essential Plan coverage.
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) led the entire New York Democratic delegation in the introduction of the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act. The Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act would restore health coverage to the nearly 450,000 New Yorkers who were kicked off of the Essential Plan under the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
“Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act represents the largest loss of healthcare in American history. Apart from cutting nearly $1 trillion from Medicaid, this bill specifically targeted New York by gutting the Essential Plan and stripping almost half a million New Yorkers of their health insurance. We must take immediate steps to repeal the harmful impacts of H.R. 1 on New York” said Representative Ocasio-Cortez. “Today, I am introducing the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act alongside Senator Schumer and the entire New York Democratic Delegation to reinstate federal funding for the New York Essential Plan and ensure that New Yorkers can once again access this critical health program.”
“Make no mistake, the ‘Big, Ugly Bill’ has been a disaster that has left American families sicker, poorer, and less safe,” said Leader Schumer. “Republicans promised lower health care costs, but they delivered soaring premiums, sky-high deductibles, and coverage ripped away from millions – all to give billionaires and big corporations a tax cut. In an act of political retribution, Republicans specifically targeted New Yorkers, kicking nearly half a million people off their coverage. Leaving working families with no affordable alternatives isn’t policy; it’s punishment. And it undermines public health and the health of our vital hospitals and community health centers. We must work to pass this legislation, reverse this cruel policy, and restore health insurance to all New Yorkers.”
“H.R. 1 decimated New York’s Essential Plan, ripping health insurance coverage from hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers and weakening the finances of every hospital in the State. That’s why the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act is so critically important. It would repeal this terrible HR 1 policy and establish a permanent option for expanded basic health plan coverage. New York’s hospital community is deeply grateful to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and the New York delegation Democrats for championing this effort to expand health insurance and strengthen New York’s health care safety net,” said Kenneth E. Raske, President, Greater New York Hospital Association.
“Losing coverage can force patients to delay care, skip medications, or make impossible choices between their health and other basic needs. Community health centers care for everyone who walks through their doors, whether they have insurance or not, and as more New Yorkers lose coverage, the strain on CHCs and their patients grows,” said Rose Duhan, president and CEO of the Community Health Care Association of New York State. “Ensuring New Yorkers have coverage helps patients get the care they need, when they need it, from providers they know and trust. CHCANYS is proud to support the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act.”
“HANYS strongly supports the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, which would reverse H.R. 1’s harmful limitations on New Yorkers’ eligibility for this affordable health insurance option and provide states the flexibility to extend this coverage to individuals with incomes up to 250% of the federal poverty line,” said Thomas J. Quatroche Jr., PhD, president and CEO, Healthcare Association of New York State. “Affordable health coverage is becoming out of reach for many New Yorkers, and H.R. 1 threatens to leave even more people uninsured. HANYS applauds Senate Minority Leader Schumer and Rep. Ocasio-Cortez for introducing this important bill and for their ongoing dedication to protecting and improving all New Yorkers’ access to healthcare coverage and care.”
“This legislation would reverse some of the worst harms of H.R. 1 and allow more New Yorkers to access affordable health insurance coverage,” said Mitchell Katz, MD President and CEO of NYC Health + Hospitals. “Our health care system is grateful to Senator Schumer and Representative Ocasio-Cortez for their leadership and commitment to keeping New Yorkers connected to care.”
The legislation would repeal the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s premium tax credit eligibility restrictions, fully restoring funding for the Essential Plan. In addition to restoring the program, the legislation would provide all states with the option to expand health coverage through the Affordable Care Act’s Basic Health Plan.
This legislation is cosponsored by the entire New York Democratic delegation including: Senator Gillibrand (D-NY), Leader Jeffries (NY-08), and Representatives Clarke (NY-09), Espaillat (NY-13), Gillen (NY-04), Goldman (NY-10), Kennedy (NY-26), Latimer (NY-16), Mannion (NY-22), Meeks (NY-5), Meng (NY-6), Morelle (NY-25), Nadler (NY-12), Riley (NY-19), Ryan (NY-18), Suozzi (NY-3), Tonko (NY-20), Torres (NY-15), and Velázquez (NY-07).

Ranking Member Scott Statement on the Trump Administration’s National School Voucher Scheme
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s new proposed rule, entitled “Federal Scholarship Tax Credit.”
“America's public school system is founded on the promise that all students should have access to a high-quality public education. Today, the Treasury Department issued a proposed rule to implement the massive federal voucher scheme that was included in the Republicans’ ‘Big Ugly Bill.’ The program effectively diverts billions of taxpayer dollars away from public schools through the voucher program to subsidize private school education. Today’s proposal goes even further by prohibiting states from adding requirements to ensure the program meaningfully benefits public schools and the students who attend them. It also prohibits states from adding additional requirements to ensure students do not face discrimination when accessing educational services.
“Voucher schemes are inefficient, ineffective, and an expensive tool to privatize public education. If just 20 percent of eligible donors participate in the voucher scheme, the cost to the taxpayer would be roughly $37.6 billion — more than all federal spending on Title I and the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) combined. Meanwhile, data from existing state voucher programs shows that most students who benefit from those programs are already enrolled in private schools. Yet ninety percent of America’s children attend public schools. Despite this, public education has gone underfunded for decades. Without long term, sustained federal investment, schools and educators lack the resources they need to teach all students effectively.
“Moreover, when federal dollars go to public schools, schools are required to use that money to serve all students equally without discrimination. By funneling these dollars into private schools, taxpayers are unwittingly paying for schools that neglect underprivileged communities, are permitted to ignore civil rights laws, and can freely discriminate against students without accountability.
“Public dollars should be spent on public education. Just imagine what we could do if this money were used to improve all of America’s public schools instead. Democrats are committed to investing in public education for all communities — not just the privileged few.”

(Washington, DC) – On Monday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) sent a letter to Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Chris Wright demanding that he answer multiple months-overdue oversight requests from the Committee regarding DOE’s 2025 award terminations.

“For more than 15 months, my colleagues and I have attempted to conduct oversight of DOE’s award termination activities,” writes Ranking Member Lofgren in her letter. “We have asked questions, requested documents, and demanded answers directly from you during official testimony. But DOE has thwarted our oversight repeatedly by refusing to provide the requested information and documents. In doing so, DOE has hindered our ability to evaluate DOE’s actions and obstructed the Committee’s ability to fulfill its constitutional role. The following oversight requests from the 119th Congress remain outstanding, and DOE must comply with them.

1. Please provide to the Committee a comprehensive list of DOE officials who participated in the “Portfolio Review Process” in 2025 and 2026.

2. Please provide to the Committee copies of the “one pagers” or “one-page summary memos” that were created for each award being reviewed as a part of the “Portfolio Review Process.”

3. Please provide to the Committee copies of the assessments that were completed for each award terminated in May 2025 and October 2025 for the purpose of evaluating whether those awards had sufficiently met the criteria utilized by DOE under the “Portfolio Review Process.”

“Secretary Wright, these are straightforward requests for specific documents and information. I cannot help but believe that your ultimate goal in refusing to comply with them is to evade responsibility for your actions. Did you believe that you could arbitrarily terminate billions of dollars’ worth of awards, lie about the reasons why, and escape accountability? Now, as the political consequences of your actions mount, it appears you hope to quietly walk away from the entire issue, while Congress simply moves on without holding you accountable. That hope would be mistaken. Congressional oversight must be respected, and my oversight requests must be complied with. If DOE fails to do so, we will redouble our efforts using every available tool at our disposal. I urge DOE to comply now.”

Access the letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Wright,

In 2025, the Trump Administration illegally began to erase all traces of federal activity that it disagreed with. At the Department of Energy (DOE), you led the charge. You targeted billions of dollars’ worth of clean energy and infrastructure investments, engaged in a politicized “review” to cast a veneer of legitimacy over your arbitrary decisions, terminated awards that you disliked in a manner that was designed to inflict maximum pain on your political opponents, and then lied continuously to the public about why you had done it. The process was a sham and a disgrace, unworthy of the oath you swore to uphold the Constitution.

But now, as lawsuits accumulate, criticism mounts, and judges declare your actions illegal, you do not seem quite as proud of the decisions that were supposedly so righteous a year ago. Indeed, you appear eager to distance yourself from the award terminations of 2025 and to avoid responsibility for them. Since the early spring of 2025, I have attempted to conduct oversight of the Department’s actions to get to the bottom of what happened. DOE has evaded my oversight at every turn. This letter serves to reaffirm that my prior oversight requests from the 119th Congress pertaining to DOE’s award terminations remain outstanding. I expect DOE to comply. If the Department does not, it should prepare to face the consequences of its obstruction.

The story of DOE’s award terminations in 2025 has been told so many times by this point that it barely needs retelling. I will briefly do so merely to provide context for my oversight requests related to the issue. Upon taking office in January 2025, the Trump Administration immediately froze tens of billions of dollars’ worth of research, development, demonstration, and commercialization projects at DOE that had been awarded under the Biden Administration. In your first Secretarial Order on February 5th, 2025, released two days after you were confirmed as Secretary of Energy, you announced that DOE would “comprehensively review its R&D portfolio” without providing any additional detail. On May 15th, 2025, you initiated a new process to “conduct focused reviews of awards and other forms of financial assistance on a caseby-case basis,” while asserting that DOE possessed the discretion to “terminate [a] project based on the outcome of DOE’s evaluation.” This process, called the “Portfolio Review Process” or PRP, moved suspiciously quickly. A mere two weeks later, on May 30th, 2025, DOE announced the termination of 24 awards issued by the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) totaling more than $3.7 billion. Several months after that, on October 1st, 2025, DOE announced the termination of 321 additional awards from across the Department totaling roughly $7.56 billion. In both instances, DOE claimed that the terminations resulted from a “thorough and individualized financial review of each award,” during which the Department had concluded that the awards “were not economically viable and would not generate a positive return on investment of taxpayer dollars.” After the October 2025 award terminations, DOE also asserted that the awards “did not adequately advance the nation’s energy needs.” Finally, in April 2026, you appeared before a House Appropriations Subcommittee and testified that the PRP was complete and that no additional award terminations would be forthcoming.

The repercussions of DOE’s award terminations were immense. Projects were thrown into chaos, companies were pushed to the brink of collapse, and jobs were lost. Taxpayer dollars were wasted. Major clean energy research, development, and demonstration projects – indeed, entire nascent clean energy sectors – were destabilized. Congressional energy priorities enshrined in law were thwarted. We continue to deal with the fallout of these award terminations to this day. From the beginning, as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (“the Committee”), I sought to conduct oversight of DOE’s actions in order to understand the processes and motivations that lay behind the Department’s attempt to wipe out over ten billion dollars in taxpayer-funded awards. On May 5th, 2025, I sent a letter to DOE along with a group of my Ranking Member colleagues in the House of Representatives and Senate that condemned the Department’s comprehensive freeze and review of Biden-era awards as “illegal and harmful to the public.” We asked how “DOE or any other part of the administration [is] assessing which DOE projects to cancel or continue, and under what criteria?” We did not receive a response from the Department before the PRP was announced on May 15th and $3.7 billion in awards was terminated on May 31st.

After DOE terminated the first round of awards on May 31st, Department officials provided a briefing for Committee Staff. Based upon the information disclosed in that briefing, I sent another letter to DOE on September 9th, 2025, along with two other Ranking Members, expressing “serious concerns” that the PRP was “haphazard, disorganized, and politically driven,” and calling upon DOE to “cease the cancellation process and restore respect for independent, merit-based reviews.” We also requested specific documents created during the Department’s review of OCED awards related to DOE’s evaluation of those awards and its assessment of whether the awards should be terminated, as well as a comprehensive list of DOE officials who had participated in the review process. DOE never provided those requested documents.

When DOE terminated more than $7.5 billion worth of awards on October 1st, 2025, the Department publicly claimed that the terminations were rooted in policy-based criteria such as economic viability, taxpayer return, and national energy priorities. You denied any political motivation behind the terminations in congressional testimony as recently as April and June 2026.3 But DOE’s cover story unraveled due to an unlikely source: its own concessions in court. Over the course of one lawsuit filed in November 2025, DOE formally stipulated that “a primary reason” for the October 2025 award terminations was “whether the grantee was located in a ‘Blue State’”; a judge ruled that DOE’s award terminations were unconstitutional and illegal in January 2026. Over the course of a second lawsuit related to the same terminations, DOE went even further and formally stipulated that the October 2025 award terminations were “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state,” and that they were not based upon “any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction, or performance-based factor.”

When you testified before the Science Committee on June 10th, 2026, Science Committee Democrats confronted you about the award terminations and reiterated the oversight requests that I had previously made to DOE. One of my colleagues, Energy Subcommittee Ranking Member Deborah Ross, demanded that DOE disclose the identities of the Department officials who participated in the PRP; once again, you refused to do so. Another one of my colleagues, Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo, pressed you to explain the contradiction between your denials of any political motivation in the award terminations and DOE’s formal concessions in the November 2025 lawsuit; once again, you denied that any of the October 2025 award termination decisions were made based on politics. It was July 2026, the very next month, when DOE’s formal concessions in the second lawsuit – even more sweeping – became public, even though you had surely known about them when you testified before the Science Committee. Your materially false statements to the Committee left me with no choice but to formally refer you to the Department of Justice, which I did along with Ranking Member Amo on August 4th, 2026.

For more than 15 months, my colleagues and I have attempted to conduct oversight of DOE’s award termination activities. We have asked questions, requested documents, and demanded answers directly from you during official testimony. But DOE has thwarted our oversight repeatedly by refusing to provide the requested information and documents. In doing so, DOE has hindered our ability to evaluate DOE’s actions and obstructed the Committee’s ability to fulfill its constitutional role. The following oversight requests from the 119th Congress remain outstanding, and DOE must comply with them. Please provide the requested information and documents no later than 5:00 PM on Wednesday, October 14th, 2026:

1. Please provide to the Committee a comprehensive list of DOE officials who participated in the “Portfolio Review Process” in 2025 and 2026.

2. Please provide to the Committee copies of the “one pagers” or “one-page summary memos” that were created for each award being reviewed as a part of the “Portfolio Review Process.”

3. Please provide to the Committee copies of the assessments that were completed for each award terminated in May 2025 and October 2025 for the purpose of evaluating whether those awards had sufficiently met the criteria utilized by DOE under the “Portfolio Review Process.”

Secretary Wright, these are straightforward requests for specific documents and information. I cannot help but believe that your ultimate goal in refusing to comply with them is to evade responsibility for your actions. Did you believe that you could arbitrarily terminate billions of dollars’ worth of awards, lie about the reasons why, and escape accountability? Now, as the political consequences of your actions mount, it appears you hope to quietly walk away from the entire issue, while Congress simply moves on without holding you accountable. That hope would be mistaken. Congressional oversight must be respected, and my oversight requests must be complied with. If DOE fails to do so, we will redouble our efforts using every available tool at our disposal. I urge DOE to comply now.

Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” The Committee possesses jurisdiction over “all energy research, development, and demonstration, and projects therefor, and all federally owned or operated nonmilitary energy laboratories, as well as the commercial application of energy technologies.”

Rep. Chu, Sen. Whitehouse Reintroduce Legislation to End Billionaires’ Tax-Free Giveaways to Dark Money Groups
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (RI) reintroduced the End Tax Breaks for Dark Money Act, legislation to close a tax loophole that allows billionaires to avoid capital gains taxes by donating appreciated assets to dark money groups, effectively subsidizing the flow of secret money into American elections.
Since the Supreme Court’s Citizens United decision in 2010 opened the floodgates to unlimited political spending, dark money has exploded in American elections. Political spending by groups that do not disclose their donors has surged from $103 million in the decade before the ruling to more than $1 billion in the decade after. In 2024, a record $1.9 billion in dark money flooded federal races, the most ever spent in a single U.S. election cycle. These groups have poured millions into campaigns that spread misinformation on issues from COVID-19 to climate change, all without ever telling the public who funds them.
The tax code gives some of these wealthy donors another advantage. Normally, when millionaires or billionaires sell assets that have increased in value, they owe capital gains taxes on that increase. And Congress has already made clear that donors cannot avoid those taxes simply by transferring appreciated assets to Section 527 political organizations, including PACs.
But a glaring loophole remains: that same rule does not apply to organizations organized under Sections 501(c)(4), (5), and (6) of the tax code. That means billionaires can pour highly valuable stock and other assets into dark money groups without paying a dime in taxes on their gains.
The End Tax Breaks for Dark Money Act would close that loophole. The bill would apply the same tax treatment to transfers of appreciated property to 501(c)(4), (5), and (6) organizations that already applies to transfers to Section 527 political organizations. Simply put: billionaires would not get a special tax break for pouring their wealth into dark money groups and corrupting our political system.
“Dark money has exploded since Citizens United, from under $5 million in 2006 to nearly $2 billion in the last election cycle alone, and it’s already flooding this year’s midterms. Billionaires already have outsized power over our politics. Even worse, they can secretly funnel their wealth into dark money groups and get a tax subsidy for it, an advantage traditional political donors don’t get,” said Rep. Chu. “That’s why I’ve partnered with Senator Whitehouse to reintroduce the End Tax Breaks for Dark Money Act. Our bill would close this loophole by applying the same tax rules we already apply to gifts to political organizations, so billionaires don’t get a free ride for bankrolling our elections in the shadows.”
“Billionaire donors attempting to wield influence from the shadows should not be rewarded with giant tax write-offs,” said Sen. Whitehouse. “My legislation with Rep. Chu would end taxpayer subsidies for dark money donations and limit the flood of toxic dark money slime that’s corrupting our political system.”
“We welcome the introduction of the End Tax Breaks for Dark Money Act. For years, the ultra-wealthy have exploited and rigged our broken tax system to their advantage, funneling billions into political campaigns while collecting hundreds of millions in tax breaks,” said Jodie Rubenstein, executive director of Americans for Tax Fairness. “This bill is a practical first step in taking on the power of dark money in our politics. It closes a tax loophole that allows wealthy donors to sidestep capital gains taxes by giving appreciated assets to politically active groups rather than paying taxes on the profit. To have a functioning democracy, we can’t incentivize or reward billionaires who seek to force their will on the political system.”
“Until Congress finally gets around to outlawing Dark Money contributions altogether, the least it can do is ensure everyday taxpayers don’t subsidize Dark Money contributions from the super-rich,” said Robert Weissman, co-president of Public Citizen. “Sen. Whitehouse and Rep. Chu’s End Tax Breaks for Dark Money Act is common-sense legislation that should win support from every single member of Congress.”
“There is no justifiable reason why rich people like me should be allowed to dominate our political system by donating massive sums of money to dark money political groups while also claiming a tax break in the process. When our tax code allows super-rich people to manipulate the levers of government while paying almost no taxes, it enables millionaires and billionaires to circumvent the democratic process and rewards them financially for doing so,” said Morris Pearl, Chairman of the Patriotic Millionaires and a former Managing Director at BlackRock. "Our democracy is not for sale. If Congress allows the influence of the ultra-rich to go unchecked, we can only expect America to continue to tip further and further into an oligarchy. The Patriotic Millionaires applaud Rep. Chu, Sen. Whitehouse, and all their congressional colleagues for standing up against billionaires attempting to buy our democracy and be rewarded for it."
“This Act is a critical tool that will help address runaway inequality by closing a tax loophole exploited by the ultra-wealthy and reducing the influence of oligarchs over our society,” said Nabil Ahmed, Senior Director of Economic Justice at Oxfam America.
The bill is cosponsored by Reps. Danny Davis (IL-07), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Laura Friedman (CA-30), Jesús "Chuy" García (IL-04), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Summer Lee (PA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12).
The End Tax Breaks for Dark Money Act is endorsed by AFL-CIO, Common Cause, the Excessive Wealth Disorder Institute (EWDi), Demand Progress, End Citizens United / Let America Vote, the Economic Policy Institute, the Institute for Policy Studies’ Program on Inequality, NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice, Oxfam America, Patriotic Millionaires, Public Citizen, Americans for Tax Fairness, United Steelworkers (USW).

Ranking Member McCollum Statement on U.S. Withdrawal from Iraq
SAINT PAUL, Minn. — Congresswoman McCollum, ranking member of the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee released the following statement after U.S. forces formally withdrew from Iraq after two decades:
“Today marks the end of America’s military mission in Iraq with the conclusion of Operation Inherent Resolve and withdrawal of the last remaining U.S. forces from Iraqi territory. More than 23 years ago, America began the war in Iraq based on lies. In 2002, I was one of 133 members of the House of Representatives to vote against the Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution,” said Rep. McCollum. “At the time I believed that President Bush’s decision to take America to war was terribly wrong. I stand by my vote and believe that history has vindicated it. The Iraq War was a catastrophe that cost the lives of thousands of U.S. service members and well over 100,000 Iraqis. It unleashed a torrent of conflict across the Middle East, including the rise of the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria. We continue to live with the consequences. To every American who served in Iraq, our nation owes you a debt of gratitude, especially to those who made the ultimate sacrifice on behalf of our nation and those who returned with wounds both seen and unseen. Your families deserve our thanks and our support. We acknowledge and appreciate the many contributions of our international allies.
“As we reflect on the end of America’s mission in Iraq, our leaders in Washington must heed the lessons of the Iraq War. Once again, our nation is mired in another destructive war of choice in the Middle East launched by a Republican President. President Trump must understand that there is no military solution to our conflict with Iran. Mr. President, negotiate an end to the Iran War and bring our troops home safely.”

Reps. Salinas, Ramirez Introduce Legislation to Require the Federal Government to Share Evidence with Local Law Enforcement in DHS Use-of-Force Incidents
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representatives Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Delia Ramirez (IL-03) introduced the ICE Shootings Transparency Act to provide local and state law enforcement agencies unfettered access to evidence in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer-involved shootings and other use of force incidents.
“When an ICE or CBP agent kills or injures someone in our community, transparency needs to be the bare minimum,” said Rep. Salinas. “Since the start of the second Trump Administration, the federal government has often refused to provide local law enforcement with critical evidence in shootings and other use-of-force incidents involving ICE and CBP officers. My bill would ensure that when these incidents occur, state and local law enforcement agencies would have unrestricted access to this evidence to deliver full justice to victims and their families.”
“DHS lies to avoid accountability. DHS agents use reckless and unlawful force and then DHS issues public statements justifying the use of force that are repeatedly proven false or highly misleading,” said Congresswoman Ramirez.“That’s why I’m joining Rep. Salinas to require DHS and the Attorney General to share evidence related to shootings by ICE and CBP officers with local law enforcement agencies to carry out investigations. We will not stop until we have justice for every person that was killed or harmed at the hands of DHS agents. We will reimagine true safety, abolish ICE, dismantle DHS, and hold all perpetrators accountable.”
In January 2026, when ICE killed Renee Good, Minnesota’s Bureau of Criminal Apprehension was tapped to conduct a joint investigation with the FBI. However, shortly after the announcement, the state agency said that they had been kicked out of the investigation, leaving the investigation in the hands of the Trump Administration. Several months later, ICE agents killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas and have also refused to work with state and local law enforcement. This has included blocking local and state law enforcement officials from accessing investigatory materials, such as Salgado Araujo’s work van and the scene of the incident.
Reps. Salinas and Ramirez introduced the ICE Shootings Transparency Act to address this issue that some local law enforcement agencies have encountered with ICE and CBP officers involved shootings that result in the injury or death of a civilian. Their bill would require the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Attorney General to share evidence on an ongoing basis with appropriate local law enforcement agencies related to shootings by ICE and CBP officers that injure or kill someone.
Additionally, this bill would require DHS and the Attorney General to provide access to the location of the incident to state and local law enforcement agencies with jurisdiction over the area to carry out regular investigative functions.
The ICE Shootings Transparency Act is cosponsored by Reps. Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-At Large), Jim Costa (CA-21), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Steven Horsford (NV-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), and Sylvia Garcia (TX-29).
The legislation is endorsed by the National Immigration Law Center (NILC).
In February, Salinas introduced the ICE and CBP Constitutional Accountability Actto hold the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) liable for violating individuals’ constitutional rights.

Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies, is pressing Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin to stop delaying meaningful federal action on per-and polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in sewage sludge. In a letter to Zeldin, Pingree warns that EPA’s latest draft guidance fails to provide a clear path toward enforceable protections for farmers, rural communities, and the nation’s food supply. The guidance was issued instead of finalizing EPA’s January 2025 draft risk assessment—which would have been an important step toward restricting the application of PFAS-contaminated sewage sludge, also known as biosolids, on farmland.

“As you and I have discussed at length, PFAS chemicals have been linked to serious health effects, including cancer, reproductive and developmental harms, and weakened immune systems. Maine farmers have had their livelihoods disrupted due to PFAS contamination, which originated in sewage sludge that was spread as fertilizer by farmers who were told by the government that it was safe to use,”Pingree wrote. “Unfortunately, this sewage sludge contained PFAS, leading to contamination of agricultural land, products, and water.”

Maine has been at the forefront of testing, cleanup, and research into PFAS contamination of farmland. An extensive state investigation found contamination on more than 50 farms linked to sewage sludge application. Farmers have lost income, faced threats to their livelihoods, and experienced health problems after unknowingly spreading contaminated sludge that government authorities had said was safe. Yet instead of completing its risk assessment and tightening protections for farmers and rural communities, Trump’s EPA released draft guidance this summer that leaves its regulatory plans unresolved.

“[...] Rather than finalizing this risk assessment, the Agency’s release of Draft Guidance for Reducing Risk from PFOA and PFOS in Biosolids leaves regulatory next steps unclear and farmers in limbo,” Pingree said.

With the public comment period on the guidance scheduled to close October 5, Pingree is calling on Zeldin to explain:

Whether EPA intends to finalize its draft sewage sludge risk assessment for PFOA and PFOS;

What scientific review supports a decision not to finalize it;

How EPA will prevent further contamination and protect farmers from the unique exposure risks created by land application of sewage sludge;

When EPA will propose enforceable limits on land application;

Whether EPA will address PFAS chemicals beyond PFOA and PFOS; and

How EPA is working with the Department of Agriculture to help farmers, ranchers, and rural communities manage PFAS contamination.

“Without additional action by EPA, farmers across the country will continue to be at heightened risk from PFAS exposure from land application of biosolids,” Pingree wrote. “It is critical that EPA takes additional steps to protect our rural communities and food supply.”

The full letter is available here and is copied below.

+++

Dear Administrator Zeldin,

I write to you regarding the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) efforts to reduce risk from per-and polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in sewage sludge, also known as biosolids. As you and I have discussed at length, PFAS chemicals have been linked to serious health effects, including cancer, reproductive and developmental harms, and weakened immune systems. Maine farmers have had their livelihoods disrupted due to PFAS contamination, which originated in sewage sludge that was spread as fertilizer by farmers who were told by the government that it was safe to use. Unfortunately, this sewage sludge contained PFAS, leading to contamination of agricultural land, products, and water.

Maine is far from the only state in this situation, but we have been on the front lines on testing, cleanup, and research. An extensive state investigation found contamination found on over 50 farms because of sewage sludge. These farmers have had their livelihoods lost or threatened and experienced health problems. This is an issue across the country whether states are taking action or not, and it is imperative the federal government, and EPA specifically, continues to advance research and remediation efforts to protect our food supply and rural economies, including by actively preventing additional contamination.

EPA’s Draft Sewage Sludge Risk Assessment for Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) and Perfluorooctane Sulfonic Acid (PFOS), released in January 2025, was an important step towards eventual restrictions on applying contaminated sludge to farmland, but rather than finalizing this risk assessment, the Agency’s release of Draft Guidance for Reducing Risk from PFOA and PFOS in Biosolids leaves regulatory next steps unclear and farmers in limbo.

Please respond to these questions by November 16, 2026:

Does EPA intend to finalize the Draft Sewage Sludge Risk Assessment for Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) and Perfluorooctane Sulfonic Acid (PFOS)?

If not, how is that decision documented, and what scientific review supported that conclusion?

If not, how does EPA intend to prevent additional land contamination and protect farmers specifically from the additional, unique exposure pathways they face from land application of sewage sludge?

What are EPA’s next steps to propose enforceable regulatory limits on land application of sewage sludge?

Does EPA plan to expand its focus beyond PFOA and PFOS to other types of PFAS contamination?

How is EPA working with USDA to help farmers, ranchers, and rural communities manage PFAS impacts in agricultural settings?

Without additional action by EPA, farmers across the country will continue to be at heightened risk from PFAS exposure from land application of biosolids. It is critical that EPA takes additional steps to protect our rural communities and food supply. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
title: Pingree Presses Zeldin for Action as EPA Leaves Farmers in Limbo on PFAS-Contaminated Sludge

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congressman Richard E. Neal (D-MA-01) and U.S. Congressman Mike Kelly (R-PA-16), Co-Chairs of the Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus, led the Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus in a letter addressed to Secretary of State for Northern Ireland Chris Bryant, calling on the Government of the United Kingdom to cancel the Orange Order parade on Garvaghy Road.

“Over the last three decades, the progress made on the island of Ireland has been nothing short of extraordinary. Twenty-eight years have passed since the signing of the Good Friday Agreement, and a generation has grown without a single memory of the Troubles,” the lawmakers wrote. “It was that same 28-year period that saw the end of the controversial Orange Order marches on Garvaghy Road in a majority-Catholic area of Portadown. During the Troubles, these parades became a symbol of the sectarian tensions, public disorder, and violence that once threatened Northern Ireland’s peace.

“This is a consequential moment on the island of Ireland, which is why we respectfully urge you to put a stop to this march,” continued the lawmakers.”Failing to intervene and allowing this contentious parade to move forward would risk undermining the progress that has been painstakingly built over the past three decades. As a guarantor of the Good Friday Agreement, the United States has a vested interest in seeing the principles embodied in the accord upheld, ensuring the gains we have achieved can be enjoyed for generations to come.”

A copy of the letter can be found here.

###
title: Neal, Kelly Lead Congressional Friends of Ireland Caucus in Letter Calling for UK Government to Cancel Orange Order Parade on Garvaghy Road

Lofgren Demands Answers to Overdue Oversight Requests Regarding DOE Award Terminations, Warns Secretary Wright of Consequences for Continued Evasion
(Washington, DC) – On Monday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) sent a letter to Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Chris Wright demanding that he answer multiple months-overdue oversight requests from the Committee regarding DOE’s 2025 award terminations.
“For more than 15 months, my colleagues and I have attempted to conduct oversight of DOE’s award termination activities,” writes Ranking Member Lofgren in her letter. “We have asked questions, requested documents, and demanded answers directly from you during official testimony. But DOE has thwarted our oversight repeatedly by refusing to provide the requested information and documents. In doing so, DOE has hindered our ability to evaluate DOE’s actions and obstructed the Committee’s ability to fulfill its constitutional role. The following oversight requests from the 119th Congress remain outstanding, and DOE must comply with them.
1. Please provide to the Committee a comprehensive list of DOE officials who participated in the “Portfolio Review Process” in 2025 and 2026.
2. Please provide to the Committee copies of the “one pagers” or “one-page summary memos” that were created for each award being reviewed as a part of the “Portfolio Review Process.”
3. Please provide to the Committee copies of the assessments that were completed for each award terminated in May 2025 and October 2025 for the purpose of evaluating whether those awards had sufficiently met the criteria utilized by DOE under the “Portfolio Review Process.”
“Secretary Wright, these are straightforward requests for specific documents and information. I cannot help but believe that your ultimate goal in refusing to comply with them is to evade responsibility for your actions. Did you believe that you could arbitrarily terminate billions of dollars’ worth of awards, lie about the reasons why, and escape accountability? Now, as the political consequences of your actions mount, it appears you hope to quietly walk away from the entire issue, while Congress simply moves on without holding you accountable. That hope would be mistaken. Congressional oversight must be respected, and my oversight requests must be complied with. If DOE fails to do so, we will redouble our efforts using every available tool at our disposal. I urge DOE to comply now.”
Access the letter here and below.
Dear Secretary Wright,
In 2025, the Trump Administration illegally began to erase all traces of federal activity that it disagreed with. At the Department of Energy (DOE), you led the charge. You targeted billions of dollars’ worth of clean energy and infrastructure investments, engaged in a politicized “review” to cast a veneer of legitimacy over your arbitrary decisions, terminated awards that you disliked in a manner that was designed to inflict maximum pain on your political opponents, and then lied continuously to the public about why you had done it. The process was a sham and a disgrace, unworthy of the oath you swore to uphold the Constitution.
But now, as lawsuits accumulate, criticism mounts, and judges declare your actions illegal, you do not seem quite as proud of the decisions that were supposedly so righteous a year ago. Indeed, you appear eager to distance yourself from the award terminations of 2025 and to avoid responsibility for them. Since the early spring of 2025, I have attempted to conduct oversight of the Department’s actions to get to the bottom of what happened. DOE has evaded my oversight at every turn. This letter serves to reaffirm that my prior oversight requests from the 119th Congress pertaining to DOE’s award terminations remain outstanding. I expect DOE to comply. If the Department does not, it should prepare to face the consequences of its obstruction.
The story of DOE’s award terminations in 2025 has been told so many times by this point that it barely needs retelling. I will briefly do so merely to provide context for my oversight requests related to the issue. Upon taking office in January 2025, the Trump Administration immediately froze tens of billions of dollars’ worth of research, development, demonstration, and commercialization projects at DOE that had been awarded under the Biden Administration. In your first Secretarial Order on February 5th, 2025, released two days after you were confirmed as Secretary of Energy, you announced that DOE would “comprehensively review its R&D portfolio” without providing any additional detail. On May 15th, 2025, you initiated a new process to “conduct focused reviews of awards and other forms of financial assistance on a caseby-case basis,” while asserting that DOE possessed the discretion to “terminate [a] project based on the outcome of DOE’s evaluation.” This process, called the “Portfolio Review Process” or PRP, moved suspiciously quickly. A mere two weeks later, on May 30th, 2025, DOE announced the termination of 24 awards issued by the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) totaling more than $3.7 billion. Several months after that, on October 1st, 2025, DOE announced the termination of 321 additional awards from across the Department totaling roughly $7.56 billion. In both instances, DOE claimed that the terminations resulted from a “thorough and individualized financial review of each award,” during which the Department had concluded that the awards “were not economically viable and would not generate a positive return on investment of taxpayer dollars.” After the October 2025 award terminations, DOE also asserted that the awards “did not adequately advance the nation’s energy needs.” Finally, in April 2026, you appeared before a House Appropriations Subcommittee and testified that the PRP was complete and that no additional award terminations would be forthcoming.
The repercussions of DOE’s award terminations were immense. Projects were thrown into chaos, companies were pushed to the brink of collapse, and jobs were lost. Taxpayer dollars were wasted. Major clean energy research, development, and demonstration projects – indeed, entire nascent clean energy sectors – were destabilized. Congressional energy priorities enshrined in law were thwarted. We continue to deal with the fallout of these award terminations to this day. From the beginning, as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (“the Committee”), I sought to conduct oversight of DOE’s actions in order to understand the processes and motivations that lay behind the Department’s attempt to wipe out over ten billion dollars in taxpayer-funded awards. On May 5th, 2025, I sent a letter to DOE along with a group of my Ranking Member colleagues in the House of Representatives and Senate that condemned the Department’s comprehensive freeze and review of Biden-era awards as “illegal and harmful to the public.” We asked how “DOE or any other part of the administration [is] assessing which DOE projects to cancel or continue, and under what criteria?” We did not receive a response from the Department before the PRP was announced on May 15th and $3.7 billion in awards was terminated on May 31st.
After DOE terminated the first round of awards on May 31st, Department officials provided a briefing for Committee Staff. Based upon the information disclosed in that briefing, I sent another letter to DOE on September 9th, 2025, along with two other Ranking Members, expressing “serious concerns” that the PRP was “haphazard, disorganized, and politically driven,” and calling upon DOE to “cease the cancellation process and restore respect for independent, merit-based reviews.” We also requested specific documents created during the Department’s review of OCED awards related to DOE’s evaluation of those awards and its assessment of whether the awards should be terminated, as well as a comprehensive list of DOE officials who had participated in the review process. DOE never provided those requested documents.
When DOE terminated more than $7.5 billion worth of awards on October 1st, 2025, the Department publicly claimed that the terminations were rooted in policy-based criteria such as economic viability, taxpayer return, and national energy priorities. You denied any political motivation behind the terminations in congressional testimony as recently as April and June 2026.3 But DOE’s cover story unraveled due to an unlikely source: its own concessions in court. Over the course of one lawsuit filed in November 2025, DOE formally stipulated that “a primary reason” for the October 2025 award terminations was “whether the grantee was located in a ‘Blue State’”; a judge ruled that DOE’s award terminations were unconstitutional and illegal in January 2026. Over the course of a second lawsuit related to the same terminations, DOE went even further and formally stipulated that the October 2025 award terminations were “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state,” and that they were not based upon “any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction, or performance-based factor.”
When you testified before the Science Committee on June 10th, 2026, Science Committee Democrats confronted you about the award terminations and reiterated the oversight requests that I had previously made to DOE. One of my colleagues, Energy Subcommittee Ranking Member Deborah Ross, demanded that DOE disclose the identities of the Department officials who participated in the PRP; once again, you refused to do so. Another one of my colleagues, Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo, pressed you to explain the contradiction between your denials of any political motivation in the award terminations and DOE’s formal concessions in the November 2025 lawsuit; once again, you denied that any of the October 2025 award termination decisions were made based on politics. It was July 2026, the very next month, when DOE’s formal concessions in the second lawsuit – even more sweeping – became public, even though you had surely known about them when you testified before the Science Committee. Your materially false statements to the Committee left me with no choice but to formally refer you to the Department of Justice, which I did along with Ranking Member Amo on August 4th, 2026.
For more than 15 months, my colleagues and I have attempted to conduct oversight of DOE’s award termination activities. We have asked questions, requested documents, and demanded answers directly from you during official testimony. But DOE has thwarted our oversight repeatedly by refusing to provide the requested information and documents. In doing so, DOE has hindered our ability to evaluate DOE’s actions and obstructed the Committee’s ability to fulfill its constitutional role. The following oversight requests from the 119th Congress remain outstanding, and DOE must comply with them. Please provide the requested information and documents no later than 5:00 PM on Wednesday, October 14th, 2026:
1. Please provide to the Committee a comprehensive list of DOE officials who participated in the “Portfolio Review Process” in 2025 and 2026.
2. Please provide to the Committee copies of the “one pagers” or “one-page summary memos” that were created for each award being reviewed as a part of the “Portfolio Review Process.”
3. Please provide to the Committee copies of the assessments that were completed for each award terminated in May 2025 and October 2025 for the purpose of evaluating whether those awards had sufficiently met the criteria utilized by DOE under the “Portfolio Review Process.”
Secretary Wright, these are straightforward requests for specific documents and information. I cannot help but believe that your ultimate goal in refusing to comply with them is to evade responsibility for your actions. Did you believe that you could arbitrarily terminate billions of dollars’ worth of awards, lie about the reasons why, and escape accountability? Now, as the political consequences of your actions mount, it appears you hope to quietly walk away from the entire issue, while Congress simply moves on without holding you accountable. That hope would be mistaken. Congressional oversight must be respected, and my oversight requests must be complied with. If DOE fails to do so, we will redouble our efforts using every available tool at our disposal. I urge DOE to comply now.
Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” The Committee possesses jurisdiction over “all energy research, development, and demonstration, and projects therefor, and all federally owned or operated nonmilitary energy laboratories, as well as the commercial application of energy technologies.”
