WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) and Congresswoman Ashely Hinson (IA-02) led a bipartisan congressional letter to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet C. Oz, MD and Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) Director Abe Sutton to address maternal health.

The representatives urged CMS to develop and test a demonstration model through CMMI that uses telehealth and remote monitoring technologies to improve maternal health outcomes. The letter calls for the CMS to leverage technology to make pregnancy and postpartum care safer, more accessible, and more effective, while generating evidence to support broader adoption of innovative maternal healthcare solutions.

Healthy Moms Healthy Babies America stands in support of Congresswoman Williams and Congresswoman Hinson’s bipartisan effort to improve maternal health outcomes.

The Members wrote:

“As sponsors of the Tech to Save Moms Act (H.R. 8317), we write to encourage the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), through the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Innovation (CMMI), to pursue a demonstration model that advances the goals outlined in our legislation and leverages technology to improve maternal health outcomes nationwide.”

“The United States continues to face an unacceptable maternal health crisis, with disproportionately poor outcomes in rural, underserved, and high-risk communities. As CMS has previously recognized, innovative telehealth payment and service delivery models for maternal health represent an important opportunity to improve access to high quality care, particularly for patients facing provider shortages, transportation barriers, and other challenges that impede access to maternity care.”

The Members requested that the CMII evaluate, develop and test a demonstration model that:

Expands access to maternal telehealth services and remote monitoring technologies for Medicaid beneficiaries during pregnancy and the postpartum period;

Supports the screening, monitoring, and management of common pregnancy-related and postpartum health complications;

Improves access to care in rural and urban underserved, low income, and high-risk communities;

Evaluates the impact of technology enabled interventions on clinical outcomes, patient engagement, and program costs with an eye toward closing health gaps socioeconomic, geographic, and racial and ethnic divides; and

Identifies best practices for broader adoption within Medicaid and other CMS programs.

The Members said:

“As we have stated publicly, innovative technology can play an important role in addressing our nation’s maternal health crisis, and we should be using every available tool to make pregnancy and postpartum care safer, more accessible, and more effective for families across the country. We appreciate CMS’s continued commitment to addressing the maternal health crisis and we look forward to working with you directly.”
title: Congresswomen Nikema Williams & Ashley Hinson Call for Technology Improvements to be Utilized to Advance Maternal Health

Ranking Member Raskin, Rep. Whitesides Demand Watchdog Probes into Taxpayer-Funded Trump Campaign Ads
Lawmakers Ask Federal Watchdogs to Investigate Administration Officials for Violating Federal Law by Using Public Funds for Propaganda Ads
Washington, D.C. (October 1, 2026)— Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. George Whitesides called on the Government Accountability Office (GAO) and the U.S. Office of Special Counsel (OSC) to formally investigate the Trump Administration’s use of taxpayer dollars to produce and air ads promoting President Trump in the weeks before the midterm elections. The lawmakers are seeking a full accounting of what the ads cost, who paid for them and whether officials broke federal law.
“The Trump Administration knows what they are doing is unlawful, as evidenced by their halfhearted attempts to defend their actions. An anonymous White House spokesperson called the ads ‘educational,’ and suggested that they are ‘clearly not political’ because the ‘president is not on the ballot.’ Yet just a few short weeks ago, at his poorly-rated Republican National Convention, President Trump pleaded for his rapidly dwindling ranks of supporters to vote, begging them to ‘pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot.’ The White House can’t have it both ways,” wrote the lawmakers.
On September 23, the White House began airing a 30-second ad labeled “Paid for by the U.S. Government.” Dozens of images of Trump flash across the screen while a singer implores viewers to “love me” and UFC President Dana White calls Trump the “toughest and most resilient person” he has ever met. Days later, the Administration aired another government-funded ad featuring Trump walking down a hallway as audio from a political rally attacks the “Deep State” and promises to “expel the warmongers” from government.
The White House has labeled the ads “public service announcements,” a patently false characterization of taxpayer-funded praise for the President. One credits Trump with reviving American manufacturing, even as the United States has lost tens of thousands of manufacturing jobs during his second term. Another boasts that he is defending law and order while federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since he returned to office. And Trump uses an ad paid for by the public to rail against “warmongers” while his war with Iran has taken the lives of 22 American servicemembers and cost more than $43 billion.
The lawmakers are asking federal watchdogs to investigate potential violations of multiple laws, including:
- Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026: Section 718 prohibits the use of appropriated funds for unauthorized domestic “publicity or propaganda.” GAO has explained that the prohibition reaches government self-promotion, including “self-aggrandizement” and “puffery.”
- Hatch Act of 1939: Federal employees may not use their official authority to interfere with an election. Although the President is exempt from the Hatch Act, Administration employees who helped create, approve or distribute the ads are not.
- Anti-Deficiency Act: Federal officials cannot authorize expenditures beyond what an appropriation permits. If Congress prohibited spending public money on propaganda, officials cannot lawfully charge taxpayers for these ads.
- Federal criminal statutes: Federal law prohibits the theft or knowing misuse of public money.
Ranking Member Raskin and Rep. Whitesides demanded that GAO identify the source, accounts and total amount of taxpayer funds used to produce and distribute the ads across major television markets and official White House social media channels. They also requested a legal determination on whether the ads violate federal law. The lawmakers asked OSC to investigate potential Hatch Act violations and determine who should be held accountable.
“President Trump is obviously desperate for the American people to ‘love’ him, a problem that goes beyond your jurisdiction. But stealing taxpayer dollars to pay for Mr. Trump’s narcissistic ego trips is plainly illegal. Your agencies have an important responsibility to hold accountable members of his Administration who violate the laws and policies under your purview,” concluded the lawmakers.
Click here to read the letter
title: Ranking Member Raskin, Rep. Whitesides Demand Watchdog Probes into Taxpayer-Funded Trump Campaign Ads

As Grocery Prices Skyrocket, Brown Sounds Alarm on New Trump SNAP Cut Taking Effect Today
As cuts kick in 5 million have already lost SNAP after Trump cuts
Washington, D.C. - Today, Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11), Vice Ranking Member on the House Agriculture Committee, warned that another SNAP cut from H.R. 1, the Republican Reconciliation Law, has gone into effect.
The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is federally funded and administered by states. H.R. 1 cut the federal share of funding for SNAP administrative costs in half, meaning that states are now required to cover 75% of SNAP administrative costs. Nationwide, this represents billions in reduced funding for SNAP.
In Ohio, this has meant a loss of an estimated $38 million in SNAP funding effective today, and potential annual cuts of $67 million. Earlier this year, the Republican-controlled Ohio legislature allocated only $12.5 million to cover this gap, leaving Ohio’s largest counties (which administer SNAP locally) with a substantial funding deficit. Cuyahoga County received the same administrative funding patch as Ohio’s smallest counties and now faces a funding gap of $7 million. For state-by-state estimates of SNAP funding cuts effective today, click here.
The reduction of administrative funding leaves states and counties with fewer resources to process applications, determine eligibility, and ensure families receive the benefits they are eligible for. This massive funding cut also jeopardizes other state and local services as states struggle to replace this lost funding. A similar cost shift, cutting federal payments to states for SNAP benefits, will go into effect October 1, 2027.
“Trump and Republicans in Congress passed tax breaks for millionaires and billionaires on the backs of families who are already struggling to afford sky-high grocery costs. Over 5 million Americans have already lost SNAP food assistance because of Trump’s cuts, and today, another SNAP cut from the Big, Ugly Law kicks in. Trump and Republicans have handed states huge SNAP funding cuts, with more cuts coming next year. Worse still, these administrative cuts are coming as Republicans have also made SNAP more difficult to access. They’ve created new paperwork and new requirements, then cut the funding used to enroll people. It’s a devastating gut punch and it’s intentional: this is a plan to wreck state SNAP programs and push millions off of SNAP and into hunger. Congress must fix these cuts through the Farm Bill and protect families who rely on SNAP to keep food on the table,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown.
According to USDA data, more than 5 million Americans, including about 2 million children, have already lost SNAP since H.R. 1 was enacted in July 2025. In Ohio, over 120,000 people have already lost SNAP.
H.R.1’s SNAP cuts were enacted alongside cuts to Medicaid and other programs to pay for tax cuts that overwhelmingly benefited large corporations and the wealthiest Americans. The Republican Farm Bill which passed the House and is currently under consideration in the Senate, locks in $187 billion in SNAP cuts. Republicans rejected all Democratic attempts to roll back SNAP cuts in the House Farm Bill.
Separately, a SNAP cost-of-living-adjustment, or COLA, took effect today. The COLA was authorized through the 2008 Farm Bill, and Republicans have repeatedly attempted to kill and weaken SNAP benefit increases. Last year, Brown introduced The Hunger Free Future Act, new legislation to block any changes to the Thrifty Food Plan, which uses economic data to determine benefit size, which would result in benefit cuts.
###
title: As Grocery Prices Skyrocket, Brown Sounds Alarm on New Trump SNAP Cut Taking Effect Today

WASHINGTON — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund Reauthorization Act, which would remove the funding cap for the ongoing groundwater treatment by the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority, reauthorize funding at $250 million, and support the completion of the ongoing water restoration project. The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water for over 1.5 million residents in the San Gabriel Valley and Los Angeles County, including the cities of Azusa, Baldwin Park, City of Industry, El Monte, Irwindale, La Puente, South El Monte, and West Covina. The San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority signed on as a supporting organization.

“The San Gabriel Valley relies on the clean drinking water provided by the San Gabriel Basin,” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “Since 2000, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has supported the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean and restore contaminated groundwater in our region. This legislation would remove funding hurdles and provide the support needed to bring this decades-long project across the finish line. Earlier this year, I worked with Congresswoman Chu to secure critical federal Community Project Funding for the restoration fund, and we’re committed to passing this legislation to further accelerate groundwater cleanup. Clean drinking water is a fundamental human right, and every family in the San Gabriel Valley deserves direct, affordable, protected access to it.”

“The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water to more than 1.5 million people across our region, but it still carries contamination left behind by industries of the past,” said Rep. Judy Chu. “For decades, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has powered the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean up our groundwater, and this bill would provide the long-term federal support needed to finish the job. I’m proud to join Congressmember Cisneros in leading this effort, building on our work securing federal Community Project Funding for this project. Families across the San Gabriel Valley deserve a safe, reliable, and sustainable source of drinking water for generations to come.”

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

###
title: Reps. Cisneros, Chu Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water

Krishnamoorthi Hails Restoration of 988 LGBTQ+ Crisis Line Following His Efforts
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), author of the bipartisan 988 LGBTQ+ Youth Access Act and a Vice Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus, hailed the restoration of specialized LGBTQ+ crisis line services through the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline after the Trump Administration shut them down in July 2025. After Congressman Krishnamoorthi helped secure $33.1 million in federal funding earlier this year to restore the program, he partnered with allies in Congress and LGBTQ+ and mental health advocates to pressure the Trump Administration to use that funding and bring the “Press 3” option back online.
“I’m proud that we secured the funding to restore this lifesaving LGBTQ+ crisis line and successfully pressured the Trump Administration to bring the program back,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “When an LGBTQ+ young person reaches out for help in a moment of crisis, they deserve to reach a counselor trained to understand and support them. This program should never have been taken away, and now we need to make sure it stays available for every young person who needs it. I’m grateful to The Trevor Project, NAMI Chicago, Equality Illinois, the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, and all the advocates and young people who worked alongside us to bring these services back.”
Congressman Krishnamoorthi introduced the bipartisan 988 LGBTQ+ Youth Access Act in September 2025 after the Trump Administration shut down the specialized services. The legislation would require HHS to maintain dedicated crisis support for LGBTQ+ youth and reserve at least 9 percent of annual 988 funding for those services.
After Congress provided funding to restore the crisis line, Congressman Krishnamoorthi repeatedly pressed the Department of Health and Human Services to follow through. In May, he joined Representatives Sharice Davids and Seth Moulton in a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. demanding a timeline for restoration and answers on the Administration’s implementation of Congress’s funding. He also helped lead four public events in Chicago and Washington calling for the crisis line’s return, including a May press conference at NAMI Chicago, a June roundtable with LGBTQ+ young people and advocates, a July press conference in Washington, and a September roundtable and press conference with Illinois mental health and LGBTQ+ leaders.
title: Krishnamoorthi Hails Restoration of 988 LGBTQ+ Crisis Line Following His Efforts

AKRON, OH – U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) recognizes October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month and is reintroducing the Skills Against Violence Act. This bill would establish a new Gender-Based Violence Survivor Workforce Program at the Department of Justice's Office on Violence Against Women. The office would award grants to domestic violence and sexual assault service providers and coalitions with a documented history of effective work in this field. The bill authorizes $40 million per year for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

Grants could fund employment counseling, occupational training, job retention counseling, and counseling on re-entering the workforce. They could also fund outreach to survivors and to employers that support a safe workspace, along with support services such as child care, disability and elder care, transportation, professional clothing and equipment, legal services, and gender-based violence and mental health counseling. Grantees would report annually on how many survivors received workforce development, occupational training, and support services, how many entered employment, and how satisfied survivors were with the services. The Director would then report to Congress every two years, beginning two years after enactment.

Rep. Sykes previously introduced the Safer Homes and Families Package, a comprehensive legislative slate consisting of four bills to protect survivors and strengthen support systems nationwide: the Fair Social Security for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, the Better Care for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, the Break Free from Domestic Violence Act, and the Electronic Stalking Act.

“Every person deserves to live free from fear and violence,” said Rep. Sykes. “I’m committed to standing with survivors and delivering real solutions that help them rebuild their lives. During Domestic Violence Awareness Month, we honor the courage of survivors and highlight the urgent need for stronger protections. The bills I’ve led reflect our promise to create safer communities where every person can heal, thrive, and live with dignity."

"A paycheck can be the difference between staying and leaving. Economic abuse occurs in 99% of domestic violence cases and is one of the most powerful ways abusers keep survivors trapped,” said Maria York, Director of Policy and Communication, Ohio Domestic Violence Network. “Here in Ohio, intimate partner violence costs our state nearly $1.2 billion every year, including $227.7 million in lost work productivity. ODVN applauds the Skills Against Violence Act for investing in job training, career support, and wraparound services like childcare and transportation that survivors need to build lasting financial independence. We're grateful to Rep. Sykes for being a continuous champion for survivors, this Domestic Violence Awareness Month and every month."

“Each of these bills represents a critical step toward removing the barriers that keep survivors trapped in unsafe situations,” said Teresa Stafford Wright, CEO of Hope & Healing Survivor Resource Center. “The Fair Social Security for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, the Better Care for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, and the Break Free From Domestic Violence Act all recognize that safety, health, and financial stability are deeply interconnected. By expanding access to financial resources, trauma-informed care, and safe housing options, this legislation affirms that survivors deserve not only protection from violence but the opportunity to rebuild their lives with dignity and independence.”

“Survivors should not have to choose between healing and thriving, nor should they have to finish healing before they are given opportunities to thrive. When survivors have access to skills training, safe working spaces, and opportunities to build sustainable careers, healing and economic independence can happen alongside each other. That is what creates pathways toward long term self sufficiency,” said Dr. Antoria Gillon, Founder and CEO of From Ordinary to Extraordinary.

“The National Network to End Domestic Violence (NNEDV) is proud to support the Skills Against Violence Act. Economic security is a critical part of safety for survivors of domestic violence. Financial abuse, disrupted employment, damaged credit, and other economic barriers can make it harder for survivors to leave an abusive relationship and build a safe, stable future for themselves and their families,” said Tonia Moultry-Pace, NNEDV Interim President & CEO. “We are grateful to Congresswoman Sykes for introducing the Skills Against Violence Act, which will create meaningful workforce development opportunities for survivors and help them build the skills and economic stability needed to rebuild.”

The Fair Social Security for Domestic Violence Survivors Act would lower the current 10-year marriage requirement for spousal Social Security benefits to five years for individuals who divorce due to domestic abuse. This change would prevent survivors from being financially penalized for leaving unsafe relationships and help them achieve economic independence.

The Better Care for Domestic Violence Survivors Act invests $50 million over five years in a pilot program to train healthcare providers in evidence-based, trauma-informed care. Because survivors often seek medical attention during or after abuse, this initiative would help healthcare professionals identify and support victims more effectively, potentially saving lives through earlier intervention.

The Break Free From Domestic Violence Act ensures survivors of domestic violence, stalking or sexual assault can break a lease without penalty, giving them the freedom to leave dangerous living situations without facing financial or legal consequences.

The Stop Electronic Stalking Act would prohibit the use of personal tracking devices to track people without their consent. Rep. Sykes introduced similar legislation in the Ohio legislature which was later signed into law by Governor DeWine.

In Ohio, there were 157 domestic violence fatalities from July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025, including 11 children. This marks a ten year high in fatalities due to domestic violence in Ohio. In 2025, 3,703 incidents of domestic violence were reported in Summit County, and 2,215 incidents in Stark County.

Rep. Sykes has long been a champion for survivors, earning bipartisan support and delivering tangible results. Last year, Rep. Sykes secured a $500,000 Transitional Housing Assistance grant for Domestic Violence Project Inc., providing critical resources to help survivors rebuild their lives. She has also co-sponsored the Healing Partnerships for Survivors Act, Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act, Crime Victims Fund Stabilization Act of 2025, Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act, the National Domestic Violence Awareness Month Resolution, & the Trafficking Survivors Relief Act of 2025. Throughout the appropriations process, she has been a strong advocate for funding for domestic violence and family violence programs, signing onto bipartisan requests for robust funding in FY27.

As a member of the Ohio House of Representatives prior to her time in Congress, Rep. Sykes authored Ohio H.B. 1, which became law and extended protective orders to victims of dating violence for the first time in the state’s history.
title: Rep. Sykes Recognizes October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month, Leads Legislation to Protect Survivors of Domestic Violence

Washington, DC – The U.S. Senate passed Congresswoman Dina Titus (NV-01)’s End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act. This legislation would prevent U.S. citizens who have been taken hostage or wrongfully detained abroad from incurring penalties for late tax payments while they were held. Representative Claudia Tenney (R-NY) joined Rep. Titus as cosponsor of the legislation which is now on its way to the President's desk.

“I am pleased to report that my End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act passed the Senate and is on its way to the President's desk,” said Rep. Titus. “It goes without saying that no one who has endured wrongful detention or been taken hostage abroad should face the additional burden of onerous tax penalties incurred through no fault of their own. This bill would eliminate that unthinkable possibility by cutting red tape in our tax code and codifying a critical support mechanism for wrongful detainees, hostages, and their families here in the United States.”

This bill extends certain federal tax deadlines for U.S. nationals who are unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or held hostage abroad and their spouses. The bill also allows for an abatement and refund of additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed to such individuals for failing to meet a federal tax deadline during a period of detention.

Specifically, under the bill, the period during which a U.S. national is unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or held hostage abroad is disregarded in determining certain federal tax deadlines, including deadlines for

filing a return for and paying federal income, estate, gift, employment, or excise taxes;

a tax credit or refund claim; and

the determination, assessment, and collection of additional taxes, interest, or penalties.

The bill requires the Department of State and the Department of Justice to annually provide the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) with lists to identify U.S. nationals who qualify for an extension.

The bill also requires the IRS to (1) abate and refund additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed for any tax year ending during a period of detention for which an extension of a federal tax deadline is permitted; and (2) establish a program allowing U.S. nationals unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or taken hostage abroad (or their spouse or dependent) to claim a refund of additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed for any tax year ending during a period of detention from 2021 to the bill’s enactment date.

The legislation’s full text can be found here.

title: Senate Passes Titus Legislation to Protect Hostages and Wrongful Detainees from Tax Penalties

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Thursday, October 1, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, returned from a bipartisan congressional delegation to Lebanon that he led with U.S. Congressman Darin LaHood (IL-16). This trip comes at a moment of rare opportunity, with a new technocratic Lebanese government in place and Hezbollah’s influence significantly weakened.

Gottheimer pressed Lebanese leaders to fully disarm and defund Hezbollah and meet the obligations Beirut accepted when it signed the June 2026 Trilateral Framework with the United States and Israel. The delegation met with Lebanese government officials — including President Joseph Aoun, Speaker Nabih Berri, Lebanese Forces Party leader Samir Farid Geagea, and dozens of Members of Parliament including Michel Moawad — to discuss removing Iranian influence from Lebanon and the full and verifiable disarmament of Hezbollah.

In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a U.S.-brokered framework under which Lebanon would disarm Hezbollah and Israeli forces would withdraw in phases as that disarmament is verified. This marks the first Lebanese government to negotiate directly with Israel, and that momentum must continue to ensure the success of the deal. Implementation is still in its early stages. So far, the Lebanese Armed Forces have deployed to an initial set of villages, but no timetable or way to verify Hezbollah’s weapons and infrastructure are gone has been agreed, and Hezbollah continues to reject disarmament. Completing the framework is critical to returning all of Lebanon’s territory to the control of the Lebanese people, out of the grip of Hezbollah and its Iranian handlers.

“Lebanon is at a turning point. For far too long, Iran has used Hezbollah, its terror proxy, to hold the Lebanese people hostage. It has drained the country’s economy, weakened its institutions, and pulled it into wars the Lebanese people never chose,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “It’s time to return Lebanon to the Lebanese people. That means removing Iran’s influence and fully disarming and defunding Hezbollah. Lebanon made that commitment in June, and now it has to follow through fully, verifiably, and across the entire country. A Lebanon without Hezbollah is better for the Lebanese people, for the Middle East, and for America.”

On the trip, Gottheimer and the delegation focused on:

Enforcing the Trilateral Framework: Backing a time-bound, Cabinet-approved plan to disarm Hezbollah with real third-party verification, so that Hezbollah’s weapons, tunnels, and command structure are removed.

Removing Iranian influence: Stopping Iran from spreading its money, weapons, and influence through Lebanon. That means cutting Hezbollah’s smuggling routes and cash couriers, enforcing sanctions on the banks and businesses that rearm and refinance it, and rejecting any Iranian role in deciding Lebanon’s future.

Disarming Hezbollah: Holding Lebanon to the commitment it made when it signed the Trilateral Framework for the full, verified disarmament and dismantlement of Hezbollah nationwide, including the seizure or destruction of its weapons and tunnels, the closure of its smuggling routes, and the demobilization of its fighters.

Returning Lebanon to the Lebanese people: Backing Lebanese leaders and institutions working to rebuild a sovereign, free, and prosperous country.

Combating terror in the region: Working with partners to cut off terror financing, stop weapons smuggling, and protect U.S. troops, Israel, and our allies.

“Lebanon made a commitment in June, and what comes next is critical to the future of the country,” Gottheimer continued. “Every day Hezbollah keeps its weapons is another day Iran gets a vote in the future of Lebanon. A stable, sovereign Lebanon, free from Iran’s terror proxies, is good for the Lebanese people and vital to America’s national security. I’ll keep working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support that outcome.”

While in Lebanon, Gottheimer also visited Maghen Abraham Synagogue and the Shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon.

Gottheimer has repeatedly pressed for Hezbollah’s disarmament. In June 2026, he and U.S. Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) introduced a bipartisan resolution condemning Hezbollah’s repeated ceasefire violations and calling on the Lebanese government and the Lebanese Armed Forces to ensure Hezbollah ceases all attacks and disarms. In December 2025, he and U.S. Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-6) led a bipartisan letter to the Lebanese President and Prime Minister urging them to disarm Hezbollah immediately, including by force if necessary.

Below: Gottheimer and LaHood in Lebanon.
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Co-Leads Bipartisan House Intelligence Committee Trip to Lebanon

Andrea Salinas Celebrates Restoration of Specialized 988 Crisis Services for LGBTQI+ Young People
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Vice-Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus and Co-Chair of the Congressional Mental Health Caucus, celebrated the restoration of specialized crisis services for LGBTQI+ young people through the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. The LGBTQI+ lifeline resumed on September 30, 2026, more than a year after the Trump Administration ended it in July 2025. Through the restored service, LGBTQI+ young people in crisis can once again connect with counselors specially trained to understand and respond to their unique needs.
“When a young person reaches out for help in a moment of crisis, they deserve someone on the other end of the line who understands what they are going through and knows how to help,” said Rep. Salinas. “That is why I fought to protect this lifesaving service, and I am incredibly pleased to see it restored. For me, this is personal. I am the mother of a queer daughter, and I know firsthand how deeply a mental health crisis can affect a family. Every young person deserves to know that when they are struggling, they have somewhere to turn and someone ready to listen.”
In July 2025, Rep. Salinas led nearly 100 Members of Congress in urging House appropriators to maintain funding for specialized 988 services for LGBTQI+ youth. Congress later approved funding requiring the Department of Health and Human Services and the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration to restore the program.
The specialized “Press 3” option was first established as a pilot in 2022 to connect LGBTQI+ youth and young adults with specialized crisis care. Since its founding, the lifeline has handled nearly 1.5 million calls, texts, and chats from LGBTQI+ young people.
Anyone experiencing a mental health, suicide, or substance use crisis can call, text, or chat 988 to connect with crisis support.
###
title: Andrea Salinas Celebrates Restoration of Specialized 988 Crisis Services for LGBTQI+ Young People

Mrvan Announces Department of Education Grant for CCSJ
Washington, DC – Today, Rep. Frank J. Mrvan announced a federal grant award for Calumet College of St. Joseph (CCSJ) through the U.S. Department of Education’s Strengthening Institutions Program.
Specifically, CCSJ will receive $1,443,864 to improve and strengthen the institution's academic quality, institutional management, and fiscal stability. In general, the Strengthening Institutions Program aims to help institutions of higher education become self-sufficient and expand their capacity to serve low-income students.
According to the CCSJ, approximately half of the grant funding will be designated to complete a kitchen and kinesiology space, which will provide more robust food service for students while also creating a more functional catering kitchen to support events. The grant will also support several areas that directly contribute to student success and well-being, including tutoring, supplemental instruction, technology upgrades, and mental health activities.
Congressman Mrvan stated, “Thank you to President Tulley and all of the leaders at the Calumet College of St. Joseph on successfully securing this vital funding to further support students during their academic journey. I am grateful for your consistent and thoughtful efforts to dedicate resources that promote the well-being and academic success of all of your students.”
“We appreciate the Congressman’s efforts to expand access to higher education in Northwest Indiana,” said Dr. Ron Tulley, President of Calumet College of St. Joseph. “This grant will provide for a more robust health and wellness center at the College. We will develop infrastructure and grow our endowment. This award will allow us to live out our mission in a more impactful way.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM-03), Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Representative Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), Madeleine Dean (D-PA-04), and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) introduced the America’s College Promise Act of 2026. The bill would make community college and two-year Tribal Colleges and Universities more accessible by waiving tuition fees for eligible students.

“In New Mexico, we know free community college can unlock the doors to a brighter future. The America’s College Promise Act builds on New Mexico’s example by making sure students across the country can attend community college without the burden of tuition and fees,” said Representative Leger Fernández. “Our bill will provide funds for services students need to earn their degrees and reduce the financial burden for low-income students to attend TCUs, HBCUs, and MSIs. From recent high school graduates to experienced workers who want to go back to school — every student deserves the opportunity to keep learning without the fear of drowning in debt.”

“Community colleges play a unique and vital role in providing students access to a quality postsecondary degree. Regrettably, the chronic underfunding of community colleges is jeopardizing their ability to support their students and communities,” said House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Scott (D-VA-03). “The America’s College Promise Act is a major investment in expanding opportunities for students and rebuilding a stronger economy.”

“Students in Southern Arizona and throughout the country should not have to take on tens of thousands of dollars of debt to get a college education,” said Representative Grijalva. “The America’s College Promise Act will provide two years of free in-state tuition and fees for students enrolled in community and technical college programs. Whether they’re just starting out or returning to the classroom later in life, every student deserves the opportunity to learn new skills and pursue higher education. By expanding access to education and workforce training, we’re strengthening the workforce that businesses and local economies depend on.”

“As a professor, it was a privilege to witness students claim their education and seize their futures — yet the real fear and burden of immense student loan debt often deters young adults and returning students from expanding their learning,” said Representative Dean. “The America’s College Promise Act provides tuition-free community college courses and expands funding for HBCUs and trade schools, making the path to higher education and career readiness available to more Americans and future generations.”

“Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to get the education and skills they need to land a good-paying job and build a better life, no matter where they come from or how much money their family makes,” said Senator Baldwin. “But for too many working families, the rising cost of higher education leaves students saddled with debt for years to come, or it is simply out of reach. That’s why I am proud to work with my colleagues to remove barriers and lower the cost of community college, so more Wisconsinites have the opportunity to compete, succeed, and live a good middle-class life.”

The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 will make the skills and credentials necessary to succeed in the workforce more accessible to all students by creating a new federal-state partnership to provide two years of tuition-free community college.

Specifically, the America’s College Promise Act of 2026:

Creates a partnership between the federal government and states to waive tuition and fees for two years of community and technical college programs for eligible students, while promoting key reforms to accelerate student success;

Creates a sliding scale for federal share beginning at 100 percent for the first year and ending at 80 percent for the fifth and subsequent years;

Ensures that programs offer academic credits that are transferable to four-year institutions in their state, or occupational training that leads to recognized credentials;

Maintains and encourages state funding for higher education;

Establishes a student success fund to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, or completion rates and labor market outcomes for underserved student populations, including students of color and low-income and first-generation college students, who attend community and technical colleges at disproportionate rates;

Waives two years of tuition and fees for eligible students at tribal colleges and universities; and

Establishes a new grant program to provide pathways to success at historically black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions by covering a significant portion of tuition and fees for the first two years of attendance for low-income students.

To read the bill text for the America’s College Promise Act of 2026, click here.

To read the fact sheet for America’s College Promise Act of 2026, click here.
title: Leger Fernández, Scott, Grijalva, Dean Introduce Bill to Lower Cost of Community College

WASHINGTON – As new technologies, business practices, and online marketplaces create new ways for companies to take advantage of consumers, U.S. Representatives Kathy Castor (FL-14) and Jan Schakowsky (IL-09) are introducing legislation to ensure the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has the tools and independence it needs to protect consumers in the modern economy.

The 21st Century FTC Act, introduced by Rep. Castor, and the FTC Autonomy Act, introduced by Rep. Schakowsky, would strengthen the FTC’s ability to respond to unfair and deceptive practices and hold companies accountable when they harm consumers.

“The current economic pain being inflicted on hardworking Americans shouldn’t be exacerbated by fraudsters and corporate wrongdoers. It’s imperative that corporations be held accountable when they take advantage of consumers,” said Rep. Castor. “The FTC is key to accountability, and the 21st Century FTC and FTC Autonomy Acts will strengthen the ability to act and restore civil penalties for first time offenses. I’m committed to restoring the FTC’s autonomy and authority, and I urge Congress to pass this important legislation.”

“Companies are constantly finding new ways to take advantage of consumers, and the FTC needs the tools to keep up,” said Rep. Schakowsky. “I’m glad to be in this fight with Congresswoman Castor to make sure the FTC has the authority and independence it needs to protect consumers. We need an FTC that can keep pace with the modern economy, not one held back by outdated rules and unnecessary barriers.”

The FTC is the federal government’s primary consumer protection agency, but outdated procedures and restrictions on its enforcement authority can make it harder for the agency to respond to emerging threats.

The 21st Century FTC Act would give the FTC streamlined rulemaking authority under the Administrative Procedure Act and allow the agency to seek civil penalties for first-time violations of the FTC Act. These changes would help the FTC respond more effectively to emerging consumer harms and deter companies from engaging in unfair or deceptive practices.

The FTC Autonomy Act would allow the FTC’s own attorneys to bring cases seeking civil penalties without first having to enlist the assistance of the Department of Justice. Removing this procedural barrier would allow the agency to pursue enforcement actions more efficiently and hold companies accountable.

Together, these bills would give the FTC the modern tools it needs to protect consumers in a rapidly changing economy. As technology and business practices evolve, consumers should not be left vulnerable because federal consumer protection laws have failed to keep pace. The 21st Century FTC Act and FTC Autonomy Act would strengthen the FTC’s ability to set clear rules, respond to new consumer threats, and hold companies accountable when they cross the line.

Full text of the 21st Century FTC Act is available HERE. Full text of the FTC Autonomy Act is available HERE.

###
title: Castor, Schakowsky Introduce Legislation to Modernize FTC and Strengthen Consumer Protections

Washington, DC. — Today, Rep. Dave Min (CA-47), and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02), Co-Chairs of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) Building Resilient Housing Task Force, introduced the Community Disaster Protection Act, which would foster and incentivize the development of new disaster insurance products to help high-risk communities secure affordable coverage and promote effective disaster prevention.

“Families across the country are watching their insurance premiums skyrocket—or losing coverage altogether—because their communities are increasingly exposed to wildfires, floods, hurricanes, and other disasters,” said Rep. Min. “We cannot wait until after disaster strikes to figure out how families and communities are going to recover. The Community Disaster Protection Act gives local communities new tools to close dangerous insurance gaps, invest in resilience, and develop coverage that actually reflects the risks they face. As these disasters become more costly, Congress has a responsibility to help ensure Americans are not left financially devastated simply because of where they live.”

“As extreme weather becomes more frequent and severe, too many Americans are unable to obtain the insurance coverage they need to recover from a disaster,” said Rep. Olszewski. “The Community Disaster Protection Act takes a commonsense approach by helping high-risk communities close coverage gaps and make disaster protection more affordable. I’m proud to work with the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) and Congressman Min to help communities prepare for the challenges ahead, protect families from devastating financial losses, and build a more resilient future.”

“The Community Disaster Protection Act is a great first step to address the rising costs and unmet needs facing Americans, and EDF research makes clear that new and innovative solutions will be critical as climate change increases disaster risk,” said Joanna Slaney, Vice President for Political and Government Affairs, Environmental Defense Fund (EDF). “This bill will be essential to help more communities identify the solutions that meet their needs. By supporting locally designed pilots that pair insurance coverage with investments in risk reduction, The CDPA would support the development of insurance products that help high-risk communities secure affordable insurance coverage, incentivize effective disaster prevention, and provide greater stability to property insurance markets. We thank Representatives Min and Olszewski for their leadership and urge Congress to move this bill forward.”

“APCIA applauds Congressman Min and Congressman Olszewski for introducing the Community Disaster Protection Act, which would support community-based catastrophe insurance solutions, including parametric and other innovative risk-transfer models, to help close protection gaps and expand options for communities facing natural disasters,” said Sam Whitfield, Senior Vice President of Federal Government Relations and Political Engagement at the American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA). “Importantly, the bill recognizes that these approaches are intended to complement, not replace, the traditional, private property casualty insurance market. By encouraging risk mitigation, promoting community resilience, expanding access to financial protection, and testing new risk-transfer models, this pilot program can help communities prepare for disasters and speed recovery when disasters strike.”

“Architects are an essential part of the solution to helping communities prepare for growing disaster risks. The Community Disaster Protection Act will give communities new tools to better understand, manage, and insure against those risks—helping create the conditions for property owners and local governments to invest in the resilient buildings and infrastructure architects are uniquely equipped to design,” said Illya Azaroff, FAIA, 2026 National President, American Institute of Architects (AIA). “AIA is proud to support this legislation and looks forward to continuing our work with Representative Dave Min, Johnny Olszewski, and the SEEC Building Resilient Housing Task Force to advance practical solutions that strengthen communities before disasters strike.”

“As natural disasters continue to worsen in both intensity and impact across the country, we need innovative solutions to help communities and economies recover from devastation,” said Jessie Ritter, Associate Vice President for Water and Coasts at the National Wildlife Federation. “The Community Disaster Protection Act encourages proactive risk mitigation, while also giving communities a flexible solution to support recovery after disasters, particularly in areas that are the most vulnerable to extreme weather. We look forward to working with Representatives Min and Olszewski on this legislation.”

“CSAC looks forward to working with Congressmember Min on the Community Disaster Protection Act to advance practical, workable solutions for California communities. Local governments need more tools and flexibility to help protect families and residents facing growing disaster risks and insurance challenges,” said California State Association of Counties (CSAC) President and Santa Clara County Supervisor Susan Ellenberg.

Background on the Community Disaster Protection Act:

As climate change drives more frequent and severe extreme weather events, communities face widening disaster coverage gaps, making it harder and more expensive for them to rebuild. In 2024, economic losses from natural disasters in the U.S. reached $217.8 billion, approximately $105 billion of which was left uninsured. Rising climate-related damage has increased insurer payouts, driven up premiums, and prompted insurance carriers to withdraw from high-risk markets. Addressing this coverage crisis requires innovative approaches that expand insurance access, promote effective resilience, and strengthen the stability of insurance markets nationwide.

Communities are exploring ways to secure or facilitate insurance for a group of properties, leveraging their local knowledge and purchasing power to improve affordability, streamline enrollment, and incentivize risk mitigation tailored to local needs. These arrangements, known as community-based catastrophe insurance (CBCI), offer significant potential to close disaster coverage gaps but are only now beginning to be explored, with just a handful of U.S. jurisdictions currently piloting or implementing CBCI programs. For example, CBCI can be developed to act as a supplement to the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), such as a parametric flood insurance program, or to cover wildfire risk in communities where insurers are withdrawing coverage or declining to write new policies."

The Community Disaster Protection Act would direct the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to establish a 5-year pilot program to award competitive grants to local governments, quasi-government bodies, and community-based organizations to design, develop, implement, or facilitate CBCI.

Specifically, this legislation would:

Close disaster coverage gaps by authorizing grants to develop or facilitate CBCI products that cover disaster risks uninsured or underserved by traditional insurance; setting actuarially justified premiums that enable broad participation; and prioritizing applicants facing the greatest coverage gaps or disaster risks.

Preserve local flexibility by allowing funds to support a range of CBCI frameworks, without restricting the disaster risks or properties covered. Eligible uses of funds could include consumer outreach and education, catastrophe-risk modeling or research into disaster risks, and leveraging non-federal funds to support long-term program sustainability.

Promote resiliency investments by requiring CBCI programs to promote specific individual or community-wide investments to mitigate disaster risks, reduce potential losses, and secure lower premiums.

Address regulatory ambiguity by directing the U.S. Government Accountability Office to conduct periodic evaluations of program performance to determine the regulatory treatment of CBCI and other alternative insurance products with respect to federal disaster aid eligibility.

Preserve state insurance authority by explicitly preserving States’ authority to regulate insurance markets and require all grant recipients to comply with applicable State insurance laws and regulations. Grants would only be a catalyst for CBCI arrangements operating within State regulatory frameworks.

This bill is endorsed by the American Property Casualty Insurance Association, American Institute of Architects, California State Association of Counties, Environmental Defense Fund, Evergreen Action, League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, and Natural Resources Defense Council.

In addition, Reps. Ami Bera (CA-06), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Ed Case (HI-01), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Mike Levin (CA-49), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), and Shri Thanedar (MI-13) have joined as original cosponsors.

The full text of the legislation can be found here and a summary of the legislation can be found here.

###
title: Representatives Min and Olszewski Introduce the Community Disaster Protection Act to Expand Insurance Access in High-Risk Communities

WASHINGTON, D.C. -- On September 28, Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25), joined by Congresswoman María Elvira Salazar (FL-27), introduced a bipartisan resolution designating October 1st as National Latino and Latina Physician Day.

Latinos make up nearly one in five Americans, yet only 6.7 percent of U.S. physicians are Latino or Latina, and just 2.8 percent are Latina. By 2050, Latinos are projected to represent more than one in four people in the United States and one in three children. At the same time, the nation faces a shortage of up to 86,000 physicians by 2036.

Research shows that when patients share the language and culture of their doctors, care and outcomes improve. Growing the Latino and Latina physician workforce means better health for our communities and for the nation.

"Growing up in a farmworker family taught me what it means to go without care, so I became an Emergency Physician to serve under resourced communities," said Congressman Dr. Raul Ruiz. "Today, too many Latino families still can't find a doctor who speaks their language or understands their cultures. This resolution recognizes the Latino and Latina physicians working to close that gap, and it challenges us to open more doors for the next generation."

"Trust in medical care is essential. Physicians that understand their community and are a reflection of it are critical when building and establishing that trust," said Rep. Salazar. "As our nation faces a healthcare workforce shortage, I am proud to co-lead this resolution that supports Latino and Latina physicians, who are helping to close gaps in care and serve as a trustworthy pillar of their community."

The resolution supports increasing the number of Latino and Latina physicians and expanding diversity in the medical field. It has earned the support of leading national medical organizations.

"The AAMC (Association of American Medical Colleges) is proud support National Latino and Latina Physicians Day and thank Rep. Ruiz and Rep. Salazar for their bipartisan work in highlighting the work of physicians critical to improving the health of patients and communities nationwide. As the nation faces a persistent physician shortage, we must support policies that increase to access to careers in medicine for future Latino and Latina physicians, and everyone in the next generation of doctors," said Danielle Turnipseed, JD, MHSA, MPP, chief public policy officer, AAMC (Association of American Medical Colleges)

"The National Hispanic Medical Association supports H.Res. 1589, introduced by Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D., recognizing October 1 as National Latino and Latina Physician Day. We need more Latino physicians serving our communities. This day not only highlights the significant underrepresentation of Latinos in the physician workforce but also recognizes the tremendous work Latino physicians do every day to care for patients and communities across our nation. We are proud to support this resolution and its recognition of the Latino physicians who serve our country," said Gilbert Burgos, M.D., MPH, President of the National Hispanic Medical Association.

Ranking Members Meeks, Garcia, Huffman, Pallone and Castro Demand Transparency on Trump Administration’s Venezuela Oil Deal
Washington, DC -- Representatives Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the Committee on Foreign Affairs; Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform; Jared Huffman, Ranking Member of the Committee on Natural Resources; Frank Pallone, Jr., Ranking Member of the Committee on Energy and Commerce; and Joaquin Castro, Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Western Hemisphere, demanded answers from Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on the details of the Trump administration’s agreement to procure a stake in the Barbados-based company North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to exploit Venezuela’s oil reserves, including the text of the agreement, concessions made by the United States to secure the agreement, and answers on how the Trump administration will ensure that revenues generated from Venezuela’s oil resources benefit the Venezuelan people.
A PDF copy of the letter is available here. An excerpt is below.
“In a remarkable imitation of the Maduro regime’s economic playbook, the White House announced on August 31st that the U.S. government would acquire a significant stake in the Barbados-based company [North American Blue Energy Partners].
“Subsequent press reporting indicates that NABEP is owned by Alejandro Betancourt, an individual facing money-laundering and corruption investigations in the United States, Spain, and Switzerland. Senior U.S. officials reportedly intervened in the Swiss criminal investigation into Mr. Betancourt on his behalf even as the Administration was finalizing this partnership with him.
“Senior U.S. officials failed to address bipartisan concerns about its recent actions with respect to Venezuelan energy deals in a closed briefing on September 14, 2026, to members of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. Troublingly, these officials did not provide or commit to providing the text of the relevant agreements for congressional review. Further Member questions also went unanswered, including what the United States has provided to NABEP in exchange for an equity stake potentially worth billions; how the United States will ensure revenue from this oil production will not be misappropriated by either Mr. Betancourt or corrupt Venezuelan officials; and how this oil will meaningfully address the high price of gas U.S. consumers are facing given the challenges inherent in refining Venezuela’s heavy crude oil.”
Additional background: On February 12, 2026, Ranking Member Meeks initiated an inquiry into the Trump administration’s decision to route Venezuela oil revenues into an offshore account in Qatar, seeking answers from the State Department on the U.S. Government’s administration of Venezuelan oil reserves and related financial and bilateral agreements. On June 8, 2026, Ranking Members Meeks and Ranking Member Jeanne Shaheen demandedanswers from Secretary Rubio on the administration’s lack of progress to push a democratic transition forward in Venezuela. On September 15, 2026, Rep. Joaquin Castro, Ranking Member on the Subcommittee for the Western Hemisphere, led Committee Democrats in offering a motion to subpoenarecords related to the Trump administration’s deal with NABEP. Republicans blocked the effort.

WASHINGTON - As new technologies, business practices, and online marketplaces create new ways for companies to take advantage of consumers, U.S. Representatives Jan Schakowsky (IL-09) and Kathy Castor (FL-14) are introducing legislation to ensure the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has the tools and independence it needs to protect consumers in the modern economy.

The FTC Autonomy Act, introduced by Rep. Schakowsky, and the 21st Century FTC Act, introduced by Rep. Castor, would strengthen the FTC’s ability to respond to unfair and deceptive practices and hold companies accountable when they harm consumers.

“Companies are constantly finding new ways to take advantage of consumers, and the FTC needs the tools to keep up,” said Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky. “I’m glad to be in this fight with Congresswoman Castor to make sure the FTC has the authority and independence it needs to protect consumers. We need an FTC that can keep pace with the modern economy, not one held back by outdated rules and unnecessary barriers.”

“The current economic pain being inflicted on hardworking Americans shouldn’t be exacerbated by fraudsters and corporate wrongdoers. It’s imperative that corporations be held accountable when they take advantage of consumers,” said Congresswoman Kathy Castor. “The FTC is key to accountability, and the 21st Century FTC and FTC Autonomy Acts will strengthen the ability to act and restore civil penalties for first time offenses. I’m committed to restoring the FTC’s autonomy and authority, and I urge Congress to pass this important legislation.”

The FTC is the federal government’s primary consumer protection agency, but outdated procedures and restrictions on its enforcement authority can make it harder for the agency to respond to emerging threats.

The FTC Autonomy Act would allow the FTC’s own attorneys to bring cases seeking civil penalties without first having to enlist the assistance of the Department of Justice. Removing this procedural barrier would allow the agency to pursue enforcement actions more efficiently and hold companies accountable.

The 21st Century FTC Act would give the FTC streamlined rulemaking authority under the Administrative Procedure Act and allow the agency to seek civil penalties for first-time violations of the FTC Act. These changes would help the FTC respond more effectively to emerging consumer harms and deter companies from engaging in unfair or deceptive practices.

Together, these bills would give the FTC the modern tools it needs to protect consumers in a rapidly changing economy. As technology and business practices evolve, consumers should not be left vulnerable because federal consumer protection laws have failed to keep pace. The FTC Autonomy Act and 21st Century FTC Act would strengthen the FTC’s ability to set clear rules, respond to new consumer threats, and hold companies accountable when they cross the line.

###
title: Schakowsky, Castor Introduce Legislation to Modernize FTC and Strengthen Consumer Protections

WASHINGTON, DC — This week, Reps. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Jen Kiggans (R-VA) introduced the bipartisan More Nurses in Rural Schools Act to address the shortage of nurses in the American public school system and ensure students have access to comprehensive, on-site care during the school day. The bill would provide access to student loan repayment for eligible nurses working in schools in health care deserts by opening up the existing National Health Services Corps Loan Repayment Program (NHSLRP) to part- and full-time registered nurses committed to serving schools in health professional shortage areas (HPSA).

While existing student loan repayment programs exist to bring qualified nurses to communities in need, these opportunities typically do not extend to school nurses, who often cannot meet full-time, year-round requirements and do not work in the 2% of public schools designated as School-Based Health Clinic (SBHC) facilities. As a result, registered nurses must choose between working in their communities and taking on the brunt of their student loans, or move to more established clinics. This leaves students without comprehensive services on-site in communities already combatting health care access challenges inflamed by H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut health coverage for 31,000 people across Southwest Washington.

The following report, by the NASN, elaborates on the challenges facing school nurses:

Specifically, the More Nurses in Rural Schools Act would eliminate these barriers for school nurses by:

Allowing the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to permit an individual who agrees to serve for a time period equal to 2 years or longer as a school nurse in an elementary or secondary school located within a health professional shortage area to participate in the NHSC LRP.

For part-time employees, the Secretary is directed to increase the time period of service to the same number of hours as an individual serving in such a position on a full-year, full-time basis.

Directing the Secretary to establish annual certification requirements for the purpose of verifying the number of hours worked by such individuals.

This follows the application process framework in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program, which allows states to track these hours as they see fit.

Defining a “school nurse” as “a registered nurse who is employed by a school or local educational agency or State or State educational agency and is qualified under State law to provide assessment, diagnosis, counseling, educational, therapeutic, and other health services to meet student needs.”

In implementation, this bill would help bring comprehensive health care services to elementary and secondary schools across the country in HPSAs – the majority of which are located in rural and partially rural areas.

“Sending your kid off to their first day of school, it’s like your heart came out of your body and it’s walking around in front of you. You want to know your school has every single option they can to take care of kids when they need it.” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “Letting schools become healthcare deserts isn’t in anyone’s best interest. My bill extends existing loan forgiveness programs to nurses who make the noble choice to serve their community and take care of our children. Especially in rural communities, they’re a priceless lifeline.”

“Every student deserves access to quality health care, regardless of where they live. As a nurse practitioner, I know firsthand how important it is to have a qualified nursing workforce available to care for patients and support their families.” said Rep. Kiggans, “I am proud to join Congresswoman Gluesenkamp Perez in introducing the More Nurses in Rural Schools Act to remove outdated barriers for nurses who want to serve their communities and bring more healthcare professionals to rural and underserved schools.”

“Every student, regardless of where they live, deserves access to a school nurse. The More Nurses in Rural Schools Act is an important step toward addressing persistent workforce shortages and ensuring that students in underserved communities are able to receive the timely, skilled care they need to stay healthy, safe, and ready to learn.” said Lynn Nelson, President of the National Association of School Nurses, “On behalf of the National Association of School Nurses, I thank Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Representative Jen Kiggans for their bipartisan leadership and shared commitment to strengthening school health services and advancing health equity for rural children and families. Their collaboration demonstrates that supporting the health and success of students is a priority that transcends party lines.”

Supporting schools, especially in rural areas, has been a priority for Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. In 2025, she passed a bipartisan bill to reauthorize the Secure Rural Schools (SRS), recovering $8.9 million in 2024 and 2025 payments for local counties and schools, after it lapsed earlier that year. She has also done extensive work funding and supporting trades education in schools. Recently, she attended the ribbon cutting for a new CTE center at Fort Vancouver High school.

In addition, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez voted against H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was signed into law on July 4, 2025. This law eliminated Medicaid eligibility for roughly 17 million Americans–including 31,000 in Southwest Washington. The bill also failed to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits, which helped cover health care coverage costs for lower-income households. Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez co-led the Bipartisan Premium Tax Credit Extension Act to extend these tax credits for one year, giving families more time to make these important health care decisions.

This legislation is supported by the National Association of School Nurses (NASN)

####
title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Bring More Nurses to Public Schools

This week, Congressional Democratic leaders released the following joint statement on Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) Director Bill Pulte’s move to shut down the FHFA Inspector General through severe, unnecessary budget cuts. The statement is signed by: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), and the following Committee Ranking Members: Rep. Maxine Waters (D-CA), House Financial Services Committee; Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee; Sen. Richard Durbin (D-IL), Senate Judiciary Committee; Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC); Sen Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, HSGAC; Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Mary.), House Judiciary Committee; and Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA), House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
“Bill Pulte is shutting down the independent watchdog that is responsible for investigating his misconduct — like his efforts to weaponize private mortgage data in sham investigations against the President’s perceived political enemies. Apparently, it wasn’t enough for President Trump to remove the acting inspector general last November — now Pulte wants to dismantle the office entirely. Pulte’s corrupt crusade to protect himself and President Trump from accountability will likely result in the firing of approximately 40 law enforcement personnel who protect families from mortgage fraud. Bill Pulte should resign, and if he does not, Congress must hold him accountable.”
***
Background
This week, FHFA put out a press release claiming it was “right-sizing” its Inspector General Budget. But the OIG communicated to bipartisan Senate and House committee staff that Pulte’s budget cuts would require the OIG to wind down its operations and cut nearly its entire staff.
In addition to its role in providing oversight on FHFA mismanagement, the FHFA OIG fulfills a unique and critical oversight function of the integrity of the US mortgage market alongside partners at HUD and DOJ, including by stamping out real threats of mortgage fraud. 
###
title: Waters, Warren, Schumer, Jeffries, Durbin, Peters, Blumenthal, Raskin and Garcia Joint Statement on Pulte Shutting Down FHFA Watchdog

Tucson, AZ — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva alongside House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Representative Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM-03), Representative Madeleine Dean (D-PA-04), and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), introduced the America’s College Promise Act of 2026, legislation to make community college and two-year Tribal Colleges and Universities more accessible by waiving tuition and fees for eligible students.

“Students in Southern Arizona and across the country should not have to take on tens of thousands of dollars in debt just to get the education and skills they need to build a better future,” said Rep. Adelita Grijalva. “The America’s College Promise Act is about making sure that opportunity is within reach for every student — whether they are graduating from high school, entering the workforce, changing careers, or returning to the classroom later in life. By expanding access to community and technical colleges, we are investing in students, strengthening our workforce, and giving communities the tools they need to thrive.”

“At Pima Community College, our students are working toward a better future while balancing jobs, family responsibilities, and the cost of their education,” said Dr. Jeffrey Nasse, Chancellor of Pima Community College in Tucson, Arizona. "45 percent of PCC students are low-income. The America’s College Promise Act would help ease that financial burden and invest in the support students need to succeed in college and contribute to our local economies. We appreciate Congresswoman Grijalva’s leadership on legislation that would help more Southern Arizonans gain the skills and credentials to advance their careers and pursue their long-term goals.”

The legislation would create a federal-state partnership to waive tuition and fees for two years of eligible community and technical college programs. It would also provide support for institutions to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, and completion rates, particularly among low-income, first-generation, and underserved students.

“Community colleges play a unique and vital role in providing students access to a quality postsecondary degree. Regrettably, the chronic underfunding of community colleges is jeopardizing their ability to support their students and communities,” said Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott. “The America’s College Promise Act is a major investment in expanding opportunities for students and rebuilding a stronger economy.”

“In New Mexico, we know free community college can unlock the doors to a brighter future,” said Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández. “The America’s College Promise Act builds on New Mexico’s example by making sure students across the country can attend community college without the burden of tuition and fees. Our bill will provide funds for services students need to earn their degrees and reduce the financial burden for low-income students to attend TCUs, HBCUs, and MSIs.”

“As a professor, it was a privilege to witness students claim their education and seize their futures — yet the real fear and burden of immense student loan debt often deters young adults and returning students from expanding their learning,” said Rep. Madeleine Dean. “The America’s College Promise Act provides tuition-free community college courses and expands funding for HBCUs and trade schools, making the path to higher education and career readiness available to more Americans and future generations.”

“Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to get the education and skills they need to land a good-paying job and build a better life, no matter where they come from or how much money their family makes,” said Senator Tammy Baldwin. “That’s why I am proud to work with my colleagues to remove barriers and lower the cost of community college, so more Wisconsinites have the opportunity to compete, succeed, and live a good middle-class life.”

The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 will make the skills and credentials necessary to succeed in the workforce more accessible to all students by creating a new federal-state partnership to provide two years of tuition-free community college.

The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 would:

Create a federal-state partnership to waive tuition and fees for two years of eligible community and technical college programs while promoting reforms designed to accelerate student success;

Establish a sliding federal funding share, beginning at 100 percent in the first year and transitioning to 80 percent beginning in the fifth and subsequent years;

Ensure educational pathways lead to opportunity by requiring programs to offer academic credits transferable to four-year institutions in their state or occupational training leading to recognized credentials;

Maintain and encourage state investment in higher education;

Establish a Student Success Fund to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, completion, and labor market outcomes for underserved students, including students of color and low-income and first-generation college students;

Waive two years of tuition and fees for eligible students attending Tribal Colleges and Universities; and

Create a new grant program for HBCUs and minority-serving institutions to cover a significant portion of tuition and fees during the first two years of attendance for eligible low-income students.

###
title: Rep. Grijalva Introduces America’s College Promise Act to Expand Access to Tuition-Free Community College
